15c9d08c2858.text: 做那些给你带来能量的事情 - 那里才是真正的影响力所在。
15c9d08c2858.original: Do things that give you energy that you are proud of.

b1c579ca9cb0.text: 我们往往低估自己擅长的事情。我们往往认为工作必须是令人不快的。所以如果某件事情很容易和有趣,我们就不会认为它很有价值。所以很多人都会朝着这个方向发展,去做那些不愉快的事情,通过艰苦奋斗来成功。但事实是,你应该去做你觉得愧疚地获得报酬的事情,如果真的有这样的事情存在的话,并且要全力以赴地去做。
b1c579ca9cb0.original: We tend to undervalue the things we're good at. We tend to think work has to be unpleasant. And so if something is easy and fun, we don't tend to think it's valuable. So I think lots of people gravitate in this direction of like, let's go do unpleasant things and grind our way through the career because that's the way to make it. But the reality is you should go do the thing that you feel guilty to get paid for, if there's a thing like that, and do the hell out of it, right? Do it as hard as you can do it.

25ac832f5fca.text: 当你发现一些让你感到有能量的事情时,就全身心地投入其中吧。通过这个过程不断地调整和学习。
25ac832f5fca.original: When you find something that gives you energy, just jump in with both feet. And try to go through that process, and pivot and learn, and pivot and learn and pivot.

91f674e81070.text: 你擅长的事情往往也是你喜欢的事情。你喜欢的事情往往也是你擅长的事情。
91f674e81070.original: You tend to be good at the things you enjoy. You tend to enjoy the things you're good at.

946c6d9a3891.text: 要获得非凡的回报,你必须做一些非凡的事情。你必须承担更大的风险,有更有趣的机会,才能在你的职业生涯中取得这种非凡的成果。
946c6d9a3891.original: I think the way you get extraordinary returns is you do extraordinary things, right? You have to take bigger risks, and have more interesting shots to have this kind of extraordinary result in your career.

11fd8032c0f7.text: 归根结底,你能在职业生涯中取得进步,是因为你产生了很大的影响力。而你能产生很大的影响力,是因为你选择了自己擅长的事情,并且以高度的投入去做,从而产生了影响。
11fd8032c0f7.original: I think there's, at the end of the day, the reason you get ahead in your career is you had a lot of impact. And the reason you had a lot of impact was because you picked something that you're good at that you did with a lot of intensity that wound up having impact, right?

5c0ed7492841.text: 工作并不一定必须很难。它往往是难的,但并非必须如此。最好的情况是,它并不难。你所产生的最大影响力,往往就是在你完全沉浸其中,做着你喜欢做的事情,而且你都不敢相信自己居然能为此获得报酬的时候。
5c0ed7492841.original: Work doesn't necessarily have to be hard. It often is, but it doesn't have to be. And the best case is that it isn't. The most impact you'll ever have is where you're in that mode where you're just in the flow and doing your thing and you're happy to do it and you can't quite believe they pay you and you don't understand how you're getting away with this, but it's super cool anyways, right?

bd142ac11f89.text: 如果你周围的人给你带来能量,并且你追随你真正感兴趣的事情,那么你就一定会在这个时代取得成功。
bd142ac11f89.original: If you surround yourself with people that give you energy and if you follow the things you're actually curious about, that you're going to be successful in this era.

456d271ed6f3.text: 如果你找到了自己的超级技能,并按照它们工作,你就会做出你生涯中最出色的工作。你会喜欢它,你会擅长它,你也不会感到沮丧。
456d271ed6f3.original: If you identify your superpowers and work in accordance with them, you will do the best work of your life. You will love it, and you will be great at it, and you won't have that frustration.

be498496492e.text: 我查看了我日程表上的会议,把它们用红色、黄色和绿色标记出来。回顾最近几周,几乎全部都是红色和黄色。这说明从能量角度来看,我并不太喜欢这些。
be498496492e.original: I went through my calendar and I changed the colors of all of the meetings on my calendar to red, yellow, and green after I had the meeting. And when I looked back at the last few weeks, it was almost all red and yellow. And I was like, okay, this is really from an energy standpoint, I don't think I love this.

1628f4ca119e.text: 要非常擅长弄清楚,你最喜欢产品经理工作的哪些方面,然后尽可能在下一个角色中优化这些你喜欢的方面。
1628f4ca119e.original: Get really good at figuring out what are the things that you love most about being a product person, and how can you optimize your next role for those things that you love?

9d4be6ac15ad.text: 当你对某件事充满热情时,你会做出更好、更聪明的工作,并且生产力会成倍提高。
9d4be6ac15ad.original: When you're passionate about something, you do better work, you do smarter work and you're, in order of magnitude, more productive.

b75dfd211201.text: 如果你真的享受自己的工作和所做的事情,它就不会感觉像是一种牺牲。一旦你开始谈论工作生活平衡,你可能就已经偏离了正轨。
b75dfd211201.original: If you truly enjoy your work and what you're doing, it won't feel like a sacrifice. The moment you start having those conversations about work-life balance, you are probably not on that track.

cbf379863807.text: 产品工作分为三个层级:影响力层级、执行层级和形象层级。我最喜欢的是影响力层级。
cbf379863807.original: Product work happens at three levels. There's the impact level, there's the execution level, and there's the optics level. My happy place is the impact level.

8ca2135ae534.text: 当我们的行为大部分时间都与我们的超级技能和内心本质不一致时,我们的工作就会变得令人沮丧。
8ca2135ae534.original: Our jobs get frustrating when we behave, most of the time, in misalignment with our superpowers and who we truly are at our core.

9b9b6e513843.text: 你需要为自己的职业生涯负责,并确定你想要去的方向。这是由你自己决定的。你可以让别人来决定,并试图改变自己以适应别人。但我告诉你,如果你花时间去了解自己是谁,并找到一份与你相符的工作,你会做得更好。
9b9b6e513843.original: You need to take responsibility for your career and where you want to go. And this is on you. And so the reality is you can let somebody else do it and you can try to morph yourself to fit other people. But I will tell you, you will be way better off if you spend the time to figure out who you are and find a job that matches who you are.

6502111f2741.text: 当你对什么都无所事事时,你就知道自己是谁了,你才能真正弄清楚这个问题。
6502111f2741.original: The moment you are comfortable doing nothing, you know who you are again, and you can actually figure this out.

ded22e6c5c78.text: 你是在关注你能控制的事情,还是关注你无法控制的事情?其次是你与变化的关系如何?第三是你如何看待自己。
ded22e6c5c78.original: Whether you are focusing on things you control or whether you're focusing on things that are beyond your control. Second, what's your relationship with change? And third is how you see yourself.

d76966ac0520.text: 如果你认为自己在数据方面得分4分,找出谁得5分。在你的组织内部,与行业内最好的人进行基准对比。你会发现你的得分会下降,这样你就会看到你需要改进和提高的地方。
d76966ac0520.original: If you think you are four on data, figure out who. And you may be four on data out of five in data. Within your organization, start benchmarking yourself with the best in the industry. You'll automatically see that your scale drops and as your scale drops, you start seeing what you need to improve and do.
d76966ac0520.originalContext: The speaker is referring to a 1-5 rating scale for evaluating product management skills across different competency areas like data, communication, and strategy.

ad97bc3dcc53.text: 弄清楚你告诉自己的故事,因为这些故事在基本层面上定义了你,这种定义很难通过框架和结构来纠正。
ad97bc3dcc53.original: Figure out what is the story that you are telling yourself because those stories are defining you at a basic level, which is then very hard to correct through frameworks and structures.

d1baf26fbfa2.text: 你不可能在每个领域都有所提高。这会让你感到不知所措。你需要选择一个最有影响力的领域来改进,然后再转向下一个领域。
d1baf26fbfa2.original: You can't improve on every single area. That's what overwhelms you. You need to pick which is the area which is the maximum leverage for you and improve on that particular aspect and then move on to the next area.

70eee1f84613.text: 在职业生涯早期就确定你是否真的想成为C级高管,因为如果你有抱负并取得成功,进入产品管理领域,人们几乎会期望你会成为那样,而你从未真正质疑或挑战过自己。
70eee1f84613.original: Determine very early in your career if you truly want to be a C-level someday because it's almost like if you're ambitious and successful, you enter product management, it's almost an expectation that you would become that and you'd never really challenge or question yourself.

45bbea858e9e.text: 不要压抑自己的特质和优势,而是要不断拓展。每遇到一个问题,就增加你可以做的事情、拥有的工具和表达自己的方式。
45bbea858e9e.original: Don't dampen who you are and your strengths, just continue expanding. Whenever you run into a problem, just add more to the things that you can do, the tools that you have, the way you can express yourself.

1c6165bd8b48.text: 我意识到一个潜在的局限性,它限制了我在这份工作中的成功,那就是我在试图使这份工作符合我认为自己喜欢做的事情。
1c6165bd8b48.original: I had realized this subconscious limiter that was limiting my success in the job, which is, I was trying to conform the job to the things I thought I liked to do.

08cbd77fe2d5.text: 我觉得很多人在微观层面上很有针对性,他们考虑下一份工作、下一个头衔,薪资和股权有多少...但在宏观层面上却很随意。他们没有考虑大局,没有思考作为一个个体自己真正关心的是什么。
08cbd77fe2d5.original: I think a lot of people are very intentional in the micro. They think about their next job, their next title, how much salary and equity there is... but they're very unintentional about the macro. What's the big picture? What do I care about as an individual?

2933ccbd45e3.text: 如果你教孩子们要好奇、独立和自信,教会他们如何思考,我不知道未来会是什么样子,但我认为这些将是在任何未来配置下都很重要的技能。
2933ccbd45e3.original: If you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think, I don't know what the future holds, but I think that those are going to be skills that are going to be important in any configuration of the future.

682377ced124.text: 每读一本书,你的大脑就会变得更贫瘠,以适应下一本书的阅读。这就是书籍的目的。
682377ced124.original: Every book you read makes your brain poorer to read the next book. That's the purpose of books.

209322a86a76.text: 你的听众一直在想'有一天我会成为X。我会成为那个副总裁。我会赚更多钱。我会创造一些东西。我会创办一家公司。'但他们没有考虑接下来会发生什么,当他们成功时,他们的北极星,他们整个职业和自我定位的方式,都围绕着达到那个目标。
209322a86a76.original: Your listeners are spending time focused on like, 'Well, one day I will be X. I will be that vice president. I will have more money. I will have built something. I will have started a company.' But they don't think about what happens next, and when it happens, when they succeed, their North Star, their entire way of wiring their career, themselves, it has been around getting to that place.

b68b25d89ec2.text: 某个时候你要明白, 你的职业生涯责任在于自己, 而不是你的工作环境。
b68b25d89ec2.original: At some point, understand that you are responsible for your career, not your workplace.

e348355364e4.text: 我曾经与一些最优秀的产品经理合作过, 但他们在管理自己的职业生涯上却很糟糕。他们只是从一份工作到另一份工作地漂泊。但如果让你为自己的职业生涯写一份产品规格说明, 成功是什么样子的? 你要如何实现那个目标?
e348355364e4.original: Some of the best PMs I have ever worked with are terrible PMs for their career. They just drift from job to job. But if I said you had to write a spec for your career, what does success look like? How are you going to get there?

885570fd12f9.text: 一旦你在职业发展上停滞不前, 你就会开始寻找另一份工作。
885570fd12f9.original: The moment you stop making progress in your career is the moment you start looking for another job.

0b65ac0c69a9.text: 你的经理应该做些什么对你来说就和一杯星巴克咖啡的价格一样重要。这个循环的关键在于它掌握在你自己手中。
0b65ac0c69a9.context: 「这个循环」指的是Evans的魔环框架:一个推进管理层关系的五步过程,以此来推进职业发展。
0b65ac0c69a9.original: What your manager should do and $4 will get you a cup of coffee at Starbucks. The point of this loop is it's in your control.
0b65ac0c69a9.originalContext: "The loop" refers to Evans' Magic Loop framework: a 5-step process for building manager partnerships to advance your career.

419dbc5abb73.text: 要清楚地知道你想要从职业生涯中得到什么, 明确提出要求, 然后让你的老板或任何能够支持或推动你的人更容易帮助你从现在到达那里。
419dbc5abb73.original: Know what you want out of your career, be clear and ask for it, and then make it easy for your boss or whoever can support or champion you to get you from here to there.

70fcfa513a24.text: 在你的职业生涯中, 它就像在建立一个产品一样。你有理论和假设, 你想办法去验证它们, 然后你要么成功要么失败。
70fcfa513a24.original: In your career, it's just a lot like building a product. You have theories and hypotheses, you find ways to experiment with them, and then you were successful or you failed.

ffab00630ab8.text: 我的职业目标实际上是拥有选择的自由, 这样我就可以选择自己想要做的事。我可以选择什么最适合我目前的生活状态、我的技能和我的性格,使我感到快乐。
ffab00630ab8.original: My goal professional is actually to have options so I can choose what I want to do. So I can choose what fits my life right now that I can choose what fits my skills and that fits my personality and that makes me happy.

adb51ba8bc21.text: 我的职业目标实际上是拥有选择的自由,这样我就可以选择自己想要做的事。你要开始思考下一年你可以做些什么来增加你的选择空间?
adb51ba8bc21.original: My goal professional is actually to have options so I can choose what I want to do. You start thinking about what can I do next year that will increase my option pool?

903869e7ac1e.text: 员工更多是在选择公司, 而不是公司在选择员工。
903869e7ac1e.original: Employees hire companies more than companies hire employees.

931fafddfa17.text: 全职工作并不是发挥你技能的最佳方式。它只是众多选择方式之一, 每个人都应该评估并利用它, 但是太多人盲目地把它作为默认选择。
931fafddfa17.original: Full-time jobs are not the best way to monetize the skill that you have. It's one of the packages that everybody should evaluate and take advantage of, but too many people blindly default to that package.

f4fdacbfe481.text: 全职工作并不是发挥你技能的最佳方式。太多人盲目地把它作为默认选择, 而没有探索其他选择。
f4fdacbfe481.original: Full-time jobs are not the best way to monetize the skill that you have. Too many people blindly default to that package and don't explore other options.

3869e665607d.text: 不要把薪酬作为优化的目标,特别是在职业生涯的早期。你会发现绝大部分薪酬是在职业生涯的最后五年获得的。
3869e665607d.original: Do not optimize for compensation, especially early in your career. You will find that the compensation is so much backloaded that you would make 90% of your compensation in the last five years of your career.

ed1e771db48e.text: 我认为我们没有意识到我们面前有多少机会。作为一个26岁的人,我肯定认为我的职业生涯已经结束了。回过头来看,这真是太有趣了。
ed1e771db48e.original: I think we don't recognize how much opportunity we have in front of us. And as a 26-year-old, I definitely thought my career was over. I was like, 'I blew it.' And looking back, it's funny.

b925fe17912a.text: 把重点放在声誉和学习而不是收益上,这对我来说效果非常好。
b925fe17912a.original: Focus on reputation and learning over earnings has served me super well.

5434f9b1a861.text: 你希望自己处于一个从不急于寻找下一个机会,而是能够非常有选择性地对待眼前的机会的位置。这需要时间、网络建设和多年的关系建设。
5434f9b1a861.original: You want to be in a position where you're never running out the door looking for what's next, but rather being able to be super selective about the things that you have in front of you. And that comes with time and network building and relationship building over years.

30d24a8de62b.text: 要长远考虑。一旦你找到这样的人,就坚持跟着他们走。只要他们愿意和你在一起,就跟着他们走。因为在你的职业生涯中,你会和同一批人一起做很多事情。与A类人建立的信任和经验将会让你走很远。
30d24a8de62b.original: Play the long game. Once you find someone like that, stick to them. As long as they want to hang out with you, but just stick to them. Because you will go on to do multiple things over your career with the same set of people. And the shared trust and experience that you build with A plus people is just going to go a long way.

42739d4e9c77.text: 永远不要考虑下一份工作,而要考虑下一个下一份工作。也许不是考虑你老板的工作,而是考虑你老板老板的工作,以及你需要做些什么来达到那个目标。
42739d4e9c77.original: Always think about not the next job, but the one after it. Maybe think about not your boss's job but your boss's boss's job and what do I need to think about to get there.

c3399c53c150.text: 生活就是苦难。所以找出一些值得苦难付出的事情。不管你选哪条路,你都会遇到苦难。我认为人们没有意识到,根本没有一条轻松的道路可以走。
c3399c53c150.original: Life is suffering. So figure out something worth suffering for. You're going to suffer either way. And that's another thing I think people don't realize, is there isn't really a path that is easy that I've ever found.

7c09742e2730.text: 拥有更多元化的职业经历,你就会成为一个更出色的创造者。这通常会带来满足感。但是,仅仅因为认为这样做会增加下一份工作的机会而去这样做,这让我感到害怕,因为这感觉更像是为了实现某种未来的梦想,而不是为了专注于创造。
7c09742e2730.context: 「偏向构建」指的是专注于获得多元化的经验来提升产品构建能力,而不是为简历而工作。
7c09742e2730.original: The more diverse career you have, the better builder you are. And that usually comes up being satisfied. But the idea of just doing that because you think it's going to make your chances better for the next job maybe scares me and it feels very much in service of some future dream that is not build oriented.
7c09742e2730.originalContext: "Build oriented" refers to focusing on gaining diverse experiences that help you become better at building products, rather than chasing jobs for resume value.

18d8af163960.text: 晋升是我们公司用来看待你前进情况的系统,它很清楚地体现在级别、你在做什么,以及决策的过程。但实际上,如果你在考虑职业生涯,你应该考虑长期的发展轨迹。
18d8af163960.original: Promotion is our system at this company to see you moving forward. And it's pretty clear in terms of levels and what you're doing and what the process is and who makes the decision. But in reality, if you're thinking career, you're thinking about the sort of long term arc.

9f759d85d38a.text: 如果你把创办一家公司视为职业生涯的一个步骤,那么它是不成功的。因为如果成功了,它将是你的整个职业生涯。它很可能会持续10年。如果不成功,那么这不是人们通常向往的事情。
9f759d85d38a.original: A non-successful startup is if you think of starting a company as a career step. Well, it is not. Because if it's successful, it'll be your entire career. It'll be 10 years most likely. And if it's not successful, then it's not something that people generally aspire to start.

ee4833b2707b.text: 我的建议是去找一份能让你在产品管理领域成为最快学习者的工作。这才是真正对你有帮助的。不管是什么课程、学位,都是无法替代的。
ee4833b2707b.original: My advice to people is go get a job which will make you the fastest learner in the field of product management. That is what will help you a lot. No course, no degree, none of those things will help.

f5fdb20466ac.text: 你今天知道的远不及明天你能学到的东西。如果你在一家增长如此迅猛的公司工作,你今天的知识就会变得毫无价值。
f5fdb20466ac.context: 格雷姆在讨论快速增长公司中,由于持续变革,技能会很快过时,她用手势表示了一条陡峭上升的增长曲线。
f5fdb20466ac.original: What you know today is way less valuable than what you can learn by tomorrow. If you're inside of a company where the growth curve is like this, what you know today is irrelevant.
f5fdb20466ac.originalContext: Graham was discussing how in rapidly growing companies, skills become obsolete quickly due to constant change, using a visual gesture to indicate a steep upward growth curve.

b08fada95e75.text: 你应该时刻思考,一年后、两年后、五年后,你希望自己已经学会什么。
b08fada95e75.original: Always be working back from, in one year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years, five years?

955be4ed743d.text: 在LinkedIn工作时,我明确告诉经理我的目标是学习如何成为一名更好的创始人。当时有很多事情我做得不太好,比如我不太懂增长,对定价也只是勉强达标,对订阅业务的构建和定价更是一知半解。
955be4ed743d.original: My role at LinkedIn was really explicit. I even told my manager this when I first came in, 'I'm here to learn to be a better founder.' So there were a lot of things when I started connected, which I didn't know how to do very well, I didn't understand growth. I was fair to middling at pricing. I really didn't understand how to build a subscriptions business and how to price it.

ba0f3cc1e798.text: 如果我只是被动地接受晋升或追求最大头衔,是不可能获得这些宝贵的学习机会的。相反,我专注于学习和成长。
ba0f3cc1e798.original: I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title. Instead, I was focused on those learnings and those experiences.

f901c66ccd57.text: 我从学习的角度来看待这一切。在这里我能学到什么,如何成长和发展?也许有人可以在一家公司工作20年,只要每天都能受到很大挑战,不断学习新事物,并从工作中获得充实的愉悦感。
f901c66ccd57.original: I really look at it from the lens of learning. What can I learn here, and how am I growing and developing? So there might be an argument for you to stay at a job for two decades. If it turns out that every single day you're being really challenged, you're learning new things, you're deriving a lot of meaningful enjoyment out of your work.

1539bb26e4ee.text: 你应该追随那些优秀的人,向他们学习。无论是最优秀的产品思考者、工程师还是销售人员,跟随他们都能学到技能精髓。
1539bb26e4ee.original: You follow people. You learn the most from people... You want to follow somebody who's either the best product thinker or the best engineer or the best salesperson. And so that you will learn the skill of how to be the best at that.

6ba2235e963e.text: 技能是无法被剥夺的。一家公司可能会倒闭,但如果你学会了某项技能,它永远属于你。
6ba2235e963e.original: Skills can't be taken away. A company can fail, but if you learn a skill, you will always have that skill.

b88fba0dc56b.text: 尝试新的事物,坚持六个月。如果不是你的菜,没关系,你已经获得了大量新技能,日后一定会派上用场。继续前进吧。
b88fba0dc56b.original: Jump into new things, give it six months. If it's not the thing, no problem. You just built a ton of new skills that's going to come in handy, I promise you that. Keep going.

d35a9b199750.text: 一个不断学习的人,总会超越那些今天是专家但后来停止学习的人。你可以在最擅长的工作中产生最大影响,但如果你不再学习,就会止步不前。相反,如果你一直在学习,你的影响力才会持续增长。
d35a9b199750.original: Someone who's always learning is always going to exceed someone who's the expert today. You can have the most impact, the job you know the best, but then you stop learning. And if you're learning all the time, you're not necessarily having impact.

df697936eef1.text: 要是你知道自己不会失败,你会做什么?这是最大的问题。如果不需要赚钱,你会做什么?你认为是玩乐的事对别人来说就是工作。
df697936eef1.original: What would you do if you knew you wouldn't fail? That's the biggest question. If you didn't have to make money, what would you do? What's play for you that is work for other people?

013fe7ae92b1.text: 有时我确实想鼓励年轻人把重点放在最重要的事情上,因为我发现自己经常在导师模式下,看到一个非常出色的年轻人过度关注工作的每一个细小维度和方面。
013fe7ae92b1.original: Sometimes I do want to encourage young people to focus on what's important because I find myself constantly in mentoring mode when I see an incredible young talent who is over-focusing on every minute dimension and aspect of considering a job.

e6398715f414.text: 我意识到我的职业道路很大程度上取决于一件事。就是,什么最受需求?什么最有挑战性?...当我来到这里,我个人面临的一个重大挑战就是,我到底在乎什么?什么对我最重要?
e6398715f414.original: I realized my career path was very much dictated by one thing. It was like, what's most in demand? What's most challenging?... And then when I came here, there was a really big challenging for me personally around what do I care about? What matters most to me?

08201ce43d70.text: 如果你对你想要构建的东西并不真正兴奋,你对它没有信念,你要让它产生重大影响会非常困难。
08201ce43d70.original: If you're not genuinely excited about what you want to build, you don't have conviction about it, it's going to be very hard for you to make a big impact.

3f7dcd900812.text: 我更关注过一种有趣的生活,而不是所谓的好生活或舒适的生活。这就是成长的来源,这就是我会最深刻记住的故事。
3f7dcd900812.original: I care more about living a really interesting life than let's say a good or comfortable life. I think that's where the growth comes from. That's where the stories come from. That's to me the things that I'll remember the most.

317999670494.text: 创办公司的唯一理由是因为你有一种不理智的渴望去做,因为它不值得赚钱。
317999670494.original: The only reason to start a company is because you have an irrational desire to do so, because it's not worth the money.

977452014fdf.text: 我确实发现很多年轻人在决定工作时都会考虑方程式的每一个方面。也许那就是他们想要的方式,但有时我确实想鼓励年轻人把重点放在最重要的事情上,因为...也许最重要的是你的热情在哪里?你是否认同这个使命?你是否相信并相信这个团队?
977452014fdf.original: I do find many of the young people today think about every single aspect of an equation when they decide on jobs. At some point, maybe that's the way they want to do it, but sometimes I do want to encourage young people to focus on what's important because... maybe the most important thing is where's your passion? Do you align with the mission? Do you believe and have faith in this team?

5836eaf4a077.text: 有一天早上醒来发现自己已经步入中年,却因为有某种生活方式或周围人的某些期望而陷入困境,不得不去工作,但同时你又看着镜子里的自己并不快乐,这真是一个可怕的陷阱。我认为我们在规划职业道路和寻找最适合自己的事物时,都应该尽量避免陷入这种境地,那通常是事业成功与工作中的意义和价值观的平衡。
5836eaf4a077.original: It's a terrible outcome to wake up one day and be late career and feel trapped because you have a certain lifestyle or a certain expectations of the people around you that you have to go work this job, but then you look at yourself in the mirror and you're not happy going in there. I think that's a terrible trap that we should all try to avoid as we navigate our career paths and find the thing that's most optimal for us. Which is usually a mix of career success, but also meaningfulness and alignment in the work that we're doing with our values.

8c1df37c69f0.text: 这是一项技能,技能是知识与练习的乘积,受到你的环境、养成的习惯和你的动力因素的影响。
8c1df37c69f0.original: This is a skill and skill is knowledge times practice mediated by your environment, the habits you form and the motivation that you have.

5826ee4346ee.text: 在你感觉它已深入骨髓之前,不要停止亲自动手做技术工作。你会感觉到你掌握了这个技能,即使暂时放下它,很快也能重新拾起。
5826ee4346ee.original: Don't stop being a hands-on technical until you feel like it's in your bones. You feel like you've got mastery that you could... if I was to pick it up, it would be rusty, but I would get there pretty quickly.

eda3e8c730e0.text: 有时我会告诉产品经理,'你不只是给我看刚刚做的那个,什么时候你要做下一个策略?我能加入你吗?我只想坐下来看你写大纲,理解你的思考过程。'
eda3e8c730e0.original: Sometimes I tell the PM like, 'Hey, don't just show me the one you just did. When are you going to do your next strategy? Can I join you then? I just want to sit and watch you write down the outline and just understand your thought process.'

1823aa1d8953.text: 我通常会给自己三个月、六个月的时间。每周都会做一些与学习策略有关的事情。持续六个月,你就能克服障碍,真正培养出这项技能。
1823aa1d8953.original: My approach is typically I'll say, 'I'm giving myself three months, six months.' Every week, I'm going to do something related to learning strategy. And I do that for six months. You do it enough that you get over the hump and then actually develop the skill.

3f65ca1b41a8.text: 通过不断迭代,而不仅仅是看最终的产品,你也能获得很多学习。这就是在有优秀的产品管理团队的公司里的好处。
3f65ca1b41a8.original: A lot of learning happens through the iterations and not by seeing the final product. That's the benefit you also get at a company that has great product management.

77a002efcd4e.text: 对于情商方面的学习,这对我来说是最令人沮丧的。但对于智商方面,有时三个月,有时六个月我就能看到明显的进步。而情商方面的东西,我一直在努力学习多年。
77a002efcd4e.original: For the EQ stuff, it was the most frustrating learning for me. For the IQ stuff, within six months, sometimes three months, I can see clear progress. But then with the EQ stuff, it's things I've been working on for years.

9e69cb22c7c4.text: 如果你一直待在舒适区内,你永远无法做出与当前不同或更好的事情。
9e69cb22c7c4.original: If you always stay in your comfort zone, you'll never do anything different or better than what you're currently doing.

f6d6c0a985a8.text: 那些让你感到受挑战或不舒服的时刻,或者你发现自己说'哦,天哪。我不应该在这里'或'我资格不足',这些正是你应该去寻找的时刻。这些时刻会让你得到新的基础。
f6d6c0a985a8.original: Moments that stretch you or moments that you feel uncomfortable in or you find yourself saying, 'Oh shit. I shouldn't be here,' or, 'I'm under qualified to be here,' those are the moments you should be seeking out. Those are the moments that stretch you and give you a new foundation.

a3e7b7bdbfd0.text: 在一家初创公司工作14年的方式就是让你一天多次遭受重击,这要么会杀死你,要么会让你变得更强大。
a3e7b7bdbfd0.original: Working in a startup for 14 years has a certain way of kicking you in the head many times a day that either kills you or makes you far stronger.

7a018da72d27.text: 在过去的六个月、一年或两年内,你有多少个'哦,天哪'的时刻?如果你问自己这个问题,答案是'我已经很久没有在某些方面受到有意义的挑战或感到资格不足了',那么值得去深挖一下。
7a018da72d27.original: How many oh shit moments have you had in the last six months, year, two years, and what are they? I think if you ask yourself that question and the answer is, 'It's been a really long time since I've been stretched in some meaningful way or I've felt like I'm under qualified to be there,' then it may be worth digging into.

eb51b03afdb1.text: 我一直努力将自己置于会带来大量成长和学习的位置。而成长和学习可能会非常痛苦。
eb51b03afdb1.original: I always try to prioritize putting myself in positions that are going to cause a lot of growth and learning. And growth and learning can be very painful.

e3caab89cd79.text: 身处不舒适的处境,感觉自己不太了解如何去做,没有做好准备,这种状态往往与职业生涯中最快速和最激烈的成长时期重合。
e3caab89cd79.original: Being in an uncomfortable situation, being in a position where you feel like, hey, do I really know how to do this, I'm not prepared for it, kind of coincides with the fastest and most intense periods of growth in one's career.

b809228b7463.text: 作为一个产品人,你天生就生活在一个没有人知道正确答案的世界里,因为如果有人知道,他们早就造出来了...拥有这种谦逊是早期职业领导者的最大区别之一。
b809228b7463.original: Being a product person means that by definition you're living in a world where no one knows the right answer yet because if somebody did, they would've already built it... having that humility is one of the biggest differentiators in early career leaders.

afaaf3be5888.text: 当你搭上火箭飞船时,不要问你的座位在哪里。那为我开启了大门,我就这样在这里干了19年。
afaaf3be5888.context: Naomi正在反思她在2005年作为Facebook第29号员工加入这家初创公司的决定,当时她就接受了任何可用的岗位。
afaaf3be5888.original: When you are on getting a rocket ship, don't ask what seat. That was my foot in the door and here we are 19 years later.
afaaf3be5888.originalContext: Naomi is reflecting on her decision to join Facebook as employee #29 in 2005, where "that" refers to accepting any available role at the promising startup.

e862d83c332a.text: 你的职业发展和能力提升,也就是说你获得更高级职位的速度,在很大程度上取决于你公司的发展势头。
e862d83c332a.original: Your career and your ability to transcend, which is really moving faster than other people to get bigger jobs, is fairly dependent on the momentum of your company.

7898a84db918.text: 最好的做法是找到那些增长迅猛的公司,因为它能以更快的速度让你的学习事半功倍。
7898a84db918.original: The best thing you can do is find companies that are growing fast because it compounds your learning at a much faster interval.

3cc8ba4ad91a.text: 我宁愿成为行业领军者的第二或第三把手,也不愿成为二线公司的老大。
3cc8ba4ad91a.original: I would much rather be the number two or number three person at the leader in a space, than the top person at a tier two company.

f4a308d12b62.text: 我做过的每一个职业决定,包括大学毕业后的第一个工作,都是想找到我所认识的最聪明的人,和他们一起工作和学习。
f4a308d12b62.original: Every single career decisions I ever made, including my first one out of college, was just figuring out who are the smartest people I know that I want to hang out with and learn from, and can I work with them?

4a34fe9c4df4.text: 我在Oracle工作了5年,团队从5人增长到7人;在Atlassian工作了4年,团队从15人扩张到100人。
4a34fe9c4df4.original: I was a leader at Oracle for five years, and my team grew from five to seven over five years. And I was a leader at Atlassian for four years, and my team grew from 15 to 100.

9328249c9df0.text: 有大量获得大笔资金的高增长公司,所以他们在2022年或2023年不会资金枯竭...我担心的是,从职业发展角度来看,很多科技从业者正在加入这些公司,但期望能从股权中获利。
9328249c9df0.original: There's these large number of growth companies who have raised substantive dollars. So they're not going to run out of capital in 2022 or 2023... My fear is, from a career point of view, so many tech professionals are in these organizations or joining these organizations with the expectation that they'll make money on their equity.

f034b76d7f64.text: 每次我接受一份工作,发现我和工作伙伴的价值观或工作方式不同时,我内心就有预感。你会告诉自己,至少在我的情况下,我会给自己编造一个故事,说这种我怀疑可能存在的情况实际上并不存在。
f034b76d7f64.original: Every single time I've taken a job where it turned out that I was working with people who had a different set of values or working styles than I had, I knew. You tell yourself that, at least in my case, I tell myself a story about why the thing I suspect might be the case isn't the case.

7272ee958788.text: 让孩子吃蔬菜就是这样一个概念,小朋友通常要尝试10到12次,甚至不喜欢,也要坚持,因为这需要时间让他们培养喜好。研究人员说,即使孩子起初不喜欢,也要让他们接触10到12次蔬菜,这样才能让他们最终喜欢上。
7272ee958788.original: Eating your vegetables is really this idea around how little kids don't really develop an appreciation for vegetables until they're 10 or 12 exposures in. So the researchers say, 'Expose kids to vegetables 10 or 12 times, even if they don't like it, because that's what it takes to get someone to like something.'

8dfcbfd2f6dc.text: 在做一件事之前,你需要多次练习,因为第一次你肯定做得不好。比如我早期职业生涯中,我在社交方面很拘谨,不太擅长。
8dfcbfd2f6dc.original: You have to do things a number of times before you really develop an affinity for it. Because the first time you do it, you're just not going to be good. So my mini example of that was early on in my career, I was really awkward and not very good at networking.

e84dc3e45c66.text: 我给自己制定了一个规则,每周必须参加一次外部活动,在那里发放10张名片。规则是,我必须全部发完名片,通过向陌生人自我介绍,并触碰场地的后墙,然后我才能离开。
e84dc3e45c66.original: I gave myself this rule where I had to go out once a week for a couple of months, go to an external event, and I would count out 10 business cards. And the rule was, I had to hand out all 10 of those business cards by introducing myself to people that were new, and touch the back wall of the venue of that event and then I could leave.

468742de0c33.text: 当你面试一家公司时,你实际上投资的是一种更稀缺的资源 —— 时间。时间是有限的,我们每个人都在一个有限的时钟上。但金钱总是可以获得的。
468742de0c33.original: When you're interviewing at a company, you are actually investing an even more scarce resource. You're investing your time. There is no way to get more time. We're all on a finite clock. You can always get more money.

8814c8a39b6a.text: 每次我降低标准,只满足了3个因素中的2个,或者认为有1个很出色,实际上并非如此,结果都不太理想。
8814c8a39b6a.context: 亚当提到了他的产品市场适配(PMF)评估框架,其包括三个关键因素:团队、使命和财务。
8814c8a39b6a.original: Any time where I've shortcutted my criteria, where I've settled for two out of three, or thought one was great, when really it wasn't, has not ended well for me, for the company.
8814c8a39b6a.originalContext: Adam's "criteria" refers to his PMF framework for evaluating companies: People, Mission, and Financials as three essential factors when choosing where to work.

b6d6dfbcca87.text: 这些创始人和高管在思考时,他们更多地谈到了一种模糊的氛围感,包括你是否感到安全,能否与他们深入探讨,以及他们是否真的了解你,并能帮助你把事情串起来。这远比他们的经历更重要。
b6d6dfbcca87.context: 艾达·陈·雷基采访了80多位创始人和高管,旨在研究选择合适教练的成功因素。
b6d6dfbcca87.original: These founders and executives when they thought about it, they actually said so much more about, it was actually this amorphous sense of vibe with the person, how safe you felt with them, how deeply you would explore with them, and how well they got you, and remembered the pieces of the conversation and help you put it together. Way more than potentially some experiences that they'd had.
b6d6dfbcca87.originalContext: Ada Chen Rekhi interviewed over 80 founders and executives about their coaching experiences to research what makes coach selection successful.

e3839ed08464.text: 你曾经发布过最差劲的产品是什么？我认为如果一个产品经理没有发布过真正糟糕的产品,那他就还没有足够的实战经验。
e3839ed08464.original: What's the worst product you've ever shipped? I don't think you're a good PM if you haven't shipped something that's really shitty, you just haven't had enough reps.

3e3bbd2c1938.text: 当你一次又一次地采取行动,不管是成功还是失败,你终将达到目标。在那些时刻,我并没有想到最终会这样。
3e3bbd2c1938.original: When you keep taking action, action, action, win or lose, win or lose, you'll get where you need to go. And that turned out to be true. But in those moments, I was not thinking that was going to turn out to be true.

7971b92805b3.text: 我很乐意尝试一些我很可能会失败的事情。
7971b92805b3.original: I'm kind of okay with being pretty sure I'm going to fail at something, and still attempting it.

edc216305fb6.text: 如果我能公开地在亚马逊这样一个富有且著名的发明家面前失败,并最终在亚马逊取得成功晋升,那么你也一定能从任何困境中走出来。
edc216305fb6.context: 埃文斯在亚马逊一次高调的产品发布失败后,却被晋升为副总裁。
edc216305fb6.original: If I can get away with publicly failing one of the richest and most famous inventors on earth, and then get promoted and finish my career at Amazon very successfully, you can dig out of any hole.
edc216305fb6.originalContext: Evans failed during a high-profile Amazon product launch that angered CEO Jeff Bezos, but was later promoted to VP.

2fc69fa1cbc5.text: 在职业生涯中,我们总是被鼓励只谈论自己的成功经历,因为这才是让人印象深刻的。但在那些成功之间,也有很多被掩盖的失败时刻。
2fc69fa1cbc5.original: We are very encouraged in our lives, especially professionally, to talk about our A side all the time because that's what impresses people... But between all of those highlights, there were so many B moments that get shoved under the rug.

464a98727b7a.text: 你痛苦的生活经验都是未来智慧的原料。
464a98727b7a.original: Your painful life lessons are the raw material for your future wisdom.

df8e5691555e.text: 所有建议都只是别人告诉你他们做过的事。我犯过书中所有的错误。后来我看完了那本书,还发明了一些新的错误。
df8e5691555e.original: All advice is just someone telling you what they did. I've made every single mistake in the book. And then I got to the end of the book and I started inventing new mistakes.

489039a7190a.text: 生命太短暂,不能全靠自己犯错来学习。我们应该从别人的失败中吸取教训。
489039a7190a.original: Life is too short to make all our mistakes ourselves. So we should be learning from other people's failures as well.

299a8509a778.text: 成功父母最大的诅咒就是无法把他们经历过的艰难困苦赠予自己的孩子。
299a8509a778.original: The biggest curse of successful parents is that that's the only gift they'll not be able to give to their kids, the gift of struggle that they had.

ebf34558e6f7.text: 不要自我否定 - 让别人来说不。不要因为自己认为缺乏经验或不够合适而不去申请。
ebf34558e6f7.original: Don't self-select because I think it's really easy to say, 'I don't have the experience,' or, 'I'm not X, Y, Z enough,' and not apply.

50d159c26388.text: 当有人给你一个机会,无论多么疯狂或荒谬,即使你不想做,但如果坚持你的信仰系统,这些常常会带来生命中最出色和最非凡的机会。
50d159c26388.original: When someone offers you an opportunity, as crazy as it is, as ridiculous, as much as you don't want to do it, which many times in my life, the yeses that I have said about something I did not want to do, but forced myself to do it because of my belief system have resulted in the best and most extraordinary opportunities of my life.

e7885540981e.text: 不要等待去创造了不起的事物。仅仅是放自己出去,就可能激发出一些了不起的事情。
e7885540981e.original: Don't wait to create amazing things. Often just the act of putting yourself out there can just spur amazing things in itself.

4711753c22be.text: 你必须退回到你真正掌握的领域。例如,当我在微软工作时,尽管我的英语不太好,有口音等,但我知道自己是最懂在线开发的人。
4711753c22be.original: You have to retreat to a place where you feel real mastery of. So for example, when I was at Microsoft, I was like, 'Well, I don't speak the language very well, English,' and I had an accent, et cetera, but I knew that I was the most online developer person out there.

49eb61c2fe66.text: 装作直到成为。我不是说谎或假装成为你不是的样子,而是一种克服内心怀疑的方式,通过为自己创造成为想成为的人的机会,从而获得实现那样的机会。
49eb61c2fe66.original: Fake it till you make it. I don't mean lie. I don't mean pretend to be something that you're not, but it's almost like a way to overcome imposter syndrome and by opening rooms for yourself to be who you want to become so that you enable opportunities to become that.

5bb30259293b.text: 每当我换新工作时,我都觉得自己不应该在那里,我是真的这么想的。
5bb30259293b.original: When every new job I've been in, I have always felt that I didn't deserve to be there and I mean I genuinely.

49f40c95fe0e.text: 接纳成为专业愚者的状态 - 提出愚蠢的问题
49f40c95fe0e.original: Learning to embrace being a professional idiot. Being the one that shows up at the meeting and is like, 'What are we talking about? What does that word mean?'

875122b2e6e2.text: 好奇心强的人会不断展示他们对自己的专业知识并不自负,当他们面临一个根本不知如何解决的问题时,他们会表现出令人难以置信的兴奋。
875122b2e6e2.original: A curious person is somebody who is constantly demonstrating that they are not proud of their expertise, and they will demonstrate extraordinary amounts of excitement when they face a problem which they have no clue how to solve.

df2a1f0fb975.text: 我越成长,我越觉得自己是个初学者。这种感觉很奇怪。我最初起步的时候,我以为自己什么都知道,或者至少知道的比实际上多。但是一旦你超越了某个高峰,就会进入一个低谷,你会意识到,哇,当你接近某个知识的边缘时,你又开始成为一个新手了,一切都变得全新。
df2a1f0fb975.original: The bigger I get, the more a beginner I tend to feel. It's a weird feeling. I think when I first took off, I think I thought I knew everything or I knew more than I certainly did. But then you get past some peak or you go into this trough where you realize, oh my God, the moment you get to some frontier of knowledge, you start to become a beginner again and everything is new.

cd7a5070d956.text: 不要觉得寻求帮助是一种羞耻的事情。这会让很多人觉得受到了极大的荣耀。在一个人的生活中,最大的荣耀,或者说是最大的荣耀之一,就是当别人求助于他们。因为我们都只是想感到自己是有用的。
cd7a5070d956.original: Don't feel ashamed to reach out to something for help. It gives a lot of them great honor. The biggest honor most people get in their lives, or one of the biggest honor is when other people ask them for help. Because we all just want to feel useful.

440691eae651.text: 这些都是可以掌握的技能。这与个性无关。我们讨论过的所有这些事情,如建立人际网络、主动出现等,都是可以学习的技能。
440691eae651.original: These are skills that can be mastered. This is not about personality. These are skills, everything we've talked about, networking, showing up, all these things. These are skills that can be learned.

8ba878a873de.text: 如果别人不了解你是谁,Lenny是绝不会得到晋升的。你不能选择自己不知道的东西。
8ba878a873de.context: "Lenny"指的是采访Pfeffer关于个人品牌建立和职业发展的主持人Lenny Rachitsky。
8ba878a873de.original: No one is going to promote Lenny if they don't know who the hell you are. You cannot choose what is not in your head.
8ba878a873de.originalContext: Lenny refers to Lenny Rachitsky, the host interviewing Pfeffer about building personal brands and career advancement.

ab8a7d716d4f.text: 如果你觉得这很不舒服,或者你认为自己在这方面不擅长,那就去找教练。单独靠自己做任何事情都是很困难的。
ab8a7d716d4f.context: "这"指的是Pfeffer所教授的可学习能力,而不是天生的性格特征。
ab8a7d716d4f.original: If you think this is uncomfortable, or if you think you're not skilled at this, get coaching. It's hard to do anything on your own.
ab8a7d716d4f.originalContext: "This" refers to developing power skills, which Pfeffer teaches as learnable abilities rather than innate personality traits.

43ca4efbb215.text: 如果你认为权力是肮脏的,那么第一件事就是我不会去做我需要做的事情来取得职业成功。
43ca4efbb215.original: If you think power is dirty, the first thing that's going to happen is I'm not going to do what I need to do to be successful in my career.

ab99613b34a5.text: 你可以拥有权力,也可以拥有自主权,但你不能同时拥有这两者。
ab99613b34a5.original: You can have power or you can have autonomy, but you cannot have both.

f4e31255b258.text: 如果你绘制出你所掌控和无法掌控的范围图表,在你刚开始职业生涯时,大部分工作都在你可以掌控的范围内。当你成长为中高级职位时,我看到对话的重心从'我能做什么'转变为'为什么组织不为我做这件事?'
f4e31255b258.context: 在产品管理职业发展对话中,'轴'指的是一个概念性图表,映射您可以控制和无法控制的事物。
f4e31255b258.original: If you drew an access of what you control and what you cannot control, as you're starting your career, most of the work that you're doing is in what you control. As you start becoming mid-senior, I see the conversation shifts from what can I do to why is the organization not doing this for me?
f4e31255b258.originalContext: Context note: In product management career development conversations, "axis" refers to a conceptual chart mapping what you can control versus what you cannot control.

ec976bf35d8b.text: 当你年轻、刚起步时,变革的步伐是疯狂的。你的成长几乎每隔6个月就会有飞跃。当你成为中高级职位时,我开始看到这样的对话:'好吧,也许我不应该那样做。也许我不应该接下这个产品。我不知道这对我的职业发展意味着什么。'
ec976bf35d8b.original: When you are younger, when you're starting off, rate of change is crazy. You are growing almost every six months. As you start becoming mid-senior, I start seeing conversations on, 'Okay, maybe I should not do that. Maybe I should not take on this product. I don't know what it means for my career.'

9fe5c70431c1.text: 如果你把一只青蛙扔进一锅沸水里,它会立即跳出来。但如果你把一只青蛙放进锅里,然后逐渐升高温度,青蛙就感觉不到危险,最终被煮熟。我将这个类比应用到你的问题上,就是很容易成为惰性的牺牲品。
9fe5c70431c1.original: If you take a frog, and you throw in a pot of boiling water, it'll jump out. But if you take a frog and you put in a pot and you increase the temperature degree by degree by degree, the frog doesn't notice and before it knows, it's boiled alive. And how I apply this to your question to come back and circle back to it is that, it's really easy to be a victim of inertia.

6a9c32094291.text: 绝对不要在你愿意免费做这件事,无论是永远还是你想一直尝试下去,都不会赚到任何钱的情况下去开始一个播客。你很可能会开始一个播客,但它不会爆红,也不会非常成功。
6a9c32094291.original: Absolutely, do not start the podcast if you wouldn't do it for free, making no amount of money in perpetuity or as long as you want to experiment with. You are most likely going to start a podcast and it will not take off and be wildly successful.

1ca616d30fdc.text: 你就是你自己最好的版本。比如说,你是一个刚从学校毕业的21岁产品经理,第一年工作...就谈谈你的成长经历,谈谈你正在做什么,谈谈你正在学习的东西。
1ca616d30fdc.original: You are the best you out there. So for example... let's say you are a 21-year-old PM, fresh out of school, first year... you just talk about your journey, talk about what you're doing, talk about what you're learning.

0dac66465120.text: 不管哪种方式,都要分享你的知识。在这个过程中,你会学到更多。如果你在考虑做一个时事通讯或类似的东西,就开始教授和分享你所知道的,以及你的观察。这可以是一份时事通讯,也可以是一个YouTube视频,或者参加一个meetup。
0dac66465120.original: Share your knowledge one way or the other. And as you're doing it, you're going to learn a lot more. If you're thinking of a newsletter or something similar, start teaching and sharing what you know and what you're observing. This could be a newsletter, this could be a YouTube video, this could be going to meetup.

c4f745dad366.text: 要成为知识很丰富的人是没有捷径的...看看Tomasz Tunguz,他之前在Redpoint,现在自己开了一家风险投资公司。我和他聊过他的博客,他说他每周早上5点或6点起床,就写3到4篇博客,坚持了10年。
c4f745dad366.original: There's no shortcuts to knowing a lot... You look at Tomasz Tunguz, who was with Redpoint and now started his own VC firm. And I was talking to him about his blog and he was like, 'I'd just wake up 5:00 or 6:00 AM every morning and write three to four blogs a week for 10 years.'

0d9cc79f9cf4.text: 我们真的在寻找这种强大的主动性,这些人不会等待别人允许他们做某事,而是会直接看到问题并去解决它。
0d9cc79f9cf4.original: High agency is something that we really look for, people that are not going to come in and wait for everyone else to allow them to do something, they're just going to see a problem and go do it.

8bbf10394831.text: 我认为这种主动性可能被稍微低估了。我们没有优先考虑如何确保我们有真正主动的人,他们渴望去创造一些东西。
8bbf10394831.original: One of the things that's maybe a little bit undervalued is this kind of agency piece. We don't prioritize how do you make sure you get people with real agency that want to build something.

930d62fccae3.text: 我认为这并不是真的。他们实际上可以做很多事情,而不必认为自己只是某个公司的受害者,被困在一个功能团队中无能为力。
930d62fccae3.original: Too many people in our industry view themselves as a victim of their company, like they're stuck in a feature team and there's nothing they can do about it other than quit. I think that's not true. There is so much they can do.

dd2e24a5d491.text: 我试着通过不放弃,一次次冷呼叫或冷露面,或者一次次主动提供帮助,直到最终实现我的目标。
dd2e24a5d491.original: I sort of tried to create the luck by not giving up and just repeatedly cold calling or cold showing up or cold volunteering until I sort of was able to make it happen.

f98a7321870b.text: 如果没有你的主动行动,这个世界会少了什么?
f98a7321870b.original: What's something that would not exist without your initiative?

55c17d90ff83.text: 把自己包围在最优秀的人之中。如果你在职业生涯的早期创造足够多的机会,让自己能与那些做着有趣事物、以不同方式行事的人在一起,正确的事物就会发生。
55c17d90ff83.original: Surround yourself with the best people you can find. If you create enough opportunities, especially early on in your career, around hanging around people who are doing interesting things and they're doing things which really are different, or they're doing things in a different manner and it's exciting, the right things will happen.

cf5ef8a145af.text: 他们与我没有什么不同,但他们总是待在这些房间里。他们与不同有趣的人交流,这就是让他们不同的原因。
cf5ef8a145af.original: There was nothing different about them versus me, but they were in these rooms constantly. They were around different, interesting people. They were having these conversations and that was what was making them different.

c91d9211ba4d.text: 我在那里学到的一个教训一直困扰着我,我认为这对其他人也可能有用,那就是不仅仅是做一些实际上很重要的事情,并且学习,还要能讲述故事,并了解其他人认为什么是有价值的。
c91d9211ba4d.original: I had one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story, and it's about understanding what other people perceive as valuable.

e27c17e83dbb.text: 我特别在更高层面上看到的最大问题是,人们谈论他们所做的事情,但并没有解释它为什么很重要。他们没有谈论产生的影响。
e27c17e83dbb.original: The biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered. They don't talk about the impact.

a3be2886479b.text: 我们总是想看到人们在推动进展,特别是在产品领域,他们的手印在哪里,他们在任职期间做过什么,并为此感到自豪。
a3be2886479b.original: We're always looking to see where people moved the needle, especially on the product side, where their fingerprints were, what they can actually point to that they did and are proud of during their time there.

823d53fdbd86.text: 我将优先考虑待办事项并将其发送给开发人员的方式有所不同。更进一步 - 你的客户是谁?你有没有去与他们交谈过?
823d53fdbd86.original: The way different story than I prioritized backlog and I shipped it off to developers. Take it a step further - who are your customers? Did you go out and talk to them?

ca7044f4b303.text: 确保你今天做的工作所讲述的故事对你的上级有意义。因此,如果你坐下来写下'在未来6个月、12个月或24个月内,当我完成或结束这个角色时,我将写下这样一段话:我解决了一个问题,我培养了一项技能,我面临了一些阻力,我采取了什么措施来克服它。'在句子中使用'我',不要使用'我们'。
ca7044f4b303.original: Ensure that the story you will tell about the work you're doing today is meaningful for your skip job. So if you sit down and you write down, 'In six months, in 12 months, in 24 months, when I achieve or finish this role, here's the paragraph I'll write. Here's a problem I solved. Here's the skill I built. Here's the headwind I faced. Here's what I did to overcome it.' Use I in the sentence, do not use we.

7177ee8a79f7.text: 不要去学习你认为值得学习的东西。找一个你真正关心的实际问题,用新的方式去尝试解决它。
7177ee8a79f7.original: Don't try to go learn something because you think it's worth learning. Find an actual problem that you care about and go try to solve it with that new thing.

9f5527c53060.text: 我一直回到这个问题上。我想,这个世界如何应对社交媒体上信息质量的问题?无论信息从哪里来,在这家公司,我可以为这个问题做出贡献,为什么不尝试一些疯狂的点子,看看是否有一个可行?
9f5527c53060.original: I kept coming back to this problem. I'm like, 'Man, how is the world going to deal with this information quality issue of what we get on social media?' Wherever get it. I'm at this company where you can make a difference on this problem, why not go and try some crazy ideas and see if one of them might work?

6c3c20a167ee.text: 对我来说,这个项目就像是在做公益事业。我把工作视为为人民和社区服务,这就是我的动力。我唯一关心的就是为世界提供有帮助的成果。
6c3c20a167ee.original: For me, this project, I feel like I get to do community service with this project. I see my work as in service of the people and the community, and that's what motivates me. The only thing that I care about is delivering the outcome that the world finds helpful.

fedbcec715d6.text: 在面试过程中,你的工作就是找出那个迫切需要解决的问题。戴上探索者的帽子,弄清楚招聘经理在引进新的产品经理时到底需要什么。
fedbcec715d6.original: It's your job when you're in the interview process to figure out what that burning problem is. Put on your discovery hat and go figure out what is the actual job to be done of the hiring manager when they're bringing on a new PM onto their team.

65f781be9227.text: 有种信念认为每个人都要当创始人。我觉得,在某种程度上,如果我们的行业有更少的创始人,会更好。有一大类聪明、有创意、勤劳、有才华,甚至有某种远见的人,他们可以筹到200万美元的种子轮,然后去建立一些永远无法成功的公司。他们最好是找到一个需要他们技能的团队,致力于一个有数学公式支撑、必将成功的问题。
65f781be9227.original: There's this belief that everybody needs to be a founder. I think, in some ways, our industry would be much better off if there were fewer founders. There's an entire category of smart, creative, hardworking, talented, borderline visionary people who can raise that $2 million seed and go off and build some stupid company that's never going to go anywhere. That would be so much better off finding a team that needs their skillset and working on a problem that has a mathematical formula that's going to win on any metric.

c79324090b9f.text: 我常常这样对那些考虑从事产品管理的人说:'这太棒了。只是你一定要非常确定自己准备好了。'这就像很多人想要当经理一样。你要知道,当经理就意味着'你要做大量的绩效评估,和很多一对一的谈话'。你一定要真的喜欢这类工作。
c79324090b9f.original: I say this often actually, to folks who are thinking about going into product management. 'That's awesome. Just be really, really sure about what you're signing up for.' It's kind of the same as, I think a lot of people want to become a manager. But just so you know, being a manager is like, 'Hey, you're doing performance reviews a lot. And you're in one-on-ones a lot.' You have to really love that kind of work.

eee0aa9e0e8a.text: 在你成为产品经理之前,就开始做产品管理的工作。打开你最喜欢的应用程序,列出你发现的前10个问题。
eee0aa9e0e8a.original: Already start product management, doing product management before you're a product manager. Open up your favorite apps. What are the top 10 problems you see?

2f76691f7baa.text: 我非常建议产品运营主管先担任过这个角色,先有过实际的产品构建经验,了解客户问题并感同身受,因为你很快就会意识到要把精力放在哪里,以及团队的努力应该集中在哪里。
2f76691f7baa.original: I strongly advocate for product ops leaders to have done that role, to have actually had hands-on product experience building and understanding customer problems and feeling that pain, because you very quickly realize where to place your efforts and where your team's efforts should go.

0da4a72ee0ce.text: 他们非常谨慎,只有那些首先证明自己是出色的前线工程师的人才能成为产品经理。你基本上没有其他成为产品经理的方式。
0da4a72ee0ce.context: 在Palantir公司,所谓的'前线工程师'是在客户现场而不是传统办公环境中工作的软件工程师。
0da4a72ee0ce.original: They were extremely careful about only making people PMs who had first proven themselves out as forward deployed engineers. You basically could not become a PM any other way.
0da4a72ee0ce.originalContext: At Palantir, "forward deployed engineers" are software engineers who work on-site at customer locations rather than in traditional office settings.

a5cd7a8bf436.text: 如果你能够放下一些事情,把时间投入到更值得你花时间的事情上,那就来做这个角色吧。公司会变,我们的流程也需要不断调整。
a5cd7a8bf436.original: Get into this role if you're comfortable letting go of things and moving on to something that is well worth your time. The company's going to change. Our process is going to need to be tweaked.

80f1cd156cdd.text: 先伸手帮助,再提要求 - 这就是如何开始建立导师关系
80f1cd156cdd.original: Go reach out to a PM and ask how you can make their day easier. Figure out what you can do in your spare time that they can offload to you and do a little bit of volunteer labor, even if that's just shadowing because I think just getting that context and understanding the sort of rhythm of how a team ideates and defines problems and prioritizes and ship software is the experience that's going to be the most important.

f37e6c88c252.text: 不要直接请求某人当你的导师,这很尴尬。首先确定你认为能对你有帮助的人,然后想办法去帮助他们。
f37e6c88c252.original: Don't ask a person to be your mentor. That's really awkward. First, identify them. Say, this is a person I think that could be helpful to me. And then, find ways to be helpful.

ab5685415612.text: 一旦我确定了预期的结果,我就会倒推回去,看看要怎么实现。接下来我就会提出问题,寻找这个领域最优秀的人,与他们探讨。
ab5685415612.original: Once I have this outcome, I work backwards to figure out how am I going to do that. What I do then is I start asking questions and then I find the best people in the field and I just go talk to them.

3353fd38cd78.text: 当人们告诉我,'嘿,我即将去一家公司面试。'我第一个问的问题是,'你做过多少次模拟面试?'答案通常是零。我建议人们进行数十次这样的模拟面试。
3353fd38cd78.original: When people tell me, 'Hey, I'm going to a interview at this company.' First question I ask is, 'How many mock interviews have you done?' And the answer typically is zero. I would recommend people to do dozens of those mock interviews.

4dd846a29d76.text: 你想要练习到即使是在最糟糕的情况下,你也能表现得足够好。我总是觉得在大多数面试中,我实际上都表现得很糟糕。只是勉强够格了。你太紧张了,无法与对方产生共鸣。
4dd846a29d76.original: You want to basically practice so much that even at your worst, you're good enough. I've always felt like most interviews, I literally did my worst. It's just that it was good enough to pass. You're so stressed out, you don't relate to the person, et cetera.

d93c277c0773.text: 在任何面试中,最重要的一个和二个因素是外表和热情。人们想要与愿意与他们合作的人一起工作。
d93c277c0773.original: The number one and two factors in any interview are appearance and enthusiasm. People want to work with people that want to work with them.

837ac5dc1ad6.text: 如果你专注于工作,并且在解决问题时能够得心应手地享受其中,很多人就会主动出来说你表现很出色,并且建议你的上司给你晋升。你不需要主动要求晋升,你的工作成果应该能够自己说话。
837ac5dc1ad6.original: If you're present in your job, and you actually have fun with it and solve the problems, people will come out of the woodwork, say, 'You're great, and tell your boss you should be promoted.' You don't need to ask for a promotion. Your outcomes should speak for themselves.

0232ba08c3b9.text: 我花了多年慢慢爬上公司的高层... 我一直认为只要把头埋下来,把手头的工作做好就够了。但后来我环顾四周... 有些人获得了更多机会。
0232ba08c3b9.original: I spent years slowly climbing the corporate ranks... And I spent years just thinking that all I need to do is put my head down, do my job really well and that was it. But then I looked around... some sort of people were getting way more opportunities.

fb15807db84f.text: 生命的奥秘就是你早就听过无数次的东西,只是你还没有准备好去领悟。
fb15807db84f.original: The secrets of life is things you've heard a million times already, you just weren't ready to hear them.

7c66eff41ea7.text: 要获得晋升的方法就是不要过于迫切地想要它。关键是要专注于产生影响。你是否在从事对企业有正确影响的正确工作?因为如果你确实在这样做,并且全力投入,这一点就会显而易见。
7c66eff41ea7.original: The way to get promoted is to not want it too badly. It is about you have to focus on the impact. Are you working on the right things that will have the right outcome for the business? Because if you are and if you are giving it to your 100%, that will be visible.

d9157206382a.text: 大多数人认为工作应该为他们完成所有事情,但事实并非如此。我们需要帮助他们平衡这一点,并认识到即使在你认为糟糕的情况下,你也能从中学到很多东西。
d9157206382a.original: Most people think their job is supposed to do everything for them and the reality is it's not. And so part of it's being able to help them balance that out and realize that even in a situation that you think is horrible, there's a lot of things you're learning in the middle of it.

b7234556eee3.text: 产品特性和产品体验是不同的,你会发现是体验让你一直留在这份工作中。这不仅仅是关乎金钱,因为你会意识到金钱只是对尊重的替代,或者我需要付账单,或者我落后了。
b7234556eee3.original: There's difference between product features and product experiences, and what you start to realize is it's the experiences that keep you at your job. It's not just about the money because you start to realize money is a surrogate for respect, or I've got bills to pay or I'm falling behind.

3e9a3328abc0.text: 53%的人说他们赚了更多钱,但实际上并没有赚更多钱。他们告诉公司他们赚了更多钱,因为他们知道他们无法反驳自己赚了更多钱的说法,这样才能让公司让他们回来。
3e9a3328abc0.context: 莫埃斯塔在讨论 Autobooks 的销售团队如何调查银行客户的兴趣与实际购买决策之间的差异。
3e9a3328abc0.original: 53% of the people who basically said they got more money, did not get more money. They told the company they had more money because they knew they couldn't argue with having them come back because they got more money.
3e9a3328abc0.originalContext: Moesta is discussing sales teams at Autobooks who were surveying potential bank customers about their interest versus tracking actual purchasing decisions.

2ddc0c321fec.text: 你的事业不等同于你的生活。生活中还有很多其他方面。
2ddc0c321fec.original: Your career's not your life. There's a lot more to it than that.

925012f35781.text: 你必须设法让你个人的成长曲线保持在公司增长曲线的前面。
925012f35781.original: You have to figure out how to keep your personal growth curve ahead of the company's growth curve.

f4260ac3ae2f.text: 如果你真的想充分利用公司的成长,你必须以与公司增长一样的速度成长,既要学会放弃你擅长的事情,又要迈向下一个新的领域。
f4260ac3ae2f.original: You have to grow as fast as your company is growing if you really want to take advantage, both learning to give away what you've gotten good at and move on to the next shiny pile of Legos.

6fdeabd6b859.text: 从零到一很擅长的公司,不一定能自然而然地成为10到100这个阶段的佼佼者。创始人必须不断进化。
6fdeabd6b859.original: Companies that are very, very good at zero to one will not naturally become great at 10 to 100. The founder has to evolve.

13fa36dfe06d.text: 我觉得让我到达这个阶段的那些特质,未必就是让我在下一阶段取得成功的那些特质。你的超级能力常常是带你到这个位置并让你成功的原因,但你总担心一旦放弃它就无法继续成功,这种担心确实很令人畏惧。
13fa36dfe06d.original: I felt that what got me to this phase is not necessarily what's going to make me successful in the next phase. Many times your superpowers that brought you to this point and made you successful, many times you think that if you let it go you won't be successful and it's frightening.

1c1da04481d7.text: 如果您想要开始管理一群产品经理,如果您想要开始运营一个业务部门或者一个支柱或者一个主题,那作为首席产品官,我会期望您能够独立撰写那份策略文档。

cfc8720f60c7.text: 即使我没有那个角色或责任或范围,我也会坐在那里,想象如果我在他们的位置,我会怎么做。我认为这很有力量。假装你是首席产品官。你会做些什么不同的事情吗?你会怎么做?
cfc8720f60c7.original: Even when I didn't have that role or responsibility or that scope, I sat there and I still imagined what I would do if I was in their position. And I think that's powerful. Pretend you're the CPO. Would you do something different? What would you do?

6bcd06138924.text: 三级和七级之间的区别可能并非在于范围。他们可能做完全相同的工作。关键在于他们的工作方式,这里有一些关于他们如何工作的说法。

ce5644eaf6d5.text: 从高中和大学开始的一切都集中在范围上。而现在您突然被告知,我们不再以范围来判断你,而是以这个'PSHE'事情来评判你。

7007aaa255c7.text: 跳崖之路要比缓慢的台阶过得有趣得多,虽然你会摔下去,但最终你会爬出比台阶更远的地方。
7007aaa255c7.original: The much more fun careers are like jumping off cliffs and you do fall, but then you climb out way beyond where the stairs could ever get you.

7b13d7340161.original: Over the course of seven years, I went from my first job, which was basically this entry level sales job at Microsoft, working on Microsoft adCenter to SVP of marketing at SurveyMonkey, leading a global team. And when I reflect back on what works across my early career, it really comes down in a nutshell to this career concept of explore and exploit.

8203eddb5b43.text: 没有线性的成功。没有一帆风顺的完美曲线图。无论是谁,连苹果也没有。
8203eddb5b43.original: There is no linear success. There's no up-and-to-the-right perfect chart where it's just one line. I don't care who you are. Apple doesn't have one. No one has one.

636552ea6720.text: 好奇心和对工作的热情投入,比皱纹更能引起别人的注意。

bddc0af0a2c9.text: 当我年轻的时候,我决定想成为一名首席营销官。在我决定想成为首席营销官的那份工作里,我比团队中其他人多工作两个小时。我当时脑子里有这样的想法,每天多工作两个小时,5年下来我就能比别人多几年的经验。

And at the job where I had decided I wanted to be the CMO, I worked two hours later than everyone else on the team. And I had this thought in my brain that two hours every day for five years would get me how many more years of experience than someone else?

082b901a2da7.text: 自我反思和请教教练的艺术。我整个职业生涯都有请教练。你不断迭代、实验,并努力成为在职业、作为父亲和丈夫方面的最佳版本。
082b901a2da7.original: The art of self-reflection and coaches. I've had coaches my whole career. You're constantly iterating, experimenting, and becoming the best you can be in your career also as a dad and as a husband.

23b69d748443.original: I dedicate an hour aside to really think about, 'What's going well? What's not going well? What am I screwing up? Why am I screwing it up?' which is often more important than 'What am I screwing up?' And 'What am I going to do about it?'

81c8276182ae.text: 如果你给我反馈,我会说'非常感谢,这非常有帮助',因为人们会想'哦,他真的喜欢这个反馈'。内心可能会难过,我会想'我以为我在这方面有所改进'。但外表上,我会说'谢谢',并且真心这样说。
81c8276182ae.original: If you give me feedback, I'll be like, 'Hey, thank you so much. This is super helpful,' because people are like, 'Oh, he actually likes the feedback.' 58a0cd9c2580.text: 这就是出色的疗愈之道,在我看来,这是卓越领导力的秘诀。它可以消除你的锐利棱角,但这些锐利棱角往往都是非常不利的。
58a0cd9c2580.original: Great, great therapy and it has to be great, is a recipe for brilliant leadership in my opinion. It takes your edges off, but they're all edges that are super counterproductive.

And after a little bit of that, I was like, 'It might be easier if I just go, I might be able save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.'

85678f136f0b.text: 你并不真正从自己的失败中学到东西,而是从成功中学到的。当然,在那段时间里我也学到了很多,成长了很多,但在我在Rippling工作的六七年里,我学到的更多,因为我见证了成功。
85678f136f0b.original: You don't really learn from your mistakes, you learn from your successes. Of course, I learned and grew a ton during that time, but in now what I think is six or seven years at Rippling, I've learned so much more because I've seen success.

f187b7ff2688.text: 我认为伟大的事业是通过认识许多从事优秀工作的人而建立的,这样他们就知道你并希望你加入他们的团队,并等待偶然机会的出现,然后抓住机会并跳进去。
f187b7ff2688.original: I think great careers are built by knowing a lot of people doing great work so they know and want you on their teams, and just waiting for serendipity and then seizing it and jumping.

d541d6415020.text: 情绪调节确实非常重要。这可能是我最常思考的事情,也是我希望我的孩子们学会的最重要的东西。
d541d6415020.original: Emotional regulation is still really, really, really important. That's probably the thing that I think about the most in terms of what I want my kids to learn.

They've been trained in data analysis or software engineering or AI, and whatnot. You can get there, anyone can get there, of course, by learning the concepts, but most people don't have that skill right now.

32ceb2265f5e.text: 我的观点是,对绝大多数人来说,他们可能不需要一个教练。我经常建议那些想找教练的人,你寻找教练的目标是什么?
32ceb2265f5e.original: My hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach. And what I often push people on is if you're thinking about getting a coach, which is usually an indication that they have a feeling of being stuck or they have a problem that they're trying to solve, I ask them, 'What are your goals when it comes to coaching?'

e7978f4ac460.text: 如果你需要一个导师,教练并不是一个很好的导师,因为那只是一个人的观点。实际上,最好是进行一个好奇心循环,向几个不同的专家征询意见,获得他们各自专长领域的建议会更有帮助。
e7978f4ac460.context: 「好奇心循环」指的是向多个不同专家寻求建议,而不是依赖一个教练的观点。
e7978f4ac460.original: If you're looking for a mentor, a coach is actually a terrible mentor in some ways because it's this one person's opinion. It's actually way better to run a curiosity loop, for example, and get the benefit a couple different minds on a specific topic and hit their wheelhouse of things that they know about.
e7978f4ac460.originalContext: "Curiosity loop" refers to Ada's term for seeking advice from multiple different experts rather than relying on one coach's perspective.

e564f2ec70d9.text: 一半的人在选择教练时,直接去了他们朋友推荐的教练。你的朋友说他的教练很好,于是你就去找了他的教练。这种方式没什么不好,但我还是很建议人们至少谈谈几个不同的教练,因为适合你朋友的教练不一定适合你。
e564f2ec70d9.original: Half of people that founder their coach literally went with the first coach that they talked to. It's that your buddy said, 'I work with this great coach.' And then you go and you hire your buddy's coach. I think that's a totally fine way to go find a coach, but I would actually really just urge people to talk to a couple because what works for your friend may not work for you.

4d789d3a2688.text: 在经济衰退期,我经历了人生中最大的职业发展。在2000年代和2008年,当其他人放慢脚步时,我能够加快前进。
4d789d3a2688.original: Some of my greatest career growth came in the economic downturns. In the 2000s, in the 2008. Because other people take their foot off the gas, and you can put your foot down.

df6f425a1011.text: 如果您愿意学习更多,主动承担新的角色或职责,在公司内部寻找没人负责的项目,就能够在不大规模招聘的时期得到发展。
df6f425a1011.original: If you're willing to learn more, hit yourself into new roles or new responsibilities that no one's covering at your company. When they don't hire tons of people for everything, there's lots of open projects where you can raise your hand and grow.

e33db34f96c3.original: The most important career decision you make is who you marry. You will have a much more successful career if your home life is in balance. It's like a yin and a yang.

a0b721e2904d.original: Get fired for doing it the way you think is right. There's nothing that was a faster career accelerator than being known in the industry as the person who stands for that principle so much that you got fired over it.

9531e343591f.text: 我认为有时候人们使用数据太多或过度,因为他们担心或害怕做出错误的选择。他们使用数据来帮助自己做出选择。但有时你仍然觉得这不是正确的选择,但数据告诉你这是正确的选择,结果可能是对的也可能不对。
9531e343591f.original: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me. 0e8c24fa27a3.text: 相信你的直觉。相信你的内心感受。它已经吸收了所有的信息。而且还吸收了一些你不知道但很有价值的信息。
0e8c24fa27a3.original: Give your intuition credit. Give your gut credit. It's absorbed everything. And plus the things that you don't know it absorbed that are valuable.

a8f4385e8c28.text: 我认为所有的决定都是一种判断。数据可以起一定作用,其他各种因素也可以。但除非你让机器做出纯粹理性的决定,否则这需要人类做出判断。
a8f4385e8c28.original: I think everything's a judgment call. And so yeah, data can play a part. All sorts of things can play a part, but unless you're letting a machine make the decision, that's purely rational. If you're asking a human to make it's a judgment call.

1eb40d9f5144.text: 实验不应该成为公司做决策的方式。了解用户、理解市场对于大脑来整合这些信息依然很重要。

db217ce92f20.text: 我认为你的直觉也是一种数据,它也是完全有效的。关键是要明确你正在使用的是什么类型的数据,然后要像对待其他任何数据一样认真对待它。
db217ce92f20.original: I think your gut actually as a type of data and I think it's a totally valid one and it's just I think you need to be clear that that's what you're working with, but then it should be taken as seriously as any other data point.

e1b905bb3672.text: 所有决策都是情感驱动的,而非逻辑分析。我们在大脑的情感中心做出决策。我们使用逻辑来试图弄清楚我们会有什么感受。没有什么所谓的逻辑决策。这个想法就好像,'我只是要逻辑地,只是做一个逻辑决策,'但这在神经学上是不成立的。
e1b905bb3672.original: We make decisions in the emotional center of our brain. We use logic to try to figure out how we're going to feel. There's no such thing as a logical decision. That idea is like, I'm just going to be logical and just make a logical decision, it doesn't. Neurologically, it's just untrue.

b3ac27002e9c.text: 如果你学会爱上所有的情感,那么以前没有的解决方案就会变得可用。如果你说,'哦,我不能感到失败,'那么你可能就不会采取某些冒险。
b3ac27002e9c.original: If you learn to fall in love with all of your emotions, then solution sets become available that you didn't have before. If you are like, 'Oh, I can't feel like a failure.' Well, then you're probably not going to take certain risks.

556ba7d520ab.text: 你试图避免的任何情绪,都会以你试图避免的方式进入你的生活。
556ba7d520ab.original: Whatever emotion that you're trying to avoid, you are inviting into your life in exactly the way that you're trying to avoid it.

a0d97f6e7bf5.text: 90%的时候我们被分心,不是因为外界发生了什么,而是因为大多数分心源于内心的无聊、孤独、疲劳、不确定和焦虑。
a0d97f6e7bf5.original: 90% of the time that we get distracted, it's not because of what's happening outside of us, but that most distraction begins from within boredom, loneliness, fatigue, uncertainty, anxiety.

4f204957e6ee.text: 拖延是一种情绪调节问题。这不是性格缺陷。你没有什么问题,也不是有什么破碎的地方。只是你没有处理情绪不适的工具。
4f204957e6ee.original: Procrastination is an emotion regulation problem. It's not a character flaw. There's nothing wrong with you, you're not broken. It's just that you don't have the tools to deal with emotional discomfort.

6fcfb97e7b66.text: 没有完全正确或错误的决定。只有快和慢的决定。大多数情况下,如果你做了错误的决定,只要决定得够快,你就能发现它是错误的,并及时纠正,比三思而后行后再下定决心要快得多。
6fcfb97e7b66.original: There's no right or wrong decision. There's just slow and fast decisions. A lot of the times if you make a wrong decision, if you make it fast enough, you would know it was wrong and you would correct it and you would still do it faster than thinking months for the right decision.

376d968473c2.text: 大多数情况下都是两条路。你可以回头。所以,拥有自己的观点并用它来凝聚团队,并让团队就此作出反应是非常重要的。
376d968473c2.original: Most things are two-way doors. You can come back. And so, it's so important to have an opinion and use that opinion to anchor people around and have people react to.

695ce6158958.text: 我给大家最大的建议是,过度分析、试图保证百分之百的正确有时反而会让你错失机会。
695ce6158958.original: My biggest advice to people is, oftentimes the analysis paralysis of dotting every eye, crossing every tee sometimes chokes you out of opportunities.

3efff86cc97c.text: 对大多数产品经理来说,你的策略应该是'我能多快从假设转到数据'。产品策略有时候被过度强调了。
3efff86cc97c.original: Strategy is a little bit overrated for product. For most product managers, your strategy should be, 'How fast can I go from hypothesis to data?'

e4b980e18753.text: 一旦做出决定,你就会在执行中获得更多高质量的信息,而不是一直停留在假设中。只要你的决定有70%是正确的,剩下的20%或30%就可以迭代优化。如果你一直犹豫不决,就永远无法获得有价值的反馈。
e4b980e18753.original: Once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical. And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.

2ad6866d5f43.text: 大多数公司需要以恰当的方式看待框架。他们把采用框架当作是最终目标……框架更像是一个工具箱。它们更像是一种学习工具。
2ad6866d5f43.original: Most of those companies need to think of frameworks appropriately. They see adopting the frameworks as the end goal...frameworks are more like a job aid. They're more like a learning tool.

444dc9a5b6dd.text: 任何框架都有其局限性,如果过于死板地遵循,就毫无用处。您需要灵活运用这些框架,体现一些微妙之处。
444dc9a5b6dd.original: Every framework at its limit is followed to such a religious extent it's just unhelpful. You need to have nuance in how you leverage these frameworks.

5e73863ba355.text: 有时候,单纯的判断力和产品意识就很重要。
5e73863ba355.original: Sometimes it's just good old-fashioned judgment and product taste.

4f83f75c345e.text: 您什么时候最后一次运用自己的大脑,而不是死板地遵循公司设计的流程?因为我想要的是前者,而不是后者。
4f83f75c345e.original: When's the last time you used your brain versus followed a process someone else designed at your company? Because I want the former, not the latter.

77b96e716649.text: 我最喜欢的面试问题就是,让别人描述自己职业生涯中学到的一个最佳实践,然后再问他们在什么情况下这个最佳实践不适用。大多数人都无法回答。
77b96e716649.original: My favorite interview question of all time is to ask people to describe a best practice that they learned in their career and then ask them to tell me a situation where that best practice would not be applicable. Most people can't do it.

6ccb1b572ca5.text: 人们不会后悔自己做过的事,而是那些没有做的事。因为如果你犯了错误,你可以采取行动来纠正它。
6ccb1b572ca5.original: People do not regret the things they do. They regret the things they didn't do. And the reason for this is if you've made a mistake, you can actually take action to correct it.

8ba31ba088fe.text: 我总是鼓励人们尽量犯行为上的错误,而不是犯疏忽的错误。因为如果你犯了行为上的错误,你可以观察它,从中学习。你会立即意识到这已经发生了。你可以迅速采取行动并进行调整,变得更好。而如果你犯了疏忽的错误,你就让现状获胜了,你没有观察,没有学习,也许甚至没有注意到机会的流失。
8ba31ba088fe.original: I always encourage people to try to make mistakes of commission rather than omission. Because if you make a mistake of commission you can observe it, you can learn from it. You know right away that it's happened. You can move really quickly and adapt and become better. Whereas if you make mistakes of omission you're letting status quo win, you're not observing, you're not learning, and you're maybe not even noticing opportunities slip by.

dce6d89c0f3b.text: 一个'是'可以随时变成一个'否'。是的,我会尝试一下。我穿过门槛,尝试一下,花一些时间去体验。我环顾四周,知道这不适合我。我再次穿过门槛,关上了门。但是在生活中,人们常常不会穿过那扇门。
dce6d89c0f3b.original: A yes can always become a no, right? Yes, I will try that. I step through the door, I give it a try, I spend some time with it. I look around and I say, you know what? Not for me. I step back through and I close the door. But so often in life, people don't step through the door.

fd3c2482de88.text: 自问一下,如果现在知道我所知道的,我会做出不同的选择吗?如果答案是肯定的,那就今天就做出不同的选择吧。不要等到下辈子、下一家公司、下一段关系或者下一个什么时候。
fd3c2482de88.original: Ask yourself, knowing what I know today, would I do something different? Now, if the answer is yes, then do something different today. Don't wait until next life or next company or next relationship or next something.

1ca0eaa23864.text: 等待得越久,你的选择余地就越少。唯一可以选择的时间就是今天。你必须尽快做出决定,就是今天。
1ca0eaa23864.original: The longer that you wait, you actually lose options. The only ability to choose is today. You actually need to make a decision rapidly, like today.

f8a33e4a7d15.text: 我很遗憾地告诉你们,你们遇到的问题并不是独一无二的。我99%确定这是事实。你们的问题在很多地方都有人感受到过,你们试图重新设计解决方案只会浪费宝贵的市场机会。
f8a33e4a7d15.original: I'm very sorry to break it to all of you, but your problem is not unique. I am 99% sure of that. Your problem has been felt by somebody somewhere in probably many, many places and you trying to re-engineer solution is time lost to market and has a huge opportunity cost.

828c30e03162.text: 你遇到的问题并非独一无二。我99%确定这是事实。你们的问题在某处已被他人感受到过,而你们试图重新设计解决方案只会浪费宝贵的市场时机。
828c30e03162.original: Your problem is not unique. I am 99% sure of that. Your problem has been felt by somebody somewhere and you trying to re-engineer solution is time lost to market.

9733693b8205.text: 没有人会随意地改变工作,这是不可能的。事实上,它都是由具体情况和环境所导致的,一旦意识到这一点,你就会发现环境因素在其中发挥着很大的影响。
9733693b8205.context: Moesta解释说,职业变动和购买决策看似随意,但实际上都是由特定环境和背景所导致的。
9733693b8205.original: Nobody randomly changes jobs, it's just not possible. And so the reality is you can describe it that way and most people would say Lucky is random, but the reality is it's caused and if it's now caused, you start to actually realize that context has a lot of impact in it.
9733693b8205.originalContext: Moesta is explaining that career changes and purchasing decisions appear random but are actually caused by specific circumstances and context.

64a327c0360b.text: 我们无法准确预测哪家公司最终会成功。这是不可能的。我们擅长的是识别失败的迹象。
64a327c0360b.original: We cannot figure out who's going to be the really successful company in the batch. That's not possible. What we're good at is knowing what failure looks like.

2d412b49f962.text: 如果你注定要失败,请用一种全新的、与众不同的方式来失败。不要重复那些我们已经见过100次的老套路。因为我们已经看到过很多人因各种原因而失败。
2d412b49f962.original: If you fail, please do it in some new exciting way. Not one that we've seen 100 times. Because we have seen people fail for a large number of reasons.

26bec88a48e9.text: 提高思考能力的最好方法就是进行实际思考。而写作正是这样的一种思考方式。如果你能够清晰地写下自己的想法,那也意味着你能够清晰地思考。
26bec88a48e9.original: The best way to increase your capacity to think is to actually do the thinking. And so that's where I see writing. If you're able to write things clearly, you're able to think through things clearly.

08527c797f3f.text: 说话能激活大脑的更多区域,相比之下,思考和写作则需要较少的大脑参与。
08527c797f3f.original: You activate a different part of your brain when you talk. You actually activate more of your brain when you talk than when you think or write. So thinking activates the least amount of your brain. Writing is a little bit better, but talking activates a whole different region of your brain.

067822097f3d.text: 追求真理,需要对自我有深刻的理解。如果你能养成每天坐下来用笔和纸给自己写作、提问并反思内心想法的习惯,那么仅凭这样一个安静的房间,就有可能达到某种内心的宁静与觉悟。
067822097f3d.original: At the end of the day, the seeking of the truth involves the seeking of a deep sense of self-understanding, and if you can get into the daily practice of being able to sit down with pen and paper and write to yourself, to ask yourself questions, to really sit there and evaluate the thoughts that are running through your head, it is possible for somebody to reach some state of bliss or enlightenment or some real spiritual awakening entirely on their own with just pen and paper and a quiet room.

fdb90c924ba7.text: 除非你清楚自己想要表达什么,否则是无法简洁地表述要点的。不清楚自己的想法,就很容易陷入冗长罗嗦。
fdb90c924ba7.original: You can't cut to the chase unless you know what the chase is. You can't unbury the lead unless you know what the lead is. And so that I found is the bottleneck to being concise. It's actually not really being clear of what you are thinking, that's what's leading to being long-winded.

873c6b5953c9.text: 用更少的词语表达同样的意思,会让每个词都变得沉重有力,这样所做的决策和权衡取舍就会更加有意图性。比如说某个东西'很棒',可能意味着能在两小时内交付,而另一个'很棒'可能是因为选择很广泛,这对于策略来说影响是完全不同的。
873c6b5953c9.original: Fewer words means every word is 10 pounds in weight instead of one, and that means that the decisions you're making, the trade offs are far more intentional, and in the case of great, if you say something is great because we're going to deliver something in two hours versus Amazon's great because the selection is very wide, the implications on strategy are completely different.

05f6018dd9a4.text: 容易选择,人生难。艰难选择,人生轻松。我发现,只要我做出容易的选择,我的生活就会变得艰难。而当我做出艰难的选择,比如关闭业务、解雇员工、放弃一个我很兴奋的项目时,这几乎总是正确的选择。
05f6018dd9a4.original: Easy choices, hard life. Hard choices, easy life. I often find that anytime that I'm making the easy choice, my life gets hard. And when I make the hard choice to shut down the business, fire the person, say bye to a project that I was excited about, it's almost always the right choice.

606a6463c331.text: 我会说,等到痛苦更加明显时再做决定。如果问题的关键是不熟悉新方式,那可能现有做法也还不错。毕竟这并不是唯一的选择。更多是因为改变真的很难,如果有好的理由去改变,比如我们已经尝试过不同的实验,甚至换过产品负责人或CTO,但仍然存在同样的问题,那么就到了我们必须尝试一些不同的东西的时候了,因为我们无法继续这种方式。
606a6463c331.context: 这里的'这'和'一些不同的东西'指的是Ryan Singer的Shape Up产品开发方法,它取代了传统的敏捷/Scrum方法,采用6周周期和事先'塑造'的方式。
606a6463c331.original: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine. Because it's not like this is the only way. It's more like, changing is really hard, and if there's a good reason to do it and it's like, look, we've done it the old way. We've tried different experiments. We've even already churned through a new head of product, or we've got a different CTO in and we're still having the same problems, then there comes a point where it's like, I know that this is uncomfortable, and I don't know somebody who's done it, but I think we need to try something different because we can't continue this way.
606a6463c331.originalContext: "This" and "something different" refer to Shape Up, Ryan Singer's product development methodology that replaces traditional Agile/Scrum approaches with 6-week cycles and upfront "shaping" work.

9744e859867b.text: 如果你继续做你一直在做的事,你就会得到你一直在得到的结果。
9744e859867b.original: If you keep doing what you're doing, you keep getting what you're getting.

dcbe647503c2.text: 如果你选择了艰难的道路,但最终未能成功,你其实也算赢了,因为你已经做了一件很难的事情。你可能与聪明的人一起工作,沿途学到了有价值的东西。
dcbe647503c2.original: If you do the hard path and it doesn't work, actually you still win because you've now done something hard. You've probably worked with smart people. You've learned something along the way that is valuable.

7b9a217e684c.text: 你应该把这个故事告诉所有人...我会永远严厉地反对那些不愿意冒险的人,你在这个案例中就没有冒险。
7b9a217e684c.original: You should tell everyone this story... I will always come down harshly on people who do not take risks, and you did not take a risk in this case.

64dda04fc091.text: 如果你有坚定的信念但却缺乏明确性,那么你其实并没有真正的确信。如果你说'也许我们应该解决五件事',那说明你就没有真正的确信。
64dda04fc091.original: If you have conviction and it's not clear, then you don't have conviction, quite frankly. If you're like, 'I think maybe we should, there are five things we should solve.' I'm like, 'Then you don't have conviction.'

1258aa098413.text: 对于重要的决策,你应该能够找到一个理由就可以支撑这个决定。我们常常依赖一系列不太充分的理由来证明决定。
1258aa098413.original: For important decisions, you should be able to identify one reason that on its own supports the decision. All too often we rely on a collection of weak reasons to justify decisions.

0ef717d3d9b8.text: 提出一个想法,即使它完全错误,也比什么都不提出要好得多,因为人们更可能对一个想法产生反应,而不是对一片空白。
0ef717d3d9b8.original: Putting out an idea, even if it's totally wrong, is a much better catalyst for getting to a good solution because people are much more likely to react to an idea than to nothing.

fbf8f2cecd69.text: 我们可能不一定对,但至少我们不会感到困惑。
fbf8f2cecd69.original: We may not be right, but at least we're not confused.

43eae4050317.text: 你必须百分之百地相信一件事,直到数据告诉你不对,然后你又百分之百地相信另一件事。这听起来很简单,但实际上做起来非常困难,因为有时人们不喜欢别人改变想法。
43eae4050317.original: You have to believe in things 100% until the data says no and then you believe in something else 100%. That sounds easy. It's very hard to do, to the extent that people get upset when you do it because, for some reason, people don't like when people change their minds.

9a26c3e1d9d0.text: 一个不好的问题例子就是,'我下一步职业生涯该怎么做?'这个问题过于模糊和笼统,会给别人带来很大的认知负担,你得到的回答也可能同样糟糕。输入垃圾,输出垃圾。
9a26c3e1d9d0.original: A good example... Well, let me start with a bad example of a question. A bad example of a question is, what should I do with my career next? It's just such a poorly formed question because it's really vague, it's not specific. It puts a lot of cognitive load on other people, and the output that you're going to get from it is probably going to be similarly bad. Garbage in, garbage out.

066cc38e4c7a.text: 我们的大脑习惯了缺乏资源的心智模式,而不是去创造替代方案或寻找不同的道路。关键是要问自己,'事情的反面会是什么样?'一旦我向自己提出这个问题,我的肩膀立刻放松下来,我感到更加放松,因为我意识到,'哦,我可以同时做这两件事,一切都会好起来的。'
066cc38e4c7a.original: Your brain is so accustomed to having a scarcity mindset as opposed to creating alternative options or seeing a different path.
