dba9c3fe68dd.text: 有一个非常有趣的时刻,用户全都告诉我们,没有问题。我们喜欢这个产品。他们每天都在使用它,一直在回来。它慢慢地在增长,但我们就是觉得,这不会让我们达到我们需要的地步。
dba9c3fe68dd.original: We had this really interesting moment where the users were all telling us, there's no problem. We love this product. They were using it every day, they were coming back. It was slowly growing and we were just like, this just isn't going to get us to where we need to be.

b7a7efa1aa06.text: 我可能最大的失败是,我是Hangouts的第一个产品经理。我手下有成千上万的人。我们拥有整个谷歌的力量。拉里亲自坐在我们旁边,说我们可以让Chrome做任何我们想做的事,但我们仍然无法打造出一款出色的即时通讯产品。
b7a7efa1aa06.original: My probably most spectacular failure was, I was the first PM on Hangouts. We had thousands of people working for me. We had entire power of Google. We had Larry literally sitting with us saying we can do anything we want Chrome to do and we still didn't manage to build a great messaging product.

d94c610c7563.text: 我们解决问题和构建产品的方式很大程度上是一种建造者的思维。就像我有一个计划,然后我操纵各种东西来匹配我的计划并实现它。这种方式确实能创造大量价值。但问题在于,它不可能创造的价值超过你投入的努力。相反,我关注的是那些可以自我成长、你只需要稍加引导或精心维护的事物 — 这种思维方式完全不同。
d94c610c7563.original: So much of the way that we tackle problems and build products is this builder mindset. It's like I have a plan. I then manipulate things to match my plan and make it happen. And this is a way you can create tons of value. Part of the problem though is it can't possibly create more value than the effort that you put into it. What I look for instead are things that can be gardened, things that can grow on their own and that you can direct or maybe give a little bit of extra energy to or curate over, and is a totally different mindset for it.

e3684b1be031.text: 任何像生态系统一样有某种网络效应的东西,都会有某种复合增长的循环。复合增长的循环并不罕见。就像寻找松露一样,你需要知道自己在找什么,找到一个如果运转的话会以加速的速度工作的动力学。
e3684b1be031.original: Anything that is shaped like an ecosystem that has some kind of network effect, and many things have network effects, have some kind of compounding loop. Compounding loops are not rare. They are, 'Look.' It's like truffle hunting. You have to know what you're looking for and find the dynamics of a thing that if it worked would work at an accelerating rate.

7e85fa83b169.text: 我们的创始人Tristan、Drew和Connor相信,那些与业务利益相关方密切合作进行数据分析的人,也应该是那些贡献创建生产就绪的干净数据资产的人,因为数据准备工作是任何分析工作的必要前提条件。所以dbt实际上是这样一种信念,如果你会SQL,我们想邀请你参与那些传统上由数据工程师负责的工作流程,但你需要经过考验才能获得这个权利。
7e85fa83b169.context: dbt 是一款开源的数据转换工具,允许分析师使用基于 SQL 的工作流来清理和准备数据以供分析使用。
7e85fa83b169.original: So our founders, Tristan, Drew and Connor, they had a belief that the people who do data analysis work, that really work closely with their business stakeholders should also be the ones to contribute to creating clean data assets in production because that data prep work is a necessary prerequisite for any analysis that you do. So dbt was really this belief that if you know SQL, we want to invite you to do these workflows that were traditionally held by data engineers but you had to earn that.
7e85fa83b169.originalContext: dbt is an open-source data transformation tool that allows analysts to write SQL-based workflows to clean and prepare data for analysis.

d434afae2563.text: 在深入任何平台领域的技术或设计执行之前,真正思考一下你正在构建的平台背后的原则,以及各方利益相关者的优先级。
d434afae2563.original: Before you even get into technical or design execution of any platform area, really think about the principles behind the platform you're building and the stack rank of constituents.

535fb4d37d0d.text: 一个市场型企业从来不是从市场型企业开始的,因为我们所认为的市场型企业是在规模上消除了双方找到对方的摩擦。但当你刚起步的时候,你是没有那种规模的。
535fb4d37d0d.original: A marketplace business never starts as a marketplace business, because what we think of as a marketplace business is something which at scale is removing the friction of the two sides finding each other. But when you start, you don't have that scale.

7a1604fd7550.text: 也许我们不应该谈论市场型创始人这个概念。每个创始人实际上都是市场型的。在他们成长之后,他们会选择是否要建立一个平台。
7a1604fd7550.original: Maybe we shouldn't talk about the concept of a marketplace founder. Really there's founders. Every founder is a marketplace founder. It'll be a choice they make after they grow as to whether they want to build a platform.

765693b97514.text: 平台终归是产品。你应该思考如何创造出一致的产品供给,使这家公司更有生产力。
765693b97514.original: Platforms are products, ultimately. You should be thinking about how do I create coherent offerings that make this company more productive?

493ca1a85a68.text: 要摧毁一家拥有网络效应的企业是非常困难的。电报机在被发明100多年后,直到2016年才被手动关闭,这就是因为它具有网络效应。
493ca1a85a68.original: It's really hard to kill a network effects business. The last telegram was sent in 2016, over 100 years after it was invented because of network effects. It had to be manually closed down.

7f17d7ab3bcc.text: 一家技术公司的技术架构比它所服务的对象和群体更多地决定了它的战略。如果你构建了正确的技术方案,并建立了一个可适应、灵活的平台,这在长远来看是非常有价值的。
7f17d7ab3bcc.original: The technical architecture determines strategy in a technology company even more than the what and who we're building for. If you build the right technical how and set yourself up to have a platform that can be adaptable, flexible, that is incredibly valuable over the long term.

6457b6a87902.text: 你需要同时做到这两点。如果你只做增量式的,你就会追随眼前最直接最陡峭的梯度。所以你需要对自己的目标有一个整体的认知,而这种认知来自于设定一个明确的北极星。
6457b6a87902.original: You need both. So if you only do incremental, you will follow the shortest, the steepest gradient in front of you... So you need coherence about where you're going and the way you get that is by creating a North Star for yourself.

42dad729b368.text: 对于每个个人用户来说,产品带来的效用会随着平台上用户数量的增加而增加...对于协作工具来说,关键不是抽象意义上的用户数量越多越好,而是团队内部、公司内部的用户数量越多越好。
42dad729b368.original: For every individual user, the utility that they derive from the product increases the more users there are on the platform... in the case of collaboration tools, it's not the more users in abstract terms. It's the more users within your team, the more users within your company.

c6645234d449.text: 这是一种生存方式。这是一种和我们行业里常见的'要么全力以赴,要么回家'的做法不同的方式。那种做法是一种方式。不过要知道,几乎没有人能靠那种方式成功。
c6645234d449.original: This is a way to be. It's an alternative to what you're often hearing in our industry, which is, 'Go big or go home. Raise a bunch of money and get huge, and unicorn status,' and the whole thing. That's a way. Just know though that basically almost nobody makes it that way.

e2d25881db88.text: 小规模不仅仅是过渡阶段,小规模本身就是一个很好的目标。
e2d25881db88.original: Small is not just a stepping stone, small is a great destination itself.

428a77fc98bc.text: 如果你要成为一家大型公司,每年收入需要达到10亿美元。这并不需要一夜之间实现,可以在20年内完成,这不是需要快速实现的目标,但这就是我的想法。
428a77fc98bc.original: If you are going to be that large company, you need to get to a billion in revenue per year. It doesn't have to be overnight, it can be over 20 years, it's not something that has to happen quickly, but that's how I think about it.

ce7231a253b9.text: 为什么不干脆就把它作为一个独立的C公司来运营?为什么不让它非常清楚地成为一个独立的实体?
ce7231a253b9.context: Mochary正在讨论在大公司内部为新产品创新团队创建独立的C公司,这里的'它'指的就是新产品/创新团队。
ce7231a253b9.original: Why don't you actually just create its own C corp? Why don't you make it so clear that this is its own entity?
ce7231a253b9.originalContext: Mochary is discussing creating separate C corporations for new product innovation teams within larger companies, where "it" refers to the new product/innovation team.

5e21a4ec4439.text: 自举适用于希望保持良好现金流的生活型企业。融资适用于那些希望实现每年10亿美元收入的公司。
5e21a4ec4439.original: Bootstrapping is for lifestyle businesses that want to cash flow. Funding is for companies trying to create a billion dollars in annual revenue.

687fc86e28a3.text: 我们希望打造一家看起来像是10个人完成的工作,但实际上有一千人在做。
687fc86e28a3.original: We wanted a company where a thousand people could work, but it'll look like 10 people did it.

f86389e26c3c.text: 如果我们早点融资,可能会有10亿美元的退出或者能一直保持下去。我们应该在生命周期更早的时候就融资。这其实是一个重大错误,因为我们陷入了效率的诱惑,这很不错,但如果融资,我们可能会进展得更快。
f86389e26c3c.original: We probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit or we could have kept going. And we should have taken money earlier in our life cycle. This was actually a big mistake because we got hooked on the efficiency and that was great, but we could have moved even quicker than we were.

72b2671b76cb.text: 聚焦不是关于我们在做什么,而是关于我们不在做什么。这些都是艰难的决定。
72b2671b76cb.original: Focus is not about what we are doing, it's about what we are not doing. These are the hard decisions.

014031011f86.text: 拒绝的能力将确保你正在为最重要的人建立一些惊人的东西,而不是为许多不同的人建立一些平庸或可以接受的东西。
014031011f86.original: The ability to say no is going to allow you to make sure you're building something that's going to be amazing for the people that matter most and not something that's going to be average or okay for a lot of different people.

8da6c2fc74ca.text: 战略的核心就是选择那些你要投资的领域以及不投资的领域。
8da6c2fc74ca.original: The core of strategy is really picking those areas and the areas you're not going invest in.

fdeeded4b80f.text: 策略应该痛苦。如果你没有进行痛苦的权衡取舍,你实际上并没有帮助人们优先考虑自己的时间。
fdeeded4b80f.original: Strategy should hurt. If you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you are not actually helping people prioritize their time.

a04c5420c879.text: 你不能有超过三个第一优先级。你可以有任意多的第二优先级和第三优先级,但你可以欺骗它...快速浏览一遍。
a04c5420c879.original: You can't have more than three P1s. You can have as many P2s as you want and P3s if you really think you should, but you can scam it... skim it, right? Go through it really quickly.

39d65d40553a.text: 每当有人想要进行战略讨论时,这意味着他们并没有真正理解自己的优先事项。优先事项总是从上到下排列的,其中有一件事比其他事更重要。
39d65d40553a.original: Whenever someone wants to have a strategy conversation, it assumes that they don't understand their priorities. The priorities is always a list from top to bottom where there's one thing that's more important than the others.

75522c8e7260.text: 任何公司都不需要超过三个公司目标,公司目标的目的是帮助人们了解成功最重要的事情是什么。
75522c8e7260.original: No company needs more than three company goals and the point of company goals is to help people know what the most important things are to success.

fd552fa59196.text: 如果我把你所有的资源都拿走,只留下五个,那你会选择建设哪一个?我采取这些专制的做法只是为了迫使你清晰地思考。
fd552fa59196.original: What if I took away all your resources and you only had five, which is the one you're going to build? I do all these Draconian things that just force clarity.

7945d522cc6c.text: 做一半做得很棒,比做一整个半吊子的东西强。
7945d522cc6c.original: A kick-ass half is better than a half-ass whole.

26720320ca4f.text: 如果我们真的做好这一件事,它将直接与做另一件事相冲突。这不仅仅是一个时序问题。在考虑优先级时,有时我们会认为,我们先做这个,然后再做那个,再做另一个。但在Facebook的情况下,有时就是'哦,如果我们做这个,我们就无法做那个'。
26720320ca4f.context: Facebook的新闻源迫使存在直接的权衡取舍,改善一个功能不可避免地会使另一个功能表现不佳,这与典型的创业公司优先考虑主要是关于时序的做法不同。
26720320ca4f.original: If we do this thing really well, it is going to directly trade-off against doing this other thing. It's not even a sequencing thing. When you think about prioritization, sometimes you think, we will do this, and then we'll do this, and then we'll do this. In Facebook's case, sometimes it's, 'Oh, if we do this, we just can't do this.'
26720320ca4f.originalContext: Facebook's news feed forces direct trade-offs where improving one feature inevitably makes another feature perform worse, unlike typical startup prioritization which is mainly about timing.

d1f78b167c1e.text: 好的战略的目标不是取悦所有人。好的战略的目标是决定我们如何利用有限的能力或有限的功能来解决我们关心的问题。
d1f78b167c1e.original: The goal of good strategy is not to appease everyone. The goal of good strategy is to dictate how we invest the limited capacities we have or the limited capabilities we have into the problems we care about.

4e60d332488e.text: 很多时候,好的战略是非常枯燥乏味的。很难去讨论它。例如,在工程方面,一个很好但非常枯燥的常见策略就是,我们只使用我们今天拥有的工具。
4e60d332488e.original: Often good strategy is so boring. It's hard to talk about. For example, on the engineering side of thing, a common strategy that's really good but very boring is we only use the tools we have today.

feb888ceb1c5.text: 选择哪些方面你可以做得不太好,找出你需要做出的权衡取舍,并确保你的权衡取舍与客户的需求相一致。
feb888ceb1c5.original: Choose what to suck at and figure out the trade-offs that you need to make and make sure that your trade-offs map the trade-offs of the customer.

794071c2df03.text: 大多数失败的产品都是因为它们做出了客户不赞同的权衡取舍。
794071c2df03.original: Most products that fail is because they made a trade-off that the customer didn't agree with.

fd965f74153e.text: 每次说'是'时,你都有把一个初露端倪的好策略变成一个糟糕的策略的风险。专注是力量和战略的根本源泉。
fd965f74153e.original: Each time you say yes, you risk turning a nascent good strategy into a bad strategy. Focus is the fundamental source of power and strategy.

deca005e2d4b.text: 说到底,战略就是要问如何才能取胜,如何才能更接近目标,也就是愿景。但同时也要考虑我们现在的位置以及我们现在能够执行的情况。
deca005e2d4b.original: Really, strategy always comes down to asking the questions about how can we win, how can we get further to the goal, which is the vision. But it's also keeping into context of where we are now and what we're able to execute on now.

c0eebc258678.text: 我是大赌注的支持者,高风险高回报。我没有那么兴奋于增量性的事情。但是,我对大赌注感到兴奋。如果你下大赌注,你将会很多地失败。
c0eebc258678.original: I'm a big believer in big bets, high risk, high reward. I don't get as excited about incremental things. But, I get excited about big bets. And if you make big bets, you're going to get a lot of it wrong.

f8dd835d8df8.text: 你要么决定付出代价,要么离开。不要半吊子。你看到这些公司说,我们做AI,他们只是撒了一点点糟糕的AI,他们也有同样的文化。这是行不通的。
f8dd835d8df8.original: You either decide to pay the price or get out. Don't half-ass it. You see all these companies saying, we do AI and they've just sprinkle a little bit of crappy AI and they've got the same cultures. It won't work.

cd96f839d7c0.text: 大多数时候,CEO们想要选择权。他们想要对冲自己的赌注,但在这些战略转折点上,你真正想要做的是全力以赴地去做一件事。
cd96f839d7c0.original: Most of the time CEOs want options. They want to hedge their bets, but what you really want to do in these strategic inflection points is go all in one thing.

0414f5cccf1f.text: 专注是创造财富的关键,分散投资是保护财富的方式。但你是一家初创公司。你不是在试图保护任何东西。你是在试图建立一些东西。这需要集中的赌注,而不是对冲。
0414f5cccf1f.original: Concentration is what builds wealth, diversification is what preserves wealth. And you're a startup. You're not trying to preserve anything. You're trying to build something. It requires concentrated bets, not hedging.

2b1294a5e160.text: 不采取大胆的风险,不做出大胆的举措,这本身就是一种风险。很多时候,人们想要惯性,人们想要只有增量的价值。但如果你想要做出飞跃,你很多时候需要放弃过去成功的事物。
2b1294a5e160.original: Not taking bold risks, not making bold moves, it's a risk for itself. Many times people want the inertia, people want just the incremental value. But if you want to do leaps many times you need to let go of things that were successful for you in the past.

e2e4a5c59bd7.text: 我真的很希望有更多人会说:'不管了,我要做一些可能会失败的事情。这很重要,值得去做,而且我会把它做好。'
e2e4a5c59bd7.original: I would really love it if more people were like, 'Screw it. I'm going to do something that's probably going to fail. It's important and it's worth doing and I'm going to do it well.'

fb10e0b2dbad.text: 你不想在第一天就去健身房尝试举起300磅的重物。所以当有人来找我,他们是第一次创业,说'我要打造下一个伟大的AI公司',我认为这就相当于那个情况。
fb10e0b2dbad.original: You don't want to walk into the gym on day one and try and deadlift 300 pounds. So when someone comes to me and they're a first time entrepreneur and they say, 'I'm going to make the next great AI company,' I think that is the equivalent.

0024a7e27c19.text: 如果一个软件项目可以在2到3周内完成,那真的意味着你所构建的东西的真正复杂性和差异化有多低吗?除非你认为自己比其他人聪明得多。但我认为那可能只是自负。
0024a7e27c19.original: If a software project could get built in two to three weeks, what does that really mean about the true complexity and differentiation of what you built? It's probably not very high, unless you believe you are way smarter than everyone else. But I think that's hubris.

d4ffd44373a4.text: 在一个高杠杆作用的角色中,你应该停止做单纯有正收益率的工作,而应该开始关注能够最小化机会成本的工作。
d4ffd44373a4.original: In a high leverage role, you should stop doing work that simply provides a positive return on investment, ROI. And you should start focusing on work that minimizes opportunity cost.

a94b30837e59.text: 当我们重塑自己的思维模式,从'这是一个好的时间利用方式吗?'转变为'这是最佳时间利用方式吗?'时,这就是一种微妙而深刻的思维转变。
a94b30837e59.original: When we reprogram ourselves to think in terms of opportunity cost, we are no longer thinking, 'Oh, is this a good use of my time?' Instead, you are thinking, 'Is this the best use of my time?' And it's a subtle but profound shift in our thinking.

0dd495ebc95b.text: 如果你是这家公司的CEO,你会全额资助你自己的团队吗?说实话,大多数人在第一时间都无法答出这个问题。
0dd495ebc95b.original: If you were the CEO of this company, would you fully fund your own team? Frankly, most of the people I ask that question to don't know the answer right away.

672285831361.text: 低影响力的工作会引发更多低影响力的工作。你做越多低影响力的工作,就越难做出高影响力的工作,你也越有可能继续做低影响力的工作。
672285831361.original: Low-impact work begets low-impact work. The more low-impact work you do, the harder it is to do high-impact work, the more likely you are to do low-impact work.

cfc0efc8623a.text: 我们仍然有太多团队在围绕工作做工作,支持工作,而不是专注于真正有影响力的机会。
cfc0efc8623a.original: We still have too many teams doing work around the work and supporting work, rather than focusing on opportunities with real impact.

b218a2c5a68a.text: 你可以遵循所有最佳实践,但如果你的公司破产了,他们也不会因为你的OKR指标达到0.6或0.7就继续给你发工资两年。
b218a2c5a68a.original: You can follow all the best practices, but if your company goes out of business, they're not going to keep writing your paycheck for two years because all of your OKRs were a 0.6 or a 0.7.

38ea660c6a11.text: 如果你今天不会开始这个项目,那意味着你投入其中的一切都是在浪费。
38ea660c6a11.original: If you wouldn't start this today, then that means that everything that you're putting into this going forward is the actual waste.

082bd1dd9f85.text: 在做某件事的时候,不仅有直接的机会成本,还有无法集中精力去做其他可能更好的事情的成本。
082bd1dd9f85.original: When you're doing something, there's not just the cost of doing something that's not worthwhile that's direct, but there's also the cost of not being able to devote your attention to other opportunities that might be available to you.

4fd171c35077.text: 基本上,策略本身没有商业价值。它只是一份包含几个词语的文档。我认为,策略只有在产生商业影响和成果时才能积累价值。
4fd171c35077.original: Basically strategy has no business value. It's basically a document with a few words. And I think it starts accumulating value as you generate business impact and results.

c7e2f2fa7b91.text: 我们每天都可以更快地交付垃圾。我们需要战略和明智的决策来确定应该交付什么。

b9ad1d6a2ace.original: If you are the leader in some core product, our takeaway here is you should continue to out invest everyone else in that core and then invest the profits that come out of that core into the next venture. Invest profits and not people, or venture capital, which is maybe net present value of profits or something to that effect.

8a2ee56ef9dd.text: 当时的问题是,我们从核心产品的投资中抽调人员去做其他事情。我们转移了人员。陷阱在于,这使你的核心产品易受到破坏,因为其他人可以在那个核心上投资得更多。
8a2ee56ef9dd.original: The issue for us at the time was that we took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things. We moved people, right? And so the trap there is that you leave yourself ripe for disruption in your core because someone else can out invest you in that core.

980a9d9f72f1.text: 没有太多人需要第六好的客户数据平台或第八好的功能标记或第十好的消息定位工具。它最终会为你贡献5到10%的收入,不会真正加速你的增长率,但会占用工程师远离核心产品。
980a9d9f72f1.context: 客户数据平台(CDP)是一种软件,它从多个来源收集和统一客户数据,用于营销和分析。
980a9d9f72f1.original: There's not that many people that need the sixth best CDP or the eighth best feature flagging or the 10th best message targeting tool. And it ends up being, in aggregate will contribute five to 10% to your revenue, won't seriously accelerate your growth rate, and then takes engineers away from the core product.
980a9d9f72f1.originalContext: CDP stands for Customer Data Platform, a software that collects and unifies customer data from multiple sources for marketing and analytics purposes.

7a3e54e62874.text: 这成为了产品的战略指南。我们不断收到来自销售、客户成功等部门的功能请求。但我们之前无法确定该接受哪些请求、哪些不该接受。现在这个标准已经很清晰了。
7a3e54e62874.original: It becomes the strategic north star for the product. We are constantly getting feature requests through sales, through customer success. And we had sort of no way, bar to decide well what do we take on, what don't we take on? And this clearly has become our bar.

cf5f0c4862fe.text: 我们收到了很多关于意见记录的功能请求。但我们不会去做这些。
cf5f0c4862fe.original: We get a lot of requests for features and a lot of them are basically about opinions, some way to record opinions. We're not going to do those.

d1a4e4289917.text: 如果条件相同,我们会选择能够保持Substack的原则性的那个。我们可以举更多这样的例子,但从优先级和策略的角度来看,Substack是一家非常有原则的公司。
d1a4e4289917.context: 「保持这个原则」指的是Substack的核心原则,即作者和读者应该能够控制自己的内容和体验,而不应受算法推荐的约束。
d1a4e4289917.original: All things equal, do the one that holds constant this principle of control. We could talk about a few other examples like this, but I think from a prioritization standpoint and from a strategic standpoint, Substack is a pretty principled company.
d1a4e4289917.originalContext: "This principle of control" refers to Substack's core principle that writers and readers should have control over their content and experience, rather than being subject to algorithmic recommendations.

de90ffe419a7.text: 这真的会帮助我们更快地实现通用人工智能吗?有很多诱人的用户参与指标摆在眼前,但我们首先要从这个角度去审视这些问题。也许这些指标确实能够帮助我们更快实现通用人工智能,但我们必须先从这个视角去考虑。
de90ffe419a7.original: Is this actually going to help us get to AGI? So there's a huge focus on there's this potential shiny reward right in front of us, which is optimize user engagement, or whatever it is. And is that really the thing? Maybe the answer is yes. Maybe that is what is going to help us get to AGI sooner, but looking at it through that lens I think is always the first step of deciding any of these problems.

4acc1df58efd.text: 我在这里任职期间做的最有影响力的事情之一,就是明确我们的整体产品策略,其中一个核心部分是我们瞄准的具体市场是什么?那个市场的细分是什么?每个细分中的目标用户群是谁？
4acc1df58efd.original: One of the most impactful things we did pretty early on in my tenure here was to hone in on our overall product strategy, but a core piece of that being what's the actual market we're going after? What are the segments of that market? Who are the personas within the segments of that market?

8db65e36e91d.text: 一个指标一旦成为目标,它就不再是一个有用的指标了。最有价值的事情与可完全量化的事情之间的重合度可能只有20%,剩下80%的价值空间是无法通过只关注可量化指标的人来解决的。
8db65e36e91d.original: The moment a metric becomes a goal it's no longer a useful metric. The overlap of most valuable things you can do with a product, and for things that happen to be fully quantifiable, it's like maybe 20% which leaves 80% of a value space unaddressable by the people who will only look at quantifiable things.

44960391cc51.text: 我认为解决少数人的问题做得非常好,比尝试解决大量人的问题却做得不太好要好得多。
44960391cc51.original: I think it's better to solve a small number of people's problem really well than trying to solve a large number of people's problem not very well at all.

3a3686ca9f5d.text: 对于一家初创公司来说,最糟糕的做法就是试图成为所有人的什么都有,因为你并没有足够的资源和时间来做到这一点。
3a3686ca9f5d.original: When you are an early stage company, the worst thing you can do is try to be everything to everyone because you don't have enough runway. You just don't have enough of anything to do that successfully.

338ce57f8a71.text: 我认为建立这些市场的最大难题在于,野心往往如同太阳般炽热,你在追求这个广阔的市场,就好像试图去温暖整个海洋。最出色的有抱负的创始人会将这份野心聚焦于一个小市场,就像是聚焦于一个小水桶。
338ce57f8a71.original: And the hardest thing I think about building these marketplaces is that the ambition can often feel like this sun, like the heat of the sun that's trying to warm everything up, and you're going after this big market, warming the ocean. And I think that, really, what the the best, ambitious founders do is they focus that ambition like a laser beam on a small market, the thimble.

c01fdaca5506.text: 要达到真正的统治地位,拥有 winner take most 格局,唯一的路径就是要引导你的市场发生转折,这才是可扩展的方式。要最大化引导市场转折的机会,你必须专注于一个非常受限的机会,这就是第一层级。
c01fdaca5506.context: Sarah Tavel 提出了一个市场等级模型,分为三个层级:第一层级(专注于受限市场)、第二层级(引导市场转折)、第三层级(主导市场)。
c01fdaca5506.original: The only way to get to that place, to get to that moment of real dominance where you have this winner take most dynamic is that you have to tip your market, and that's the only scalable way to do that, and that's what level two is. And so, how do you maximize your chance of tipping a market? You have to focus on a really constrained opportunity, and that is level one.
c01fdaca5506.originalContext: Sarah Tavel's marketplace hierarchy has three levels: Level 1 (focus on constrained market), Level 2 (tip the market), Level 3 (dominate market).

bfeec5f28a09.text: 我们不会开始某件事情,除非我们能从一开始就看到最终结果。我们不会拿一个大概念然后说,'这件事需要多少时间?'相反,我们会先问自己,在业务愿意投入的时间内,我们能做出什么样的东西?
bfeec5f28a09.original: We are not going to start something unless we can see the end from the beginning. We're not going to take a big concept and then say, 'What's the estimate for this thing?' We're going to go the other way around and we're going to say, what is the maximum amount of time we're willing to go before we actually finish something? How do we come up with a idea that's going to work in the amount of time that the business is interested in spending?

a377866c2d34.text: 你不可能把10磅的垃圾塞进一个5磅的袋子里。所以,这是一个非常理想化的说法,我们不能拿任何项目,无论有多大,然后交给团队说,'在6周内通过砍掉一些内容就能做出有意义的东西。'
a377866c2d34.original: You can't put 10 pounds of crap in a five pound bag. So, it's a high academic statement and we can't just take any project, no matter how giant it is, and then throw it at a team and say, 'Figure it out and ship something meaningful in six weeks by cutting away scope.'

c08581c7b8e7.text: 如果我们把6周作为最长的时间,这就会迫使我们问自己一些非常好的问题,比如我们真的认为自己能在这个时间内完成什么?因为如果你说,'在6个月内我们会发布这个东西',你根本无法预见到在整个6个月的工作期间会遇到什么问题。
c08581c7b8e7.original: If we think of six weeks as a maximum, that's going to force us to ask some really good questions to ourselves about what piece of this do we really think we can land? Because if you try to say, in six months, we're going to ship this thing, you can't get your arms around all of the problems that have to get solved for an entire six-month chunk of work to actually happen.

9d58db8db12e.text: 给自己一个固定的时间期限去采取一些决定性的行动,看看效果如何。我们能在6周内全力以赴地完成目前最重要的一件事吗?
9d58db8db12e.original: Give yourself a fixed period of time to take some decisive action and see if it feels better. Can we take six weeks to try to make it work? Can we just spend all of our time 100% on the one and only one thing that matters right now?

345151a30cc2.text: 不要承担那些需要6个月或1年才能完成的项目,因为你根本无法控制外部环境。
345151a30cc2.original: Don't take on projects that are going to be six months, a year, because you just generally don't have control over the macro.

a5d7b11888ab.text: 当你考虑投资回报时,我们可以让几个工程师花几个小时实现它。这就是真正发生的事情,有个人在Bing里看到这个待办事项一直在,说,'天哪,我们花了太多时间讨论这个了,我直接实现它就好了。'
a5d7b11888ab.original: When you think about return on investment, we could get the data by having some engineers spend a couple of hours implementing it. And that's exactly what happened. Somebody at Bing who kept seeing this in the backlog and said, 'My God, we're spending too much time discussing it. I could just implement it.'

0a450eea23c1.text: 这最终就变成了囚徒困境。不要自欺地认为你可以不参与这个游戏。你是逃不掉这个游戏的。
0a450eea23c1.original: It ends up being a prisoner's dilemma. Don't trick yourself into thinking that you can't play the game. There is no opting out of the game.

eaaeabddc76a.text: 如果你是一家后期公司,你要下多个赌注。但对于初创公司来说,这是完全不同的游戏。你必须选择一个并全力以赴。
eaaeabddc76a.original: If you're a late-stage company, you place multiple bets. For startups, it's a totally different ballgame. You have to choose one and go all in.

3593a8450cf0.text: 并不是每件好事都会由你发明出来。说到底,你只是在剥夺你的用户群拥有更好产品的机会。
3593a8450cf0.original: Not every great thing is going to be invented by you. At the end of the day, you're just robbing your user base of the opportunity to have a better product.

eda695a683ba.text: 你会遇到这样的时候,感觉就是每个系统都有递减的边际收益,觉得你可以让50个人参与这个项目,但也不会大幅推动针对性指标。这就是你需要回到第一性原理,尝试这些新事物的时候了。
eda695a683ba.original: You get to these points of just diminishing marginal return in every system where it feels like you could put 50 people on this project, it's just not going to dramatically move the needle. That's where you need to go more first principled and try these new things more.

504f697fab1e.text: 领先于他们不是优化问题,而是重塑解决方案。我感觉在之前的角色中,我可能只有5%的时间在创新增长,而现在我有95%的时间都在创新增长,只有5%在优化上。
504f697fab1e.context: "他们"指的是那些专注于优化而不是创新的增长领域竞争对手。
504f697fab1e.original: To be ahead of them is not optimization of the problem, it's reinvention of the solution. I just feel like I usually spend maybe 5% innovating on growth in my previous roles, right now, I'm spending 95% innovating on growth, and only 5% on optimization.
504f697fab1e.originalContext: "Them" refers to competitors in the growth field who focus on optimization rather than innovation.

51ebb79cc31b.text: 我们将LLM成本归类为免费增值和赠品营销成本,而不是需要降低以提高利润率的成本。这是我们需要投入更多的增长秘诀的一部分。
51ebb79cc31b.context: Elena Verna正在讨论她公司如何将LLM(大型语言模型)AI成本归类为营销投资,而不是运营开支。
51ebb79cc31b.original: We track them over our LLM costs on freemium and giveaways as our marketing costs, and it doesn't go into our something we need to reduce to make our margins better. It goes into, this is something that we need to spend more in because this is part of our growth secret sauce.
51ebb79cc31b.originalContext: Elena Verna is discussing how her company categorizes LLM (Large Language Model) AI costs for their freemium product as marketing investment rather than operational expense.

d29f801bec81.text: 你不会通过出色地完成10件事来取胜。你会通过真正出色地完成一件事来取胜,其他九件事也许会失败。我只需要在那个最重要的课程上获得A+。其他所有课程我都可以得到F。
d29f801bec81.original: You don't win by doing 10 things well. You win by doing one thing really well and maybe you fail nine things. I just need to get an A+ on the one class that matters. And then I can get an F in all the other classes.

a0cda80c9e62.text: 初创公司的优势在于资金紧张,所以你需要创造稀缺性。公司往往会过度投资。
a0cda80c9e62.original: Startups have the benefit of starving, and so you need to create scarcity. The company has a tendency to over-invest.

e892705ab80a.text: 如果你减少投放面积,那么在同样的力量作用下,你就能施加更大的压力。压力大小等于力量除以面积,这是物理的基本公式,但同样适用于沟通。如果你减少投放面积,不试图用各种方式来吸引所有人,而是针对性地对准你想要交流的对象,并且将信息浓缩到关键要点,那么你就能用相同的努力、开支或时间产生更大的影响,施加更大的压力。
e892705ab80a.original: If you decrease the surface area than with the same amount of force you can apply more pressure. So the amount of pressure is the force divided by the surface area, this is a basic equation for physics, but it's also true of communications, which is if you decrease the surface area and don't try to appeal to everybody with everything. And you're targeting exactly whom you're talking to and you are sharpening your message to a point, to get them in the bullseye of the cultural erogenous zone. Then you're able to with the same amount of effort or expense or time, you're able to make more of an impact, you're able to apply more pressure.

0aab658b3716.text: 我认为,如果你找到一个你坚信能改变世界的重大想法,并且对其他一切说'不',那才是建造一些真正有意义的东西的唯一方式。
0aab658b3716.original: I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.

83c9f2ee3575.text: 实际上你可以设计一个市场。通过这样做,你为人们创造了一种之前不存在的全新价值区隔。
83c9f2ee3575.original: You can actually design a market. And in so doing, you create a new distinction in value for people that didn't exist before.

5c2d6220d486.text: 设计出这个领域并使之在大规模上获得普及的公司...能够让世界上很大一部分人认同他们对问题的定义,这样也就导致了他们对解决方案的定义。任何规模上能做到这一点的公司,都将胜出。
5c2d6220d486.original: The company that designs the space and gets it to tip at scale... gets a meaningful percentage of the world to agree with their definition of a problem set, which then leads to their definition of a solution set. The company that does that at any kind of scale, wins.

bbd531e58614.text: 市场定义了产品,市场定义了品牌,市场定义了公司。
bbd531e58614.original: The category makes the product, the category makes the brand, the category makes the company.

c72cdd46ea8c.text: 创业公司之所以会赢,是因为它提出了一种截然不同的未来愿景。这会扰乱行业现有格局,并推动人们走向这种全新的未来。
c72cdd46ea8c.original: The way startups win is because it proposes a radically different future. Disorients the incumbent and chaotically moves people to that different future.

1be640aec085.text: 你想要强迫选择,而非对比。如果大家都在卖苹果,我无法成为10倍更好的苹果。我要成为全世界第一个香蕉。
1be640aec085.original: You want to force a choice and not a comparison. If everybody's selling apples, I can't be a 10 times better Apple. I want to be the world's first banana.

3846609d50c5.text: 产品市场契合度...仔细听听这些词:产品、市场、契合度...你要做的是为你的产品设计一个市场领域,而不是将产品塞入现有的市场领域。
3846609d50c5.original: Product market fit... Listen to the words, product, market, fit... What you want is you want to design a market category for your product, not fit your product into a market category.

18bb147e99a7.text: 市场设计者与现状竞争...现状就是敌人,也就是如今的样子。
18bb147e99a7.original: Category designers compete against the status quo... The enemy is the status quo. That is to say the way it is now.

bc65896095f6.text: 几乎每一家你想合作的初创公司,都是从反向定位开始的,因为你要记住,产品市场契合度的本质是一种替代。
bc65896095f6.context: 反向定位是一种战略力量,新的商业模式优于现有模式,但由于现有约束,行业巨头无法轻易复制。
bc65896095f6.original: Almost every startup that you want to deal with starts with counter positioning because remember what product market fit is primarily is a substitution.
bc65896095f6.originalContext: Counter positioning is a strategic power where a new business model is superior but unattractive for incumbents to copy due to their existing constraints.

671039be019c.text: 直到有竞争对手出现，你才算是真正创造了一个新品类。在整个创建新品类的过程中,我学到,当新公司进入并声称自己属于同一品类,这实际上是在验证一个新品类的存在。
671039be019c.original: You're not building a category until there is competition. It's not officially actually a category until there's more companies that do that. And that was a big learning for me in this whole process of category creation, is that it's actually okay when new companies come in that say they're that category because it's just validating the fact that there is a new category.

c377d75e18a5.text: 在创建新品类时,你需要确保分析师和目录网站等渠道对这一品类进行了验证。同时,你需要通过行业领导地位来阐述这个品类的独特价值主张和解决的痛点,并制作大量相关内容,因为你需要教育买家这个品类值得他们预算投入。
c377d75e18a5.original: When you're building a category, you need to make sure that there is a category that's validated by analysts and directory sites and things like that. But also, you want to have a lot of traction in terms of thought leadership like why is this the category? What are the unique value propositions of this particular thing? What are the pain points it solves? And then of course, getting a lot of content around because when you're generating a new category, you're also needing to educate buyers that there is a category that they can now budget for and why they should allocate budget for that.

b4b29addafbe.text: 一旦你成为某个市场的主导player,一个不错的策略就是扩大品类的边界,这样你就可以继续增长。我们看到的大多数成功的品类创建案例都是在公司收入达到2-4亿美元、主导自己领域时,才决定去扩大品类边界。
b4b29addafbe.original: Once you're the dominant player in that market, a cool move to do is to actually extend the boundaries of the category so that you can continue to grow. And most of the category creation examples we see are companies that when they were 200, 300, 400 million revenue dominating their space, then decided to move the goalposts.

4e001d3b2d9c.text: 有趣的是,即使是成功的品类创建者,在开始的时候也并非如此。他们起初只是在某个既有品类中找到了一个细分领域进行切入。
4e001d3b2d9c.original: Category creation is interesting. Like most companies, if you look at their arc, even the category creators that are successful, they did not start out as category creators. So they started out as a niche play in an existing category.

76856ae1b162.text: 在品类创建过程中,PR也非常重要。你需要把这个品类和定位推广到高层,测试它是否有意义并得到响应。
76856ae1b162.original: One thing that's really important in category creation as well is actually PR. You need to get this category and positioning out there at a high level in order to test it out and see if it makes sense and if it's resonating.

f6e44d93dc55.text: 你需要与分类网站建立关系,共同定义你的品类。以可视化协作为例,我们起初在G2 Crowd上没有被归类,需要与他们会面解释这个品类的特点和与其他品类的差异,让他们了解如何将其与其他品类区分开。
f6e44d93dc55.original: You need to build relationships with them. You need to work with them to create your category as well. So with the visual collaboration, for example, we weren't ranking, we weren't categorized in visual collaboration on G2 Crowd, and we had to meet with them and explain what it was and talk to them about the differentiation of this category versus other categories in terms of features and all of that stuff so that they could understand how they would differentiate this category from another category.

968ee2919839.text: 很多公司想要定位自己为品类创造者,但我实在不喜欢。这行不通,也不太符合事实。
968ee2919839.original: A lot of companies want to position themselves as category creators, and I actually hate that. It doesn't work. It doesn't land with press, and most of the time it's not totally true.

821211db9dfd.text: 你要有一个足够大的目标细分市场,但又足够小到能主导,且与你的核心优势相吻合。这就是成功的公式。
821211db9dfd.original: You want to have a target segment that is big enough to matter, small enough to lead and a good fit with your crown jewels. That's the formula.

7c47fcd57643.text: 最简单的占领一个大市场的方法,就是定义一个被市场领导者忽视的细分市场。

8922a7a601d3.text: 当你处于鸿沟期时,你的倾向会是'我只需要更多客户。我应该接受任何能找到的客户',因为我们需要收入。这就像用火柴在一根木头上来回划,是点不着的。那么,你如何点燃一堆火呢?你需要先点上一些碎纸屑,然后把火苗集中在一处,直到火势起来。

8922a7a601d3.originalContext: "The chasm" refers to Geoffrey Moore's framework describing the difficult transition period between early adopters and mainstream customers in technology adoption.

e85d2819f7b5.text: 这就是临近细分市场如此重要的原因。如果你点燃了火焰,但木头在另一个房间,这是行不通的。

2bafe46c8323.text: 如果你是一个行业的领导者,比如Oracle和数据库,你已经做了40年了。你仍然是领导者,因为生态系统围绕着你组织起来了。但当你还小的时候,让生态系统围绕着你组织起来的唯一办法,就是进攻一个你在那个小圈子里是大鱼的细分市场。

4770dfea902a.text: 我们在特定细分市场上有多强的契合度?在公司的发展历程中,第一年我们只关注'我们能否在早期创业公司细分市场上达到契合'。在前两年,我们都集中在'我们能否在早期创业公司细分市场上达到契合'。

c376381ec3dc.text: 我们的定位是中小企业。这不是一个市场进入策略,也不是'我们首先要征服中小企业市场',不是什么桶中策,也不是Geoffrey Moore的理论。

c376381ec3dc.originalContext: "Bowling Pin" refers to Geoffrey Moore's go-to-market strategy of targeting one market segment first, then expanding to adjacent segments sequentially.

b866122e7499.text: 你要建立一些即使是最通用的模型也无法替代你的东西。通常情况下,你建立的东西对某些特定用户来说非常出色,实际上现在的护城河在于你是否聆听他们的意见,是否能快速迭代。

cd8e24009b51.text: 人们正在为此开发仪表板,这是非常了不起的。我认为,在这方面做得很好的产品,它们对自身应用程序的表现有非常清晰的认知,这就是他们的护城河。

bce13ae5545c.text: 你的品牌就是人们如何认知你,而制定品牌策略就是要确定你想成为什么样的人,你希望别人如何看待你,以及你将采取什么措施来塑造这种印象。

cac7824a43fd.text: 我非常相信,在消费者业务中,最重要的两件事是产品和品牌,并且是按此顺序。我不需要向你们这个群体推销这个理念,因为你们很清楚产品是绝对关键的。但是将品牌视为次要因素,这无疑是消费科技企业巨大的机会丧失。

2ecc96fd3900.text: 优秀的品牌会在客户心中产生超越典型交易或实用性的联想,成为人们身份的一部分。

f274746869f6.text: 你要在所有客户触点上保持一致。因此,品牌不仅仅是一个酷炫的标志、有趣的广告和优美的形象,更是客户或用户对你的产品和企业的整体印象。

92739496afec.text: 总会有一些特点,比如出乎意料。我们的交流方式有些幽默。我们不过于自重,这会使接收到信息的人产生某种感受。再次重申,这都是关于如何让人产生感受。

4d3b4a52b9b1.text: 我认为,你的品牌就是你的承诺,而你的产品体验就是对这一承诺的兑现。这两者必须保持一致,否则就会有期望和实际结果不符,从而让客户大失所望。
4d3b4a52b9b1.original: I like to think of your brand is the promise that you're making and your product experience is your delivery of that promise. And those two things have to be in lockstep with each other, or you're going to have mismatched expectations and some really disappointed customers.

7ef80c8553ad.text: 如果你是唯一一个在做这件事的人,而没有其他人在做,其实这是一个问题。你并不希望成为唯一一家,而是希望在一个有竞争的市场中。

90eb8857269d.text: 产品引领式销售假设用户会从最初的个人使用案例,逐步升级到企业级解决方案,以满足企业级需求。

b4466d854d7f.originalContext: "Lenny" refers to Lenny Rachitsky, the interviewer. "Playing to play" means competing without a clear strategy to win distinctively.

9899ffc767a8.text: 要想实施一个你认为会奏效的策略,你必须有一个合理的理由,这个理由源自于某种力量或优势。
9899ffc767a8.original: To undertake a strategy that you think will work, you've got to have a reason that it makes sense and that reason is derived from some source of power, some source of advantage.

86e0288274da.text: 你如何发现自己的力量?从不对称性开始。我公司与其他公司有哪些不同?我们掌握了别人不知道的信息?我们拥有别人没有的东西?
86e0288274da.original: How do you figure out your power? Start with asymmetries. In what way is my company different than other companies? What do we know that other people don't know? What do we possess that other people don't possess?

f7eb2c0bf91c.text: 如果两个战斗者实力均等,胜负是五五开。要制定策略,你需要利用某种不对称。也许你反应稍快,或者对方稍差劲。总之,必须有某些不同。
f7eb2c0bf91c.original: If two fighters are equally balanced, it's 50/50. For a strategy you need to exploit an asymmetry of some kind. You hear a little faster. Or they're a little... Something has to be different.

c2771014f14b.text: 商业世界只谈论战术。定位博弈就是,你在地图上占据了哪块领土?你扮演什么角色?你赢得了多少商家的信任?这就是定位博弈。
c2771014f14b.original: The business world only talks about tactics. The positional game is like, what is the territory on the map that you are taking? What role do you play? How much trust do you have of merchants? This is the positional game.

2647dc072110.text: 最理想的情况是,你永远不需要使用的武器才是最强大的。获胜的最佳方式,就是避免被迫进行正面竞争。
2647dc072110.original: The ultimate is, it's like the ultimate weapon is the one you never use. The ultimate way to compete to win is to never actually be forced to compete.

6a120cda5fcc.text: LLM就像是魔法般的胶带。它们主要是由整个社会的直观智慧汇聚而成,在人类和普通计算之间运作,使成本结构大大降低。
6a120cda5fcc.original: LLMs are magical duct tape. They're formed principally by the distilled intuition of all of society into a thing that operates between, a cost structure between human and plain old computing.

1a4b4939d9a0.text: 过去只有富人或大公司才能买得起的东西,现在变得便宜得多,所以每个人都可以使用。
1a4b4939d9a0.original: There are these things that were historically really expensive that only rich people or big companies could buy... becoming orders of magnitude cheaper so that everyone can use them.

afc77dd49e76.text: 随着成本的下降,人们将制造更多软件来改善生活和工作,并创办更多初创公司。
afc77dd49e76.original: As the costs go down, people will just make a lot more software to improve their lives and to improve their work and start more startups.

2d2a271af6b0.text: 新兴的公司类型也会发生变化。它们不仅规模更小,而且从根本上说,它们是由擅长技术和产品的创始人创办的,而不是擅长推销和炒作的。因为员工更少意味着需要的资本更少,所以不需要融资。
2d2a271af6b0.original: The types of companies are going to change too. It won't just be that they're smaller, we're going to see fundamentally different companies emerging. If you think about it, fewer employees means less capital. Less capital means you don't need a raise. So instead of companies started by founders who are great at pitching and great at hyping, you'll get founders who are really great at technology and product.

cc908a6f547b.text: 专业人士现在可以访问建立他们最终想要的工具。以前,每个公司只需要10%的功能,但现在已经完全改变了。现在他们可以自己构建定制解决方案。
cc908a6f547b.context: 以前,垂直行业的软件公司之所以成功是因为它们提供了全面的功能集,即使个别客户通常只使用约10%的可用功能,但缺乏构建定制解决方案的技术资源。
cc908a6f547b.original: The domain specialists now have access to build the tools that they ultimately wanted. Each individual company only wanted 10% of the features, but that has now changed entirely. Now they can.
cc908a6f547b.originalContext: Previously, vertical software companies succeeded because they offered comprehensive feature sets, even though individual customers typically only used about 10% of available features, but lacked technical resources to build custom solutions.

089242bd3602.text: 我喜欢那些具有暗示性或唤起情感的名称,当我告诉你这家公司是做什么的时候,你会觉得很有道理。但是这个名称并不完全告诉你这家公司做什么。
089242bd3602.original: I like to think of those kinds of names that are suggestive or evocative, where when I tell you what the company does, you're like, oh, that makes sense. But it's not that what the name is tells you exactly what the company does.

98514f835e0c.text: 舒适区内没有力量,在市场上也没有。
98514f835e0c.original: There is no power in comfort, not in the marketplace.

1ec225e2ad2d.text: 人类只会关注新鲜或不同的事物。所以如果你看鞋子,它们全都是黑色、黑色、黑色,然后下一双鞋子是红色的,这就是你首先关注的。
1ec225e2ad2d.original: Humans only pay attention to what is new or what is different. So if you're looking at shoes and they're all black, black, black, black, and then the next pair of shoes is red, that's the first thing you focus on.

f508d480b022.text: 一个好的名称只会帮助你,但一个糟糕的名称不会伤害一家好公司。
f508d480b022.original: A good name is only going to help you, but a bad name won't hurt a good company.

c5bd0e39cc2b.text: 随着时间的推移,一个词可以变得超越它本身的含义。比如,迪士尼今天意味着魔法,沃尔沃意味着安全。这些名称并不好。如果我只是把它们放在电子表格或者名单里,没有人会选择它们。
c5bd0e39cc2b.original: Over time, a word can come to mean something that is beyond what that actual word means. Like Disney means magic today. Volvo means safety. Those names are not good. If I just put it in a spreadsheet or one of those lists, no one would pick it.

6af777d7e987.text: 我认为在一个双边市场中,你要先从供给端着手,至于最后是优化需求端还是偏重某一方,都取决于具体情况下的取舍。
6af777d7e987.original: I actually just think they're two-sided and you start with the supply and at the end of the day, you can optimize for the demand side or choose who you're going to prioritize in terms of if there's a conflict, we're going to pick this side or the other.

77ce73d3c481.text: 在那种实时性很强的双边市场,比如打车软件,如果没有足够的供给,或者供给方不满意,甚至罢工,又或者受到监管限制,这都会直接影响你的业务。
77ce73d3c481.original: In a marketplace like that where it's real time people trying to get a cab to go from uptown to downtown, you see the inexperience firsthand the impact to your business if you don't have suppliers, if your suppliers aren't happy, if they go on strike, if there's regulations that mean you can't use your service.

1c878ccc1b6e.text: 事实上,Airbnb的产品就是它的房东,没有房东,Airbnb什么都不是。
1c878ccc1b6e.original: Your product really wasn't your technology. Airbnb is nothing without its hosts, nothing. If anything, Airbnb's product was its hosts.

b3c980443b5c.text: 想要推动一个市场的发展,必须让供给方主动投入到你的平台上。我的合伙人Bill Gurley就提到,优秀的双边市场往往能孕育出新的行业巨头。
b3c980443b5c.original: In order to tip a market, you need suppliers to want to lean in on your marketplace. My partner, Bill Gurley talks about how great marketplaces create the new incumbents. So you basically have suppliers who aren't the incumbents.

5a8947927f52.text: 我认为一般建议大家应该更多关注需求端,而不是过度关注供给端。毕竟,能够聚集住自己行业需求的,才是最终的赢家。
5a8947927f52.original: I think on average when you hear advice about where to focus, people over rotate on supply and actually are under focused on demand. I think ultimately demand is the only thing that matters. If you are successful at aggregating the demand in your industry, you will have the winning marketplace.

254d4660c060.text: 数据飞轮的关键在于,你可以从独有的数据开始,但关键是要持续维护和积累这些数据。另一个关键点就是工作流整合。
254d4660c060.context: 彼得·邓是在讨论人工智能创业公司的两个关键策略:数据飞轮(通过用户数据不断优化的系统)和将产品深度嵌入用户日常工作流程中。
254d4660c060.original: The data flywheel part is just, you can start with proprietary data, but the flywheel is really just sort of how do you continue to maintain that and generate that. And the second thing is, again, it's the workflow.
254d4660c060.originalContext: Peter is discussing two key strategies for AI startups: data flywheels (systems that continuously improve through user data) and workflow integration into users' daily processes.

a02d21955851.text: 世界上最富有的公司愿意不惜一切代价提升模型的能力。
a02d21955851.context: 布伦丹·富迪是Mercor的CEO和联合创始人,Mercor帮助人工智能公司聘请专家评估和改善人工智能模型的性能。
a02d21955851.original: The wealthiest companies in the world are willing to spend whatever it takes to improve model capabilities.
a02d21955851.originalContext: Foody is CEO of Mercor, which helps AI companies hire experts to evaluate and improve AI model performance.

46232e2dfb22.text: 我们非常专注于一些非常通用的使用场景,比如一般的推理能力、编码能力和写作能力。当涉及到一些垂直应用领域时,我们的模型可能永远无法像哈维的那样出色。
46232e2dfb22.context: 洛根·基尔帕特里克是OpenAI的开发者关系负责人。哈维是一家专注于为律师和法律公司构建定制模型和专门工具的人工智能初创公司。
46232e2dfb22.original: We're deeply focused on these very, very general use cases like the general reasoning capabilities, the general coding, the general writing abilities. I think where you start to get into some of these very vertical applications... that's a great example of our models are probably never going to be as capable as some of the things that Harvey's doing.
46232e2dfb22.originalContext: Harvey is an AI startup that builds specialized legal tools and custom models for lawyers and law firms.

84f3b31c0530.text: 人们严重低估了这些应用程序价值创造的所在。虽然用户界面和数据模型很有用,但最关键的是产品背后多年来不断优化的工作流。
84f3b31c0530.original: People really underestimate where the value is created in these applications and they just kind of get it completely wrong. It's not the UI that matters and it's not the data model that matters, although those are both very useful. It's the years and years and years of evolution of the underlying workflows of the product to support the customers.

7cf2ccb70092.text: 如果我们发布的东西可以被任何人仅凭我们的现成模型就能构建,那虽然也有很棒的东西可以用我们的模型构建,但我们应该专注于那些能发挥我们独特优势的东西,也就是模型研发和产品体验开发相结合的地方。
7cf2ccb70092.context: 迈克·克里格尔是Anthropic的产品负责人(Instagram联合创始人),他在讨论Anthropic的人工智能模型(如Claude)以及模型开发和产品体验开发之间的交集。
7cf2ccb70092.original: If we're shipping things that could have been built by anybody just using our models off the shelf, there's great stuff to be built by using our models off the shelf by the way, don't get me wrong, but where we should play and what we can do uniquely should be stuff that's really at that magic intersection between the two.
7cf2ccb70092.originalContext: Mike Krieger is discussing Anthropic's AI models (like Claude) and the intersection between model development and product experience development.

d1ca99c30d2b.text: 每一部电影都从某种世界的转变开始,我把这种转变称为从旧游戏到新游戏的转变。这种结构真的是关于定义一个运动,这与'嘿,我要解决你的问题'有很大不同。
d1ca99c30d2b.original: Every movie starts with some kind of shift in the world, and I call this shift the shift from the old game to a new game. This structure really is about defining a movement, and that's very different from, 'Hey, I'm going to solve your problem.'

067357a28c5c.text: 我们必须向他们展示,未来不会仅仅是有点好。他们看到的是在一个非常负面的结果和一个潜在的非常积极的结果之间的分裂。
067357a28c5c.context: Raskin正在讨论他的战略叙事框架,公司必须向潜在客户展示,未来要么是非常负面的,要么是非常积极的,而不是平庸的。
067357a28c5c.original: We got to show them that the future is not going to just be sort of okay. They see it as split between a very negative outcome and a potentially very positive outcome.
067357a28c5c.originalContext: Raskin is discussing his strategic narrative framework where companies must show prospects that the future holds either very negative or very positive outcomes, not mediocre ones.

114b1293cf34.text: 某种程度上,你并不是在推销产品。产品只是让这个故事成真的道具。非常重要的道具,但有一个更高层次的框架成为对话的重点。
114b1293cf34.original: In a way you're not pitching product. Product is like a prop for making the story come true. Very important prop, but there's this higher level overlay that becomes the focus of the conversation.

9c9166afd0e2.text: 他们不仅在为一个工具而努力,也在为一种新的工作方式而努力。如果你能给你的客户提供这种理念,这是他们可以真正支持和倡导的东西。
9c9166afd0e2.original: It's not just that they're championing for a tool, they're also championing for a new way of working. If you can equip your customers with that philosophy, that's something they can really get behind and champion.

bfaad2f74cf1.text: 您能有多大成功,完全取决于您所在的品类的规模。
bfaad2f74cf1.original: You can only be as big and successful as your market category.

57c67914f658.text: 在考虑品类创造时,关键是要明确我们的目标范围,不能把目标定得太小。
57c67914f658.original: When you're thinking about category creation, it's really, for us, it was really about the scope of what we're trying to do and not wanting to be in something too small.

abe92cc29e90.text: 我们不是要去创造一个新的品类,而是要提升现有品类的价值。我们会集中所有资源来让这个整个品类对用户和企业更有价值。
abe92cc29e90.original: Instead of spending the time and money to build a new category, we were going to spend the time and money to elevate the value of this category. So rather than changing the category to something else which we could value at whatever it was, we were just going to spend all of our resources to make this whole category much more valuable to the users, to companies.

7a4f753d5c85.text: 我们不能只从总可寻址市场(TAM)这个角度来限制自己。从Figma Design来看,我们并没有数据支持说世界上设计师的数量足以支撑Figma Design成为一个很大的市场。
7a4f753d5c85.context: 总可寻址市场(TAM)是用来评估业务机会潜力大小的一个指标。
7a4f753d5c85.original: You can't constrain by always sorting, descending by TAM, but we're not very much, from Figma Design, there is no reason, no data that we could look at that said, there are enough designers in the world for Figma Design to be a big market.
7a4f753d5c85.originalContext: TAM refers to Total Addressable Market, a measure used to evaluate the potential size of a business opportunity.

ff2066c31846.text: 你不需要超越竞争对手,这太昂贵且防御性很强。你要去做小于竞争对手的事。我们需要更多的简单和清晰。
ff2066c31846.original: You don't need to outdo the competition, it's expensive and defensive. Underdo your competition. We need more simplicity and clarity.

137826de8c66.text: 我更看重一致性而非全面性。我们宁愿在更少的手机上提供更一致的体验,也不愿在所有手机上提供不一致的体验。
137826de8c66.original: I value consistency over comprehensiveness. We would much rather be on fewer phones with a more consistent experience than be on all of them with an inconsistent experience.

5b3fed4d057e.text: 我们做出这个选择时...很难记得了,对吧?因为这已经是18年前,17年前的事了。在那个时代,Office是难以撼动的,对吗?所以软件必须要实体分发,必须要被购买和安装。使用起来也更困难。因此存在着非常高的交易成本。由于交易成本很高,买家总是会做这样的决定:'我要选择1000个功能的还是995个功能的?我不知道那最后5个功能是什么,但我可能还是都要拥有吧。'
5b3fed4d057e.original: We made this choice with... So it's a little hard to remember, right? Because it's like 18 years, 17 years ago now, 18 years ago almost. In that era, Office was impregnable, right? So software had to be distributed physically, right, it had to be shipped around, it had to be bought and installed. It was harder to use. And so there's a very high transactional cost. Because there's a very high transactional cost, the buyers would always make this decision like, 'Do I want the thing with 1,000 features or the thing with 995 features? I don't know what those last five are, but I might as well have all of them.'

d73634f05f95.text: 我听说过一些很棒的创业建议,就是创业公司应该专注于一件事,并在那件事上成为真正卓越的专家。而我们最初的选择正好相反。
d73634f05f95.original: Some of the best startup advice I've heard is startups should focus on one thing and be really, really exceptionally world-class at that one thing. And one of our early zigs is we are going to do exactly the opposite of that.

85e1f198f16c.text: 有人同时看到你正在做什么,或有多位设计师同时在文件中工作,这其中存在着某些争议性。我们最初看到的反应之一就是'如果这就是设计的未来,我就退出'。这种紧张感正是你正处于革命之中的信号。
85e1f198f16c.original: There's something controversial about everyone seeing what you're doing, or multiple designers being in the file at the same time. One of the first responses we saw was 'if this is the future of design, I'm quitting.' That tension is signal that you're part of a revolution.

c06d6c850ed3.text: 我们公开展示我们的会议,甚至有些令人不安,这是一种'如果我们是他们,为什么他们应该相信我们?为什么任何人都应该相信我们?'的行为。我们掌握着你最敏感的个人数据和专业数据。如果我们一次次失去了信任,你为什么要相信我们?
c06d6c850ed3.original: Building in public showing you our meetings, uncomfortably so, is an act in, 'If we were them, why should they trust us? Why should anyone trust us?' We have your most sensitive personal data. We have your most sensitive professional data. Why should you trust us if we've had our trust broken again and again?

49672abec40b.text: 我们称之为'糖衣青菜'。人们不想吃青菜,但是他们喜欢糖,所以我们给他们糖,然后把青菜藏在里面。
49672abec40b.original: We call it sugar-coated broccoli. People don't want to eat the broccoli but people like sugar, so it gave them the sugar then hide your broccoli inside of it.

af08e501be50.text: 我们真的鼓励客户提出独特、不同且大胆的观点。如果有9个人持有一种观点,而另一个人持有相反的观点,那么很可能这个人就是记者想要采访的对象。
af08e501be50.original: We really push our clients to have something unique and different and bold to say. If nine of them have one stance on something happening in the field and one has the other stance, chances are that one is going to be the one that a reporter wants to talk to.

223f804868a1.text: 真正反映产品市场契合度的信号,最终是让人掏腰包付费给你。
223f804868a1.original: The true signal of product-market fit is ultimately having people open up their wallets and pay you.

3b879978718f.text: 当你绝对确定自己拥有产品市场契合度时,你就拥有了它;因此,如果你还不确定,那么你就还没有它。
3b879978718f.original: Product market fit is a sort of thing where you absolutely know it when you see it, and therefore if you don't absolutely know it, you don't have it.

0f6257866f8f.text: 第二天你问自己的两个问题是,『我们是在扩展一个产品吗?我们有热爱我们的客户,并有持续大量需求的声音吗?还是我们还在寻找那股客户需求的声音?』如果答案是『我们还在寻找它』,然后你问『这个估值是数亿还是数千万?』,如果答案是数亿或更多,但你还在寻找那股需求之声,那你就是一家已不再增长的公司。
0f6257866f8f.context: 「需求之声」指的是强烈的客户需求,能自然地吸引人们使用你的产品,这是产品市场契合度的标志。
0f6257866f8f.original: The two questions you ask yourself the day after we listen to this podcast is, 'Hey, are we scaling a product? We have customers that love us and we have a tremendous sucking sound? Or are we trying to find that customer sucking sound?' And if the answer is, 'We're still trying to find it,' and then you're like, 'Is your evaluation hundreds of millions or tens of millions?' and if the answer is hundreds or more and you're still trying to find that sucking sound, you're an ex-growth company.
0f6257866f8f.originalContext: "Sucking sound" refers to strong customer demand that naturally pulls people toward your product, indicating product-market fit.

ceb4c5b9d6f8.text: 如果你有一个能很好留住用户的产品,但找不到更多用户,我认为那还不算是产品市场契合度。
ceb4c5b9d6f8.original: If you got a product that retains well and you can't find more users for it, I don't think that's product market fit.

94dc3bd66c39.text: 我说 OKR 更像是一种维生素,而不是药物。所以,如果你采用 OKR,认为它就能解决你公司所有的问题,那是不可能的。它只会暴露出公司内部存在的各种问题。
94dc3bd66c39.context: OKR 代表目标和关键结果,这是一种目标设定框架,被许多科技公司用于季度规划和团队协作。
94dc3bd66c39.original: I say OKRs are more of a vitamin, they're not a medicine. So, if you take OKRs and you're like, 'Oh, this will fix everything that's wrong with you.' No, that's not going to happen. It's just going to reveal everything that's wrong with your company.
94dc3bd66c39.originalContext: OKRs stands for Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting framework used by many tech companies for quarterly planning and alignment.

9052a86ae96f.text: 对我来说,一个好的 OKR 有三个关键特征:可读性、可操作性和真实性。可读性是指人们看了就能理解它在说什么;可操作性是指 OKR 能推动行动;真实性则是指 OKR 是否如实反映了你日常工作的实际情况。
9052a86ae96f.context: OKR (目标和关键结果)是一种目标设定框架,被许多科技公司用于定义可测量的目标并追踪其结果。
9052a86ae96f.original: For me, there are three things that really matter about a good OKR, and one is legibility. People look at it and understand what it is... I think actionability, I want OKR to inspire action... And the third one is authenticity, which is, does this actually, honestly depict what you're doing, what you're trying to do on a day-to-day basis?
9052a86ae96f.originalContext: OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) are a goal-setting framework used by companies to define measurable objectives and track their outcomes.

2fb74ff3a0d3.text: 无论你如何称呼它,一个好的 OKR 都有三个关键特征:可读性 - 人们能理解它在说什么;可操作性 - 它能激发行动;真实性 - 它如实反映了你日常工作的实际情况。
2fb74ff3a0d3.context: OKR (目标和关键结果)是一种目标设定框架,被许多科技公司用来让团队围绕可测量的结果保持一致。
2fb74ff3a0d3.original: No matter what you call it, there are three things that really matter about a good OKR: legibility - people understand what it is; actionability - it inspires action; and authenticity - does this honestly depict what you're doing on a day-to-day basis?
2fb74ff3a0d3.originalContext: OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) are a goal-setting framework used by many tech companies to align teams around measurable outcomes.

7c561841b9a5.text: 有时候,我只是想让产品体验更好。当然,我可以想出一种愚蠢的方法来衡量这一点,但这并不是我每天都在考虑的事情。所以 OKR 看起来很形式主义,需要大量工作。
7c561841b9a5.original: Sometimes you're just, I'm just trying to make the experience better. And sure, I can come up with this BS way to measure what that looks like, but that's not what I'm thinking about every day, anyway. So it just seems very performative, and there's just a lot of work that goes into it.

b9011900462e.text: 当你在处理核心体验时,有时你只是想让产品体验更好。当然,我可以想出一种愚蠢的方法来衡量这一点,但这并不是我每天都在考虑的事情。所以 OKR 看起来很形式主义。
b9011900462e.original: When you're working on a core experience, sometimes you're just trying to make the experience better. Sure, I can come up with this BS way to measure what that looks like, but that's not what I'm thinking about every day anyway. So OKRs just seem very performative.

8ea4a1b79427.text: 要么你想出一些次要指标,但没人真的关心它;要么你锁定某些业务目标,但你无法证明自己真的推动了它们。所以要么你锁定了一些很重要但你无法推动的东西,要么是你能推动但实际上并不重要的东西。
8ea4a1b79427.original: Either you come up with some secondary metric that nobody actually cares about, or you anchor on business goals that you can't actually prove you moved. So either you anchor something that matters but you can't move, or something you can move but doesn't actually matter.

50283705eb52.text: OKR 是行不通的。为什么?因为 OKR 的根本假设是它能解决某类用户的需求,但如果它要同时服务于三种不同类型的用户,那么所有目标之间就会相互矛盾。
50283705eb52.context: OKR 代表目标和关键结果,这是一种目标设定框架,团队通过设定可测量的目标和关键结果来追踪进展。
50283705eb52.original: OKRs will not work. Why not? So, fundamentally, OKRs are a way to think about objectives and key results, but the fundamental assumption here is that it is solving for a kind of user, and that kind of user, you can divide and conquer. But if it is working for three different kinds of users, then all the goals will all the time be in conflict with each other.
50283705eb52.originalContext: OKRs stands for Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting framework where teams set measurable objectives with specific key results to track progress.

e39b3b489f8f.text: 计划没有用,但是做计划却很有用。花时间停下来思考一下很有价值:'我们做了什么?哪些事情进展顺利?哪些不顺利?我们学到了什么?接下来我们打算做什么?'
e39b3b489f8f.original: Plans are useless. Planning is helpful. It's really valuable to have a moment where you stop and go, 'Okay. What did we do? What worked? What went well? What didn't go well? What did we learn and now what do we think we're going to do next?'

97596f8add43.text: 路线图的真正目的不是作为计划,而是用来试验你的策略。
97596f8add43.original: The whole point about a roadmap is that it's not designed to be your plan. I think about it as being a prototype for your strategy.

f266dc622ee4.text: 路线图的价值不在于最终成品,而在于制定路线图的过程本身。你实际上是在梳理解决问题的假设。
f266dc622ee4.original: The value isn't in your roadmap, the value is in the roadmapping process. What you're actually doing is laying out your assumptions of the problems that you're solving.

d5a14ea01134.text: 战略中的路线图不是承诺,而是一种方式来检查你的计划是否有意义且可行。因为我看到的每个团队做路线图的时候,最后都会发现:'我们在5年或10年内实现愿景是不可能的,这简直是一个30年的愿景,如果我们保持现有的进度的话。'
d5a14ea01134.original: A roadmap in strategy is not a commitment. Instead, it's a way to double check if your plan makes any sense at all and is even anywhere near feasible. Because what happens to every team I see do these roadmaps, you put it together and you realize 'We're not going to hit our vision in five years or 10. This is like a 30 year vision, if we keep going at the pace we're going.'

2ef99e229b12.text: 确保在任何给定的时间段内,你的计划不会超过该执行期的10%。这是一个非常容易犯的错误...你最终会计划得太多,而且通常在启动或学习之前,你并不真正知道接下来会发生什么。
2ef99e229b12.original: Ensure that you're not for a given time period planning for more than 10% of that execution period. And I think this is a really easy mistake to make... you end up just planning way too much and oftentimes you really don't know what's ahead until you've launched or learned something.

e4d6fbcc7c66.text: 这是一个产品领导人的时刻,真正的战时时刻,你需要完全抛弃路线图,与所有人分享背景,说'好了,各位,我们现在的任务跟几周前完全不同了。'
e4d6fbcc7c66.original: This is a product leader, it's a real wartime moment where you just need to blow up roadmaps, share context with everyone and say, 'Okay, everyone, we have a totally different mandate than what we did a couple weeks ago.'

224bc823e25f.text: 我们进入了两周的规划模式。Greg Greeley,曾经担任Airbnb总裁,他常说,'你无法制定一年或一个季度的计划,我们要每两周制定一次计划,对应每两周的反应。'
224bc823e25f.original: We went into two week planning mode. Greg Greeley, who was the president of Airbnb used to say, 'Look, can't plan for a year, can't plan for a quarter. We're going to plan every two weeks. We're going to react to every two weeks.'

17e16bd1d56f.text: 新闻的传播速度如此之快,你无暇顾及路线图。我们的团队摆脱了一些常规流程的束缚,能够专注于真正重大新闻和内容的叙述。
17e16bd1d56f.context: 亚历克斯·哈德曼讨论了新闻机构如何在重大突发新闻事件期间调整其编辑流程,因为传统的内容计划变得不切实际。
17e16bd1d56f.original: The speed of news is so fast that you don't have time to mess with roadmaps. We really have teams who are freed up from some of the normal processes around that, so they can really just focus on storytelling for really big stories and pieces.
17e16bd1d56f.originalContext: Alex Hardiman was discussing how news organizations adapt their editorial processes during major breaking news events, where traditional content planning becomes impractical.

a7b5fc8fa8a3.context: Alex Hardiman在讨论新闻组织如何在重大突发新闻事件中调整其编辑流程,因为传统的内容计划在这种情况下变得不切实际。
a7b5fc8fa8a3.original: Two types of crisis. One is I would call that a cash crisis. All of a sudden, your cash program or plan is being jeopardized, losing a customer, disappearing investor. And the other one is lose of product market fit.

a929bb2296b5.text: 两种危机类型:一种是现金危机,就是你的现金计划或方案突然受到威胁,失去客户,投资者消失。另一种是产品市场适配性消失。
a929bb2296b5.original: When product market fit disappear, you actually need to go back to square one. Then you basically say everything that I know so far is irrelevant anymore.

e876c1915eb4.text: 时间线的问题在于,一旦你有了时间线,它就变成了一种数学图表,你有X轴上的时间,Y轴上的要做的事情,结果就是所有东西下面都被分配了截止日期或迭代。
e876c1915eb4.original: The problem with the timeline is that as soon as you have a timeline, it turns it into a math chart sort of thing, where you've got time on the X axis and things to do on the Y axis and you basically end up with everything underneath is assigned a due date or a iteration.

bc08f83df946.text: 如果你在某个季度、某个星期或某个日期要求太多,你就会做出奇怪的决定来控制范围。
bc08f83df946.original: If you ask too much for a particular quarter, a particular week, or date, you will make strange choices about scope.

aab3b124f06f.text: 产品经理似乎是唯一被要求给出具体交付日期的人。你的销售团队不会被要求给出他们工作的确切交付日期。
aab3b124f06f.original: Product people are the only ones who seem to be pinned down to be required to give concrete dates as to when things are going to be delivered in this way. Your sales team isn't asked to give exact delivery dates on their work.

04c733bff953.text: 你在讲一个故事。所以我希望从你那里得到的是主题,是一个故事。为什么这些是最大的投资重点,最大的杠杆点?
04c733bff953.original: You're telling a story. So what I want from you is I want themes, I want a story. Why are these things the biggest things to invest in these levers, the biggest ones to pull?

94a447420d99.text: 人们真正渴望的是'我为什么要做这项工作?'我认为在你自己的头脑中清晰地阐述这一点是非常重要的。
94a447420d99.original: What people, what humans really crave is like, 'Why am I doing this body of work?' And I think it's also really, really important to have that really crisply articulated in your own head.

f61073033447.text: 为了持续发展,你每 18 个月都需要引入一些新事物。
f61073033447.original: Every 18 months you need to introduce something new in order for it to continue evolving.

793b16670e3d.text: 将产品、营销和销售等多种增长模式整合并持续迭代创新,而不是只关注单一方法的优化,这是很多增长团队常犯的大错。
793b16670e3d.context: Elena 在讨论增长团队应该不断叠加不同的增长模式(产品驱动、营销驱动、销售驱动),而不是过度优化单一方法。
793b16670e3d.original: Not overlaying every single way that you can grow through product, through marketing and through sales as an evolution. Is a huge mistake that a lot of growth teams fail to iterate on and innovate on.
793b16670e3d.originalContext: Elena is discussing how growth teams should continuously layer different growth models (product-led, marketing-led, sales-led) rather than over-optimizing single approaches.

f966fa029df3.text: 我们应该每 6 到 12 个月就去'吞噬'掉现有的产品状态。每 6 到 12 个月,我们的新产品应该能让现有产品显得毫无意义、甚至愚蠢。
f966fa029df3.original: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly. It should almost make the form factor of existing product look dumb.

909a72d028b4.text: 我认为成功公司正在出现一些新模式:第一,他们拥抱 AI 并让所有人都精通 AI;第二,他们开始思考如何用 AI 改善现有流程;第三,在看到影响力和广泛应用后,他们就开始探索如何利用 AI 推动增长。
909a72d028b4.original: I think there's a pattern that's starting to emerge for successful companies. One is they are embracing AI and everybody becomes AI fluent. Number two, they start to say, 'Okay, how can I take a process that already exists and apply AI to making it better?' The third thing then is like, 'Okay, great. Now that you've seen impact, everybody is using it, how do you actually use it to inflect growth?'

4459989e1e37.text: 第一步是理解'物理规则';第二步是思考增长环和漏斗的定量指标,看是否符合这些'物理规则',如果不符合就需要改变 4 到 5 件事。
4459989e1e37.context: '物理规则'指的是你的商业模式的基本约束和参数 - 比如目标市场、产品能力、分销渠道和变现模式等。
4459989e1e37.original: Step one is, what are the physics? Step two is when you think about loops and growth funnels and the quantitative inputs to each loop, does that fit into these physics or do you have to change four or five different things?
4459989e1e37.originalContext: "Physics" refers to the fundamental constraints and parameters of your business model - things like your market, product capabilities, distribution channels, and monetization structure.

a160115aa2f3.text: 度量指标不能主宰日历。因此我们会有一个两年的路线图。除了一些基础设施项目外,公司内的每一件事都必须在路线图上。
a160115aa2f3.original: Metrics are going to be subordinate to the calendar. So we're going to have a roadmap. It's going to be a two-year roadmap.

c19033729775.text: 你只有把它放在路线图上,才能上线推出。所以公司内的每一件事,除了一些基础设施项目外,都必须在路线图上。
c19033729775.original: You can't ship something unless it's on the roadmap. So every single thing in the company, with the exception of some infrastructure projects have to be on the roadmap.

8af5d95c7491.text: 我基本上会避免从产品角度使用OKR。我想专注于速度,也就是产出,也就是你的路线图,但它们更适用于跨职能的工作。
8af5d95c7491.context: OKR(Objectives and Key Results)是一个目标管理框架,团队定义目标并通过特定的关键结果来衡量进度。
8af5d95c7491.original: I largely stay away from OKRs from a product perspective. I want to focus on velocity, which is just output, which is your roadmap, but they're pretty strong at more of the cross-functional side of things.
8af5d95c7491.originalContext: OKRs stands for Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting framework where teams define objectives and measure progress through specific key results.

e552277c8fd5.text: 我发现这种方法在规划中非常有用...60%的时间用于增量改进...30%我希望用于大型新举措...10%我希望用于稳定性和基础设施。
e552277c8fd5.original: I have found that approach very useful during planning... 60% of our time on incrementals... 30% I want to allocate towards big new initiatives... 10% I'd like us to allocate towards stability and infrastructure.

11cb13b95db4.text: 对于大多数团队来说,Slack任何产品团队的路线图都是一个投资组合,并且是多元化的。一方面,你想多元化那些旨在成为新功能的东西,另一方面,你想让已经构建的东西每天都有一点点的改进。
11cb13b95db4.original: I think for most teams, our roadmap for any feature team at Slack is that it's a portfolio and it's meant to be a portfolio that's diversified a couple different ways. One is you want to diversify things that are meant to be new capabilities versus making the thing you've already built a little bit better every day.

9d7ab40686c0.text: 我们改变了这种方式,创建了非常小的团队,设立了诸如探索、创造、影响力、扩大规模等阶段门控。目的是在每个阶段评估这些尝试。其想法是快速迭代,或者证明这个方案行不通,或者证明确实可行,值得进一步投入。
9d7ab40686c0.original: We changed that to create really small groups with stage gates that we call wonder, explore, make, impact, and then getting to scale. And that meant to assess those bets at every stage. And the idea was to iterate really quickly, either to it not working out and proving that it couldn't be a business or iterate really quickly to yes it could and we should invest more in this.

56dd1c5e0586.text: 我们可以说,我们非常纪律严明,要求产品在每个阶段都证明自己。
56dd1c5e0586.original: We were very disciplined, I guess you could say, about having the product prove itself at every given point.

fc98805a1a37.text: 每当我们提议做一些产品方面的事情,比如进行研究测试、试运营或扩大试运营,我们都有说服我们这是个好决定的数据支持。
fc98805a1a37.original: Anytime that we were proposing doing something with the product, like running some research test, or running the pilot, or expanding the pilot, we always had the data that had convinced us that that was a good decision.

5adeb7ed2128.text: 在能见度有限、面临重大阻力的情况下,我认为制定一个非常保守的计划,并设置短期里程碑来解锁增长和支出的能力,是一个好办法。
5adeb7ed2128.original: The way I think about setting up a plan when you have limited visibility and some major headwinds is setting up a really conservative plan and then having milestones, short term milestones that unlock the ability to lean into growth and spend based on hitting those targets.

f15d4f8cd882.text: 你的工作是大梦大做,同时也要制定计划去实现它。这里有五个里程碑,我将在每个季度完成,以实现这个非常非常宏大的目标。
f15d4f8cd882.original: Your job is to dream big and also have a plan to go tackle it. Here are the five milestones that it's going to take me to do quarter over quarter to achieve this really, really ambitious thing.

7f16b496f96c.text: 让一个团队独立工作,给予他们过程自由。他们不希望我们被现有产品线的阻力分散注意力。当你在开发现有产品线时,会有固定的节奏,但是当你在开发新事物时,需要更快的迭代循环。
7f16b496f96c.context: 「阻力」指的是开发成熟产品线时,更缓慢、更僵化的流程和节奏。
7f16b496f96c.original: Taking a team off to the side, giving that team process freedom. They didn't want us distracted from the drag. When you're working on an existing product line, you get this cadence and it can become a mature cadence. Maybe people work in two weeks or one week now, but when you're working on something new, you need faster iteration loops.
7f16b496f96c.originalContext: "The drag" refers to the slower, more rigid processes and cadences of working on existing mature product lines.

d527ff963fdc.text: 由于我们有以用户为先和精益求精的操作原则,我们的制定计划方式都围绕着预留足够时间来确保体验良好。
d527ff963fdc.original: Because we have operating principles of users first and being meticulous in our craft, we actually tend, all of our ways of building plans tend to be wired quite well around this idea that we're going to reserve enough time to really make the experience good.

099561435d7a.text: 每个季度,给你的销售负责人一定的预算,无论是故事点还是占整体开发资源的10%。当你这样做时,事情会发生根本性的改变。
099561435d7a.context: 「故事点」是敏捷项目管理中用于衡量开发团队产能的单位;「饼状图」指的是整体开发资源的分配情况。
099561435d7a.original: Every quarter, give your head of sales a certain budget, whether it's story points or 10% of the pie chart. When you do this, things will radically change.
099561435d7a.originalContext: Story points are development team capacity units used in agile project management; "pie chart" refers to overall development resources allocation.

42660fa4a0ac.text: 一个产品团队,一个赋权的产品团队,不再被分配一张功能路线图,而是被给予要解决的问题。现在这些可能是客户问题,也可能是业务问题,或者两者兼有,但他们被赋予解决问题的任务。通常每个季度会有一到两个这样的问题,除了所有人都需要做的那种维持基本运转的工作。他们被赋予艰难的问题去解决,衡量的标准不是交付了什么,而是解决了问题。
42660fa4a0ac.original: A product team, an empowered product team, instead of being given that roadmap of features, they're given problems to solve. Now they're customer problems or they're business problems or both, but they're given a problem to solve. Usually one or two a quarter on top of of course the keep the lights on kind of work that everybody does, but they're given hard problems to solve and the measure is not ship the thing. The measure is it solves the problem.

af513f2d9330.text: 对于一个特性团队来说,基本上就是被分配了一张输出的路线图。这就是关键所在,就是产出。换句话说,他们的功能就是项目,通常可能来自高管,可能来自大客户,可能来自其他地方。但它们就是一堆功能,你需要被要求去设计、开发、测试和部署这些功能。
af513f2d9330.original: On a feature team, you're basically given a roadmap of output. That's the key, is output. In other words, their features are projects that usually it could have come from an executive, could have come from a big pocket customer, could have come from wherever. But it's a bunch of features and literally you're being asked to design, build, test, deploy that feature.

437afd5e15ba.text: 对于一个特性团队来说,基本上就是被分配了一张输出的路线图。换句话说,他们的功能就是项目,通常可能来自高管,可能来自大客户,可能来自其他地方。但它们就是一堆功能,你需要被要求去设计、开发、测试和部署这些功能。
437afd5e15ba.original: On a feature team, you're basically given a roadmap of output. In other words, their features are projects that usually it could have come from an executive, could have come from a big pocket customer, could have come from wherever. But it's a bunch of features and literally you're being asked to design, build, test, deploy that feature.

1c71906471cf.text: 你不能真正将路线图委托给一个研发团队。负责维护产品、构建产品,与最终用户有最密切反馈循环的团队,他们才是真正应该拥有和掌控路线图的人。
1c71906471cf.original: You can't really delegate roadmap to an R&D team. The team who's responsible for maintaining the product, for building the product, who has the closest feedback loop with the end customer, they're the ones who really need to own and feel like they control the roadmap.

e953cbbd067a.text: 一次好的转型就像回到家一样。它更温暖、更接近你擅长的领域。
e953cbbd067a.original: A good pivot is like going home. It's warmer, it's closer to something that you're an expert at.

bf2c951880e8.text: 如果情况不太理想且你没有更多创意,那通常是一个很好的转型时机。但是如果你还有半打或一打很好的增长想法没有尝试,那就去试试看吧。
bf2c951880e8.original: If it's not going well and you're out of ideas, that is usually a good time to pivot. But when you have half a dozen or a dozen really good growth ideas that you haven't tried yet, try them.

2e803cbea316.text: 从一个产品到两个产品很难。从两个到无数个就容易多了,但从一个到两个实在是太难了。
2e803cbea316.original: Going from one to two products is hard. Going from two to end is much easier, but going from one to two is hard.

b61b9e932102.text: 产品市场契合度只是关于产品本身的,不是一家公司,也无法实现规模化。
b61b9e932102.original: Product market fit is just the product, and that is not a company, and that will not scale.

6f467514806a.text: 我们有一个我们认为是公共路线图的东西。这基本上就是人们要求我们提供的...它不会在击败竞争对手方面成为一个游戏改变者。所以我们有一个我们认为是秘密路线图的东西。
6f467514806a.original: We have what we think of as the public roadmap. This is basically what people have asked us for... It's not going to be a game changer in terms of winning against your competition. So we have a second roadmap which we think of as a secret roadmap.

5d037180b1c3.text: 秘密路线图是我们从未公开讨论过的、从未告诉任何人的东西,我们只是宣布它们并将它们交给用户,看看会产生什么影响。
5d037180b1c3.original: The secret roadmap is things we never talk about publicly, never tell anybody about, and we announce them and just give them to users and see the effects.

b45ca227f432.text: 从创办公司的那一刻起就要开始为出售公司做准备,这是一件奇怪的事情,因为显然,如果你正在创办一家公司,对大多数创始人来说,他们希望它成为下一个大事物,而不是为了出售它,但把它放在你的雷达上是一件好事,因为谁也不知道未来会怎样。
b45ca227f432.original: Start preparing to sell your company from the moment you found it which is a weird thing because obviously, if you're starting a company, for most founders, they want it to be the next big thing, they're not starting it in order to sell it, but it's a good thing to have on your radar because you never know what the future holds.

5b0c7fb9228f.text: 我们就是说:'好吧,我们该怎么办?我们要把这个东西放出去。每个人都会有一堆问题。他们可能会非常怀疑,我们知道它可能会是一场彻底的灾难。'
5b0c7fb9228f.original: We're like, 'Well, what do we do? We're going to put this out there. Everyone's going to have all these questions. They're probably going to be really skeptical, and we know it might be a total dumpster fire.'

fca07382a93a.text: 展示而不是讲述是一种方法,产品经理从整体的用户体验开始思考,并与团队一起创作出一系列用户使用场景的素材。
fca07382a93a.context: 「展示而不是讲述」是拉蒂的产品方法论,产品经理创建详细的用户旅程可视化和素材,而不只是书面规格。
fca07382a93a.original: Show don't tell is essentially a way in where the product manager starts ideating with the entire experience, and they actually create all the collaterals together of a user they need to begin with.
fca07382a93a.originalContext: "Show don't tell" is Rathi's product methodology where PMs create detailed user journey visualizations and materials rather than just written specifications.

7609c595f8fe.text: 我实际上要求我的团队撰写三份不同的新闻稿,以涵盖多样性。
7609c595f8fe.original: I actually ask my teams to write three press releases, alternative and divergent.

9f96de82db60.text: 当我总结其他人的意见,特别是来自不同利益相关方,我会在会议中甚至会议外独立思考,如何让这个想法变得更好。
9f96de82db60.original: When I summarize what other people are saying and especially multiple different stakeholders, then I can think about offline and not in the context of right in the meeting, sometimes in the meeting too I guess, is how do I make this idea one click better?

610871027576.text: 我会尽可能多地尝试,看哪些方法能奏效。我在寻找能转化成胜利战略的有潜力的战术。
610871027576.original: I'm throwing everything against the wall. I'm looking at what's going to stick. I am looking to try to find the winning tactic and turn it into a winning strategy.

5f1f8cb05661.text: 赢家和输家有相同的目标。目标本身是不够的,你必须有一个跟进目标的过程。
5f1f8cb05661.original: Winners and losers have the same goal. Goals by themselves are not enough, you have to have a process by which you follow up on the goals.

c2d91aa1984d.text: 所以第一点是设立团队目标,不要超过一步公司目标。不要让它被层层递进到无关紧要的地步。
c2d91aa1984d.original: So the first is in setting team goals, no more than one step away from company goals. Don't let it get cascaded into oblivion.

5d9eb858013c.text: 所以预演是不错,但前提是你要设置好终止标准。要承诺在看到那些信号的时候采取行动。
5d9eb858013c.original: So a pre-mortem, it's great only if you set up kill criteria. Commit to actions that you're going to take if you see those signals.

1fa057a95109.text: 产品已不再是那些我们开始发布的静态制品,只需要创意、解决问题、发布,再稍微改进一下就能拥有一个仪表盘。现在整个关键绩效指标变成了产品团队的代谢能力,能够吸收数据,消化奖励模型,并产生一些结果。
1fa057a95109.context: 在AI产品开发中,"奖励模型"是一个评估和评分产品成果的系统,"消化"它意味着处理并行动于其反馈。
1fa057a95109.original: All of a sudden products aren't just like these static artifacts that we start to ship that's not just like, 'Hey, come up with an idea or an insight. Go solve a problem, ship it into the world, maybe make it a little bit better and then have a dashboard.' All of a sudden, the whole KPI is what is the metabolism of a product team to be able to ingest data and then digest the rewards model and then create some sort of outcome?
1fa057a95109.originalContext: In AI product development, a "rewards model" is a system that evaluates and scores product outcomes, and "digesting" it means processing and acting on its feedback.

8419ac070b46.text: 从80%的性能提升到90%,再到99%,再到99.9%,这其中存在很大差异。未来一两年内,模型将自动完成平均六级软件工程师60%的工作。再过几年会达到90%,之后又需要几年才能达到99%。
8419ac070b46.original: I think there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance. Within the next one or two years, the models are going to automate 80% of the average L6 software engineer's job. It's going to take another few years to move to 90%, and another few to 99%.

feb5a57e07f4.text: 把SEO视为一个产品。负责SEO的产品经理应该思考这个问题,因为它是一个产品问题。

374aa2907afc.text: 我确实认为我们需要更多创新。增加数据、GPU和更大的当前模型架构还有很大提升空间,但我绝对认为我们需要更多创新。
374aa2907afc.context: "缩放损失"似乎是一个录音错误 - 很可能应该说"缩放规律",这指的是随着数据、计算能力和模型规模的增加,AI模型性能呈现的可预测模式。
374aa2907afc.original: I definitely think we need more innovations. I think scaling loss of more data, more GPUs, and bigger current model architecture is there's still a lot to be done there, but I absolutely think we need to innovate more.
374aa2907afc.originalContext: "Scaling loss" appears to be a transcription error - likely meant to say "scaling laws," which refer to predictable patterns in AI model performance as you increase data, compute, and model size.

cd47000bb950.text: 我们希望确保我们提出的数字一定能达成,这使我们在估值较低方面承担了一些稀释。从这一点建立的信任,意味着当我们告诉人们会做某事时,他们会坚信我们一定会做到。
cd47000bb950.original: We wanted to make sure that we put forth numbers that we knew were going to hit, and that cost us some dilution upfront in the form of lower valuations. f08f12bf0eb1.text: 我认为越早越好,就像在我加入之前就已经改变品牌。能否让我更改名称是我加入的标准。总的来说,越早越好,但显然要在你知道已经找到产品市场契合,并有可扩展的东西之后,否则你不会想投入太多精力去建设一个最终可能无法让你达到目标的品牌。
