a4f8ef0606a1.text: 每个人都在关注通过'漏斗'各个阶段的绝对人数。所以不是我试图去转化一大堆人,而是转化率,而是我只是想让更多人被激活。一旦你开始这样思考,你就会意识到实际上有时候让更多人进入的最好方法就是让更多人进门。
a4f8ef0606a1.context: Archie在讨论Shopify的转化漏斗优化,团队专注于推动用户通过注册到激活等各个阶段。
a4f8ef0606a1.original: Everyone is thinking about absolute number of people who made it through their 'stage' of the funnel. So instead of I'm trying to convert a bunch of people, a conversion rate, I just want more people to get activated. And then once you start thinking that way, you realize actually the best way to get more people to get to a step sometimes, and often they just get more people in the door in the first place.
a4f8ef0606a1.originalContext: Archie is discussing conversion funnel optimization at Shopify, where teams focus on moving users through stages like signup to activation.

f0ab638d9880.text: 当团队自然地将世界划分为不同的漏斗阶段或不同的旅程点时,很容易过度关注我在漏斗中的那一部分以及通过该部分的转化率。然后团队就会把这个转化率作为他们的北极星来优化。但实际上,通常情况下仅仅让前一步更难就能够提高你的转化率。
f0ab638d9880.original: When you have teams naturally break up the world into different funnel stages or different points in the journey, it gets very seductive to look at my part of the funnel and what's my conversion rate through that part of the funnel, right? And then the team starts to optimize for that conversion rate as their north star. But in practice, it's actually almost always easier to just make it harder to do the thing right before your step in the funnel to increase your conversion rate.

19f36132e7d1.text: 提高我的注册到激活的最简单方法就是让注册更困难。当团队专注于这种局部转化率时,会导致很多奇怪的团队激励,因为他们实际上是在优化于隐含地让前一步更加困难。
19f36132e7d1.context: Archie在讨论为什么Shopify在衡量跨不同漏斗阶段的团队业绩时,更关注绝对数字而非转化率。
19f36132e7d1.original: The easiest way to increase my signup to activated thing is just make it harder to sign up. Nuts and bolts, that will always happen is when you have teams on that local conversion rates, you get all these weird team incentives, because they're optimizing to basically implicitly make it harder to do the step before them.
19f36132e7d1.originalContext: Archie is discussing why Shopify focuses on absolute numbers rather than conversion rates when measuring team performance across different funnel stages.

abf51e1e3718.text: 其中存在一个根本性的缺陷,那就是你关注的是成本而不是获得的价值。因此,当你专注于降低客户获取成本(CAC)时,往往会做一些非常有害的事情,即你成功降低了CAC,但实际上引入的客户价值更低,因为你只能以较低的CAC吸引到这些客户。
abf51e1e3718.original: There's a fundamental flaw to it which obviously is that you're focusing on cost and not the value derived. And so when you focus on CAC and reducing CAC, what tends to happen is you actually might be doing something very damaging where you're succeeding in reducing CAC, but you're actually bringing in customers that are less valuable because those are the ones that you're able to attract with a lower CAC.

2eaf5654dbf5.text: 归因分析并非一蹴而就,而是一个持续的探索过程。任何声称自己掌握了单一信息源的真理的人、模型或工具都是不准确的。
2eaf5654dbf5.original: The advice is that there's no single source of truth. Anyone who claims that they are a single source of truth, whether it's an individual, a model that they've created, or a tool that they've created, is not being accurate. The approach that works to attribution is that it's an ongoing investigation and it never stops.

e91dcbe722d1.text: 基于点击的归因分析或数字化归因分析都过于依赖基于Cookie的数据,并未真正揭示媒体投放与业务结果之间的因果关系,只能提供相关性洞见。要确定因果关系,唯有通过受控实验。
e91dcbe722d1.original: Click based attribution or the digital attribution were all fawning over cookie based and click based... it never demonstrated a causal relationship between our media spend and business results. It was only good for correlative insights. And the only way to determine causality is through real controlled experiments.

407c9768e430.text: 即便其他营销手段有效,付费获客也很可能奏效。但大多数公司都有一个错误认知,以为付费渠道的数据就能提供完整的归因洞见,这是错误的。

The issue for most companies is in this incorrect assumption that the data that is provided through paid channels allows you to have full end-to-end understanding of attribution. 7c44e393c13b.text: 我现在更关注营销人员如何利用概率型数据来做决策,因为我大部分工作都在说,我们无法获得某个受众群体或用户来源的确定性数据,那么如何利用其他信息构建模型,覆盖总体的30%,并借此外推到整体情况。

a973c7f82ca1.text: 保留率是一个非常糟糕的目标指标。在短时间内很难在这方面取得有意义的进展。最终,你要找到一个短期可衡量的指标,可以推动长期输出。
a973c7f82ca1.original: Retention is a terrible thing to goal on. It's almost impossible to drive in a meaningful way in a short term. Ultimately, you want to find a short-term metric you can measure that drives a long-term output.

5c9a048bccae.text: 我认为稍微更加可行的指标是一个稍微更难定义,但在我看来要有效得多的指标。这就是我所谓的市场健康指标,基本上就是可以最好地预测你的流动性的代理指标。
5c9a048bccae.original: The metric that I think is slightly more actionable is a little harder to define, but so much more helpful in my opinion. It's what I call a market health metric, and this is basically think of your proxy that is the best predictor of your liquidity.

1ab8e445c9bd.text: 其实并不存在所谓的长反馈循环。你可以选择缩短反馈循环的方法,就是找出那些与你最终想要的结果相关的因素。
1ab8e445c9bd.original: There is no such thing as a long feedback loop. And the way you choose to shorten the feedback loop is to say, what are the things that are correlated with the outcome that I eventually desire?

334b0e2934ec.text: 我们在自己的增长引擎上确定了这些因素。这种识别这些因素的过程是公司发展中如此关键的一刻,因为它让公司意识到,'好的,我们需要花时间关注如何测量这些因素,然后如何改善每一个因素?'

0acd16f843d8.text: A/B 测试很棒,但很少能告诉你为什么会出现这种变化。你不需要猜测。我认识一个人可以给你一个答案。
0acd16f843d8.original: AB tests are great, but the AB test rarely tells you why it changed in the way it did. You don't have to guess. I know somebody who can get you an answer.

486794a6bf68.text: 我们只改了七个字符就让 Airbnb 赚到了数百万美元,因为我们发现的问题非常简单。那个按钮感觉太吓人了。按钮上的呼吁行动感觉太吓人了。
486794a6bf68.original: We changed seven characters and made Airbnb millions of dollars, because what we found out was really simple. The button feels scary. The CTA on the button feels scary.

cffaa10d71a9.text: 能够识别各种微观和宏观的反馈循环,了解它们之间的联系,并用定性模型来传达对于如何实现增长的共同认知,这真的很强大。然后再用定量数据来指导季度目标,确保能有意识地投资,这就成为一个很大的推动力。
cffaa10d71a9.original: Being able to identify the various micro and macro loops, how they're all connected, being able to document them in a qualitative model to communicate a shared understanding of how you grow, it's really powerful. Augmenting that then with the quantitative side of things that helps guide quarter to quarter focus and ensure you can be intentional about where you're investing, that becomes a big enabler.

6464d73198e2.text: 我认为很多人过早地进行 A-B 测试,因为他们从未做过任何错误分析。如果你要进行 A-B 测试,而且是基于我们今天展示的实际错误分析,那就太棒了,去做吧。但如果你只是根据你认为重要的假设来做,那我建议你重新考虑一下。
6464d73198e2.context: 错误分析是指系统地检查 AI 系统失败的原因,识别模式和根源,这是演讲者之前演示过的。
6464d73198e2.original: I think a lot of people prematurely do A-B tests, because they've never done any error analysis in the first place. If you're going to do A-B tests and they're powered by actual error analysis as we've shown today, then that's great, go do it. But if you're just going to do them based on what you hypothetically think is what is important, then I would encourage people to go and rethink that.
6464d73198e2.originalContext: Error analysis refers to systematically examining AI system failures to identify patterns and root causes, which the speakers demonstrated earlier in their presentation.

df273b4f6298.text: 不要把收集指标当作娱乐。它不是用来让你说'哦,这很有趣,多新颖'然后不采取行动的。所以真正有价值的信息是那些能改变你在现实世界中所做事情的信息。
df273b4f6298.original: Do not treat metric gathering as entertainment. It's not there for you to be like, 'Oh, that's interesting, how novel,' and then not act on it. So real news is information that changes what you do in the real world.

766cad5ad2c5.text: 真正有价值的信息是那些能改变你在现实世界中所做事情的信息。如果你不改变自己的行动,你所做的只是在获取娱乐。
766cad5ad2c5.original: Real news is information that changes what you do in the real world. And if you don't change what you're doing, what you are doing is just getting entertainment.

0f6adb283da4.text: 只有当你明白'为什么'的时候,这种洞见才会带来价值。为什么这个人会做这件事?了解了原因,你就会采取不同的行动。
0f6adb283da4.context: 这里的'这个'指的是从数据指标中获得的洞见 - 了解用户行为背后的原因,而不仅仅是观察发生了什么。
0f6adb283da4.original: The insight will provide value when you have this, why answered? Why is this person doing this thing? Here's why. And then you are going to act differently.
0f6adb283da4.originalContext: "This" refers to insights derived from data measurements - understanding the "why" behind user behaviors rather than just observing what happened.

08677e92add7.text: 评估的目的是为了指导产品开发。我认为评估很有帮助,因为它能帮你发现进展顺利的机会。
08677e92add7.context: '评估'指的是用于系统地测试和衡量AI模型在不同指标和用户群中表现的框架。
08677e92add7.original: The goal of eval is to guide the product development. So you see eval, because I think I'm a big fan of eval, is that it helps you uncover opportunities where the progress are doing well.
08677e92add7.originalContext: "Eval" refers to evaluation frameworks used to systematically test and measure AI model performance across different metrics and user segments.

790d748bcfbc.text: 什么是一个出色的增长引擎和增长团队呢?那就是你制定了文化,设定了简单明确的北极星指标,通常一个,最多两个。你培养了一种基于数据定义假设的文化,并培养了一种能够快速执行和拥抱MVP心态的文化,无论是产品还是非产品项目,人们都可以快速失败和学习,快速迭代。
790d748bcfbc.original: What a great growth engine and a great growth team is one that where you set the culture, set very simple north star metrics, usually one, at most two. And you've created a culture of defining hypotheses that are data driven and a culture where that can be executed quickly and have an MVP mentality for product and non-product projects where people can fail and learn quickly and iterate quickly.

48dd2553e959.text: 当你建立一个增长团队并聘请合适的增长负责人时,他们会开始提出所有正确的问题,因为增长型产品经理的典型特征就是'等等,为什么会这样?让我们收集X、Y和Z方面的数据吧。'
48dd2553e959.original: When you build a growth team and you hire the right growth leader, they start asking all the right questions because when the archetype of person who is a growth PM will be like, 'Well, wait. Why is this happening? And let's get the data on X, Y and Z thing.'

ef2448e058cc.text: 除非你有至少数万用户,否则数学和统计学在你关心的大多数指标上都无法奏效。请在拥有数万用户时开始实验。在此之前,先建立文化,搭建平台,进行整合。
ef2448e058cc.original: Unless you have at least tens of thousands of users, the math, the statistics just don't work out for most of the metrics that you're interested in. Start experimenting when you're in the tens of thousands of users. Below that, start building the culture, start building the platform, start integrating.

b2e79fb19606.text: 作为产品经理的挑战在于,每个人都认为自己可以胜任这份工作。一旦你建立了实验机制,就已经使之具有了科学性。
b2e79fb19606.original: The challenge with being a product manager is, everybody thinks they can do the job. The moment you build experimentation, you've now made it scientific.

8e564869f35f.text: 对于使用这个指标我会保持开放和灵活的态度。指标的稳定性很好,可以帮助建立势头和专业知识,但有时我们会过于专注于选择完美的北极星指标,等到你觉得找到了完美的指标时,实际上已经是时候转向不同的机会了。
8e564869f35f.original: I would be open-minded about being dynamic and changing that metric over time. Stability in metric is great, it helps with momentum, it helps with building expertise, but sometimes we overfocus on picking the perfect north star metric and by the time you feel like you've found the perfect one, it's actually time to move on to something different and work on a different opportunity.

e70219741481.text: 收入对于公司来说更加重要,但也更远离增长团队直接影响的范畴。在Instacart,我们的增长北极星指标是每月活跃订单量。这就是我们每天关注和共同努力的目标。
e70219741481.original: Revenue is, for better or worse, more important to the company, but also much farther down the line of whether or not the growth team can directly impact that. And so at Instacart, for example, our north star metric for growth was monthly active orders. And that's what we all rallied around and looked at every day.

134c5f90dfe8.text: 我们通过财务和数据团队制定了一个将每个团队的指标转化为每月活跃订单量的机制。如果你的结账流程让一个客户多下一个周订单,它会对公司的每月活跃订单量产生一定影响,我们会将所有项目计划以及预期影响都归结到这个单一的每月活跃订单指标上。
134c5f90dfe8.context: 每月活跃订单量(MAO)是Instacart的增长北极星指标。
134c5f90dfe8.original: We created via the finance and data team, a translation layer for every team's metric into MAO. It would be like if you got one extra weekly order because of your checkout flow from the same customer, it would have point X impact on the company's MAO and then you would just roll up all project plans as well as project impact back into this singular MAO metric.
134c5f90dfe8.originalContext: MAO refers to Monthly Active Orders (or Monthly Active Orderers), which was Instacart's north star growth metric.

898bc9582151.text: 如果你不知道如何推动某个特定指标,那么正确的目标应该是提高你对此的理解,而不是去直接推动该指标。
898bc9582151.original: If you don't understand how to move a particular metric, then the right goal is to set a goal to increase your understanding not to move that metric.

f66367881f0c.text: 增长掩盖了所有问题。当你拥有令人难以置信的增长时,你并不真正了解哪些方面发展顺利,哪些方面出现问题。
f66367881f0c.original: Growth masks all problems. You don't really have a true understanding of what is working well and what is not working well when you have incredible growth.

e3692f7353ce.text: 我认为很多快速增长的公司目前并没有很好地利用数据。这些公司完全依靠良好的直觉和良好的感觉,但最终总会出现增长停滞的情况。
e3692f7353ce.original: I don't actually think a lot of the fast growing companies are using data well at this point. These companies are totally getting by on just good instincts and good vibes, but what always happens is eventually things stop growing.

e05467f7fc02.text: 指标的危险性。当你面临从零到一的情况时,如果过早地决定某个指标,这在本质上就是错误的精确性。我是说,点击率。当你只有一千名用户时,它根本没有任何意义。
e05467f7fc02.original: The danger of metrics. When you're looking at something zero-to-one. If you decide on a metric too prematurely, that's false precision first of all, right? I mean, CTR. When you have a thousand people, it doesn't mean anything.

767642c5aabc.text: 以米罗(Miro)为例,如果你经历他们的启用体验并注册使用,他们会问很少的问题,非常针对性。他们让你直接开始,询问你的用例,你是来做头脑风暴会议还是制定路线图?然后他们就快速给你提供模板,让你在5分钟内完成从网站注册到使用所需的全部流程。
767642c5aabc.original: Think about Miro, as an example. If you go through their activation experience and sign up to usage, they ask very limited questions, very targeted. They drop you, kind of, they ask you about your use case, what are you here for? Are here to do a brainstorm session? Are you here to develop a roadmap? And they quickly gave you templates to get started. Just like in maybe five minutes, you finish the entire journey from go to the website and sign up, answer a few questions, and you are already using the template they provided to do the thing you want to do.

ff1cc5aae654.text: 尽量不要命名产品功能。在实践中很容易这样做,虽然在理论上听起来很简单。
ff1cc5aae654.context: 演讲者建议不要在新手引导中直接命名产品功能,而是解释其价值或好处。
ff1cc5aae654.original: Try not to name features. It can be very tempting in practice, even though it sounds easy in theory.
ff1cc5aae654.originalContext: The speaker is advising against literally naming product features in onboarding tooltips, instead recommending explaining the value or benefit to users.

45a03374d416.text: 我很喜欢那种不是贴在体验之上,而是利用产品本身来教用户如何使用产品的做法。
45a03374d416.original: I really like something that is not pasted on top of the experience but something that uses the product to teach someone else how to use the product.

4106a58da0ca.text: 我们有一些非常棒的高级功能,比如Airtable的自动化功能。但是用户并不一定需要从第一天就学习这些高级功能。在他们还没有看过工作流程之前,他们并不需要去学习这些高级内容。
4106a58da0ca.original: We have some awesome advanced features of really cool stuff you can do with Airtable, automations being a great example. However, users don't necessarily need to get that started on day one. They don't need to learn about the advanced stuff when they haven't even looked at a workflow before.

fee7dee35021.text: 真的要努力去思考,一个买家手中、一个买家家中的情景是什么样的?这也许可以给下一个购买者更多信心,了解它的尺寸和颜色是否合适。
fee7dee35021.original: Really trying to lean into, well, what does it look like in a buyer's hand, in a buyer's home? Maybe that gives the next purchaser a bit more confidence that it's the right size, it's the right color, whatever it might be.

959bbc836be9.text: 对我们来说,重要的是迈出第一步,特别是对Canva这样的创意工具来说。人们对白色页面都存在一种恐惧。所以在任何新手引导思考之前,我们就有一个白色页面。我们有几个小贴士,告诉人们这里可以做什么,那里可以做什么。但是人们还是会被留在这个白色页面上而感到恐慌。
959bbc836be9.original: For us, it was taking that first step, particularly with Canva and any I think creative tool. There's a real fear of the blank page. So prior to any onboarding thought from us, we had a blank page. We had a few coach marks that said, 'Here's where you do this, here's where you do this.' And then they'd be left on this blank page and people would freak out.

4a15f1270342.text: 经过多年测试,我们得出的口语化表述是:'我从未想到自己也能成为设计师。'这就是我们通过不断完善新手引导流程所实现的,即降低进入门槛,同时提升用户的愉悦感。
4a15f1270342.original: The words that we literally got out of years at testing were, I didn't know I could be a designer. And that was what we managed to do through several rounds of refinement on the onboarding process. It is lowering the barriers to entry and also increasing the amount of delight.

83e715e82d8c.text: 坏的阻力很糟糕,而好的阻力很有帮助。没有什么是简单的,所有阻力都是坏的这种说法是错误的。
83e715e82d8c.context: 劳拉·沙费尔在讨论Twilio的一个实验时提出,加入注册问题意外增加了转化率,这挑战了人们对用户阻力的假设。
83e715e82d8c.original: Bad friction is bad, and good friction is good. There's no such thing as it being simple. It's just all friction is bad.
83e715e82d8c.originalContext: Laura was discussing an experiment at Twilio where adding signup questions unexpectedly increased conversion, challenging assumptions about user friction.

1dcb3bd6c0ca.text: 我们几乎创造了一种人工阻力,来帮助区分用户是真心想要还是仅仅需要某件事。如果用户没有填写那份问卷调查,也许他们实际上在寻找别的东西。
1dcb3bd6c0ca.original: So we almost create this artificial friction to help differentiate how deeply a user wants something or needs something. And if the user doesn't fill out that questionnaire, maybe they're actually looking for something else.

97a8acab9697.text: 我们实际上在注册流程中增加了更多的阻力,帮助用户更好地思考自己的需求。通过这样做,我们实际上帮助他们更快地完成首次购买。
97a8acab9697.original: We actually put more friction in the onboarding flow to help to start to solve for that. So we actually slowed you down. We made you be more thoughtful about what you were listing. And by doing that, we actually helped you get to a first sale faster.

f1c9219e1098.text: 不要跳过那些注册问题。它们并不会降低注册完成率,而那些在填写个人信息环节退出的用户,本来就是意向较低的。
f1c9219e1098.original: Do not skip those onboarding questions. No, they do not detract for your onboarding completion rates and people that do drop off in the profiling stage, they were low intent anyways.

b4916e8e691e.text: 在Writely刚开始的时候,我们甚至都不要求输入电子邮件地址,因为那是一个全新的东西。我们不想在注册过程中添加任何阻力。所以你可以直接进来创建文档,开始使用,不需要告诉我们任何关于自己的信息。大约2分钟后,如果你还在这里,我们会非常温和地说,'请给我们您的电子邮箱,不需要密码或其他任何信息。'
b4916e8e691e.context: Writely是Sam Schillace创办的基于网页的文字处理软件,后来被谷歌收购并成为Google文档。
b4916e8e691e.original: When we did Writely at the beginning, we didn't even ask for an email address, because it was such a novel thing. We didn't want any friction at all in the onboarding process. So you could just come in and make a document and start using it without telling us anything at all about yourself. And after about two minutes of typing, if you're still there, we'd very gently just say, 'Please give us your email address, no password, no anything.'
b4916e8e691e.originalContext: Writely was Sam Schillace's web-based word processor startup that was later acquired by Google and became Google Docs.

482b67b8d4f9.text: 完全去除步骤或简化到失去产品身份和功能的地步,这是一种彻底失败的增长策略。
482b67b8d4f9.original: Just removing steps or yanking or simplifying things to an oblivion where you lose an identity of what you even do or what you're capable of doing is a completely failed growth tactic.

ff230f76d31c.text: 从更高层面来说,这就像采用以产品为导向的市场推广策略,你的产品工作就是增加收入,人员只是一个后备方案,而不是主要方式。
ff230f76d31c.original: At the highest level, it's like taking a go-to-market approach where your product job is to grow revenue and you use humans as a backstop and not the other way around.

967a1257e13d.text: 产品引领增长的核心就是让你的产品传达企业的价值主张,即使你还无法建立一个强大且复杂的实验实践,也仍能实现这一目标。
967a1257e13d.context: 产品引领增长(PLG)是一种商业策略,产品本身带动客户获取和扩展,而不是依赖传统的销售团队。
967a1257e13d.original: PLG at its core is just having your product sell the value prop of what your business does, and you can still deliver on that without being able to stand up a very robust and sophisticated experimentation practice.
967a1257e13d.originalContext: PLG stands for Product-Led Growth, a business strategy where the product itself drives customer acquisition and expansion rather than traditional sales teams.

741147b5510a.text: 产品入门流程可以替代销售和账户管理团队,服务于数百万客户。关键在于如何让这个流程接近并友好亲和如同人工服务一般。
741147b5510a.original: Onboarding is a substitute for sales and all these account management teams for millions of customers. The task is how do you make it approximate a human and how friendly a human is and how approachable a human is?

ce5d1ed635e6.text: 关键是找出当没有人陪伴时,用户是如何体验到产品价值的,这种价值不一定需要涵盖产品的全部功能。
ce5d1ed635e6.original: The key is to figure out what it would be like for someone to experience value when there's no human sitting next to them, and that value doesn't have to be full functionality of the product.

c86f17f63128.text: 你可能应该从产品激活开始。对大多数B2B软件来说,产品激活是一个很好的切入点,因为历史上B2B软件并不是为了快速入门而设计的。
c86f17f63128.original: You should probably start with activation. Activation is actually a common good starting place for most B2B software. Because usually B2B softwares are not designed to really get you to use quickly, historically.

7dcf6a1923c0.text: 我们都倾向于当下偏好,这意味着我们会优先照顾当下的自己而非未来的自己,所以有很多原因会让您的客户、用户采取某种行动,但您实际上必须给他们一个今天就采取行动的理由。
7dcf6a1923c0.original: We are all present bias, which means we prioritize our present self over our future self, so there are plenty of reasons that somebody, your customer, your user should take an action, but you actually have to give them a reason to take an action today.

c8663b21522e.text: 您可能会注册使用One Medical服务,六个月后生了病,但您是否会记得六个月前注册的这个应用程序?可能不会。您会采取之前的做法,打电话给您惯常就诊的医生。
c8663b21522e.original: You're going to sign up for One Medical, six months later, you're going to get a fever and get sick, and are you going to remember this app that you signed up for six months ago? Probably not. You're going to do the same thing you did before, which is call the doctor that you've normally gone to.

cc51b1b2a80f.text: 通常这发生在养成习惯的引导体验中。是什么让人真正理解产品价值,那第一个'啊哈'时刻?令人震惊的是,许多团队都不太清楚对他们来说那个时刻是什么。
cc51b1b2a80f.original: Usually it's somewhere in the onboarding to habit-building experience. What does it take for someone to actually understand the value, that first moment, that first aha moment in the product? And a lot of teams, it's shocking how many teams don't really understand what that moment is for them.

cd5295a1ef9d.text: 我想大约70%的人只登录过一次应用程序或产品就再也不回来了。这真是令人难以置信。所以很多公司没有某种唤回或重新参与的机制,这一直让我很吃惊。
cd5295a1ef9d.original: I think it's like 70% of people log into an app, log into a product once and never come back. It's wild. So the fact that so many companies don't have some sort of win back or re-engagement always blows my mind.

2f60aa4f1fc6.text: 我们称之为'正确的错误',做正确的事却出于错误的原因,正确的事可能是完成流程,但错误的原因是为了让那个报错消失。
2f60aa4f1fc6.original: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.

2ab1f4213058.text: 我们发现根据客户的学习方式和建设方式对客户进行细分要比使用更传统的细分方式（如你是营销人员还是产品经理还是运营人员）更有效。
2ab1f4213058.original: We found bucketing customers by their learning style and their building style was more effective than more classic segmentation, like do you work in marketing, do you work in product management, do you work in operation.

25a106a966b3.text: 一般来说,你在注册流程中收集的信息应该比大多数人认为的更多。如果你能利用这些信息来个性化指导,这对于SaaS产品来说很有帮助,比如Shopify在用户入职时提供的指导。
25a106a966b3.context: 此处以Shopify为例说明SaaS产品的用户入职指导,并非针对Shopify产品本身的建议。
25a106a966b3.original: You usually want to collect more information than most people think you do in your sign up flow. If you can then leverage that to personalize the guidance. And this is for SaaS product, the guidance that someone can get when they onboard into Shopify.
25a106a966b3.originalContext: Shopify is used here as a general example of SaaS onboarding, not advice specific to Shopify's product.

ba652d6d2f89.text: 我们确实有一个Slack集成,可以收集任何注册Airtable的人的大量信息,包括他们的头衔、所在公司等。我们还有一个小按钮,可以让我们立即给认为值得联系的人发邮件。
ba652d6d2f89.original: We literally had a Slack integration that we pulled in a whole bunch of information about anyone who signed up for Airtable, including their title, the company that they worked at, et cetera. And literally would sit there and had a little button in each of the records that would allow us to email them immediately if we had decided that they might be someone we want to talk to.

26bb4f8bb31e.text: 我们甚至还没碰注册后的体验,试用转付费率就增加了40%,这仅仅是因为通过门的客户更合适、更合适。
26bb4f8bb31e.original: We didn't even touch anything after the signup experience. We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it. It was just because a more qualified, better fit customer was coming through the door.

497f727c70c0.text: 所以我谈到了使用司机销售GoPay。在那之前,我们做的一件事是,实际上将某人的虚拟账号号码放在信用卡图片上。你知道什么是信用卡,这对你来说很熟悉。很多人不知道什么是数字钱包。
497f727c70c0.original: So I talked about using drivers to sell GoPay. Before that, one thing that we did was to actually take someone's virtual account number and put it onto a picture of a credit card. You know what a credit card is, that's familiar to you. A lot of people didn't know what a digital wallet was.

fdc655ca4c40.text: 我觉得GPT很酷的一点是,你可以把它包装成'这就是AI可以很好解决的一个非常具体的问题',然后我可以与你分享这种体验,现在你可以去尝试这个GPT,让它真正解决问题,你会说'哇,它为我做了这件事。我应该花时间调查一下我有的这五个其他问题,看看AI是否也能成为这些问题的解决方案。'
fdc655ca4c40.original: I think the cool thing about GPTs is you can package down like, 'Here's this one very specific problem that AI can solve for you and do it really well,' and I can share that experience with you and now you can go and try that GPT, have it actually solve the problem and be like, 'Wow, it did this thing for me. I should probably spend the time to investigate these five other problems that I have to see if AI can also be a solution to those.'

5991d9d9dc1a.text: 我注意到一个现象,创始人以及人们普遍倾向于像PR人员一样写作,而不是像人一样写作...你的客户或用户如何向其他人描述你的产品呢?

dd93dc8f220d.text: 我们实际上看了他们朋友购买并喜欢的食物,把这作为数据集,'嘿,这是Lenny购买并喜欢的食物。也许你也会喜欢。'这就是我们用来黑掉信任因素的一种方式。

961255110915.text: 我们有一个例子,我们在购物车体验中添加了一些文字,结果出现了我们真的没有预料到的大幅提升。这更多是我们在传达我们作为企业的价值观,这似乎真的与我们的买家产生了共鸣。
961255110915.original: We had one example where we added some text to the cart experience, and we just saw huge uplift that we really, really didn't expect. It was more us communicating our values as a business, and it was something that really seemed to resonate with our buyers.

23c1493676d6.original: The text change was in our cart where we call out Etsy offsets carbon emissions from every delivery. f05ebaed7784.text: 最大的错误是,招聘一个增长负责人,却不给予任何资源,却期望他们能像变魔术一样解决问题。

c63807e7682a.original: You have to understand that people have really limited attention and no one cares about your product the way that you do. And so it can feel like you're dumbing it down or oversimplifying. And if you don't feel that way about your onboarding, about the growth work that you're doing, it's probably too complex.

d7362c0e93e2.text: 即使是在设计在线产品的最初阶段,也要想想'有人第一次来这里会是什么体验?我会要求他们集成什么?我会要求他们上传什么,或邀请其他人吗?用户要经历哪些步骤才能获得你应用的全部价值?'这是一个非常有用的思考角度。

c0f9754490ba.original: The amount of impact by just nailing those flows has never ceased to amaze me and setting up that person for long-term success. So monetary friction. Then just really good onboarding, personalization, a well of opportunities there.

86bb803d4455.text: 在dbt Labs,我们有一个核心价值观,即我们更关注于创造价值而非捕获价值。我们真的这么做了。当我们谈论dbt Labs对客户的价值时,他们常常说它的价值相当于他们在云数据仓库上支出的20%到35%。但我们向客户收取的费用只占这20%到35%的一小部分,这是有意为之的。

But what we charge our customers is a very small fraction of that 20 to 35% and that's by design.

22d9749b8f3c.original: To stop churn, you need to attract customers who won't leave. That sounds counterintuitive, but that's the best way to actually stop churn.

7a2d1f73aa5a.text: 这通常发生在转化之前的那一步。所以如果他们不确定用户为什么打开应用程序,或者他们不确定用户为什么会进入这个结账页面,这通常是某种方式上的复制或路径不够有效。
7a2d1f73aa5a.original: It's usually the step right before conversion. So if they aren't sure why the user opens the app or they aren't sure why the user got to this checkout page, it's often some copy or the path has been ineffective in some way.

b991c83ca765.text: 关注早期用户体验是非常有影响力的。你经常会看到产品团队说,我们应该关注唤回,因为我们有如此庞大的已流失用户池。如果我们能找回其中1%的用户,这将会产生巨大的提升。问题在于,这个用户池正是那些已经尝试过产品并决定不再使用它的人。
b991c83ca765.original: Working on early user experience is highly impactful. You often see product teams say we should work on resurrection because we have this huge pool of users that is churned out. If we get just 1% of those people back, it's going to be such a big lift. The problem is that pool of users is the group of people who has tried the product and decided they don't want to use it.

82620b8284fd.text: 很少应该直接去源头发送更多电子邮件或推送通知之类的东西。这真的是要了解客户的体验以及他们真正关心的是什么。
82620b8284fd.original: Rarely should you go right to the source and send them more email or push notification or something like that. It's really actually about understanding what is the customer experience and what matters to them.

c2ee9ce7ac6e.text: 你的心态应该几乎就像是在努力创造一个口碑传播机器。如果你能做好这一部分,其他一切都会变得容易得多。即使你有一个B2B产品,即使你不能告诉所有的朋友,你也应该告诉那些相关的同事。
c2ee9ce7ac6e.original: Your mindset should almost be like you're trying to create a word of mouth machine. If you can get that part right, everything else becomes significantly easier. And if you have any, and I think this applies to both prosumer, B2C, as well as even B2B products, if you have a B2B product, even if you're not telling all of your friends, you should be telling colleagues where that product is relevant.

b997b46ae053.text: 对于你的产品,必须要有这种近乎不理性的情感反应。内部员工必须真心热爱某些东西,才能真正支持它。但是在外部,如果人们能高声歌唱你的产品有多棒,那就是一个很棒的状态。
b997b46ae053.original: There has to be this almost irrational, emotional response to your product. People internally have to authentically love something to really stand behind it. But externally too, if people can sing at the top of their lungs about how great your product is, that's a wonderful place to be.

7a7623099557.text: 质量就是增长。如果你能想办法让你的产品更容易使用和更容易理解,当然会吸引更多人使用,使用更多,并且有更好的体验,他们也会愿意与他人分享。
7a7623099557.original: Quality is growth. And if you think about how you can make your product easier to use and more understandable, that will of course drive people to use it, and use more of it, and have a better experience with it that they'll want to talk about with others.

94cb9603c74b.text: 在推出会员推荐计划之前,Dropbox已经有了惊人的推荐率。现在有些公司想复制它,说'为什么没有人谈论这个产品?让我们添加一个有激励措施的推荐计划吧。'在我看来,当它已经有效运作时,这是一个很好的加速器,但如果人们不想谈论你的产品,它是无法解决问题的。
94cb9603c74b.original: Before the referral program, Dropbox had amazing referral rate. Companies that are trying to copy it are like, 'Why isn't anyone talking about a product? Let's add a referral program with incentives.' To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.

250bfdaf8e0e.text: 人们认为增长是一蹴而就的,但事实并非如此。它是一系列短期胜利和短期执行,最终达成长期目标,真正理解你有很多短期行动来实现长期成果。
250bfdaf8e0e.original: People think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain and really understanding you have a lot of short terms towards the longer-term outcomes.

618d4b71afde.text: 我总是首先着眼于人们为什么使用这个产品,以及哪些领域存在增长潜力?通常即使在一个大型产品或成熟复杂系统中,也会有某些部分在不断增长。
618d4b71afde.original: The first thing I always do and think about is you get in touch in terms of why are people using this product, and where are the areas of growth? And so usually even in a big product or a mature in a complex system, there's a part of it that's growing.

d93b875eed03.text: 一旦你进入这个圈子,就可以获得首选供应商的地位。你现在可以跨界进入其他业务部门。
d93b875eed03.original: Once you are in, you are in. Once you are in, you are now a preferred vendor. You now have the ability to cross over into other business units.

f3a7d4039bb5.text: 不要过快过大地增长。我们实际上很仔细地思考了什么样的健康增长速度是最合适的。如果你迅速发展到拥有5000名代理商,这听起来确实很不错,但实际对话效果反而会受到抑制,因为人们会感觉自己在对着一个礼堂讲话。
f3a7d4039bb5.original: Not growing it so big so fast. One thing that we actually thought about pretty carefully was what a rate of healthy growth would be. If you grow to something like, oh we have 5,000 ambassadors, which feels really good to say on a website, the conversation is actually very muted because people feel like they're speaking to an auditorium.

0cf709bb7cd3.text: 我们真的专注于一个关键指标来追踪我们的增长或表现情况。我们称之为D5、D7。许多其他公司称之为L5、L7。但其人性化解释是每周至少有多少人使用Arc五天?这就是我们从指标角度唯一关注的,因为对我们来说,它概括了留存、参与度和增长。
0cf709bb7cd3.original: We really focus on one key metric as it relates to tracking our growth or how we are doing. We call it D5, D7. A lot of other companies call it L5, L7. But the human explanation for that is how many people turn to Arc at least five days a week? That is all we obsess over from a metrics perspective, because for us it captures retention, engagement, and growth in a single metric.

8f130e34148d.text: 没有任何自然力量会推动公司在其旅程的早期就关注最终用户的享受和成功。如果组织中没有人真正的激励是要衡量他们的最终用户的成功、享受、满意度、留存和参与度,这是不会发生的。
8f130e34148d.original: There is no natural force that pulls companies towards thinking about the end user's enjoyment and success early in their journey. If there is nobody in the organization whose true incentive is to measure their end user success, their enjoyment, their happiness, their retention, their engagement early on, it will not happen.

aab0da611997.text: 当你考虑留存时,这还不够具体。所以我使用了一个来自《讲好故事》一书的心理模型,他们会告诉你:'Lenny,想想世界上所有橙色的东西。'你会说:'橙子。还有什么?'然后如果你改变这个结构,把它限定在建筑工地里的所有橙色物品,你就会真正意识到并抓住具体的概念。
aab0da611997.context: 《讲好故事》是一本关于如何让想法更容易记住的书;'沙盒'结构是指添加限制条件,使思考更加具体和具体。
aab0da611997.original: When you think about retention, that's just not specific enough. So there is this mental model that I use from made to stick where they'll tell you like, 'Lenny, think of everything in the world that is orange.' And you're like, 'An orange. What else?' And then if you change that structure with sandbox to think of everything orange that's in a construction site, then you really start to realize and grasp at concrete concepts.
aab0da611997.originalContext: "Made to Stick" is a book about making ideas memorable; the "sandbox" structure refers to adding constraints to make thinking more specific and concrete.

da3f15d85ade.text: 这些模型的绝大多数都没有考虑到获客之后的留存、扩展等因素。所以总之来说,销售漏斗是有问题的。
da3f15d85ade.context: 传统的营销和销售模型通常关注客户获取指标,如销售漏斗的转化率,而不是衡量购买后发生的情况。
da3f15d85ade.original: The vast, vast majority of these models don't take post-acquisition, retention, expansion, all of that into account. So yeah, in a nutshell, funnels are bad.
da3f15d85ade.originalContext: Traditional marketing and sales models typically focus on customer acquisition metrics like conversion rates through sales funnels, rather than measuring what happens after purchase.

0f9436d04336.text: 看起来更漂亮的东西会增加信任。你可以看到我们在这上面下了很大的功夫,我们关心看得见的细节,这也给你保证我们也同样关心看不见的细节。
0f9436d04336.original: Things that are more beautiful, increase trust. You see that we've put painstaking detail into this, and we care about the details of how something works, and that gives you assurance that we care about other details that you can't see too.

b62a3975dd0e.text: 我实际上认为把品牌的光芒融入每一次互动,是我们增长策略的一个重要手段。我一直与团队讨论这个问题,因为这是我们增长故事中的一个重要杠杆。
b62a3975dd0e.original: I actually see it as part of growth strategy to make sure that that brand shines through every single interaction. And I always talk to my team about it, because that is one big lever in our growth story.

96d43ba161a3.text: 当你和整个团队都在使用Devin时,就像一个新加入的工程师一样。如果你是在第一天加入,和你在公司工作了五年、自己写了一半代码、触及了每个文件并构建了每一个部分、了解所有工程师的人相比,Devin会随着时间的推移而学习并建立起对你的代码库、技术栈和流程的深入理解,从而能够做出更多更有价值的贡献。
96d43ba161a3.context: Devin是认知实验室开发的一款能够自主编写和修改代码的AI软件工程助理。
96d43ba161a3.original: As you use Devin and as your whole team uses Devin, it's the same thing with an engineer. If you're joining on day one versus you've been at the company for five years, you wrote half the code yourself, you've touched every file you've built every single piece, you know all the engineers. And so similarly, it's like Devin will really learn and build its representation of your code base and of your stack and of your process over time and will be able to do a lot more with that.
96d43ba161a3.originalContext: Devin is an AI software engineering agent built by Cognition Labs that can write and modify code autonomously.

26aea30fe798.text: AI是终极的红娘。它被低估、被误解,但其实就是关于价值交换。如果我能够很好地实现这种价值交换,那么人们就会一次次回来并参与其中。
26aea30fe798.original: AI is the ultimate matchmaker. It's underutilized, it's misunderstood, it's really about value exchange. And if I'm able to do value exchange really well, then people will come back and they do and they engage.

b2bd1f43d095.text: 网络效应是指一个产品或者业务拥有越多用户或客户时就会越好。
b2bd1f43d095.original: A network effect is when a product or a business gets better with more users or customers using it.

e43b89919720.text: 我们每天发送两条与您的主要连续学习记录有关的通知,第一条是练习提醒,我们在您前一天练习后的23.5小时发送该通知。
e43b89919720.original: We send two notifications related to your core streak each day, the first is a practice reminder, we send it 23 and a half hours after you practice the day before.

233bebafab94.text: 因为人们非常关注自己的连续学习记录,这种提醒通知让他们觉得很积极,而不是消极的。
233bebafab94.original: Because people care about their streak, that notification reminding them, hey, come back and... People see this by and large as a positive notification and not a negative notification.

cadd2d963da8.text: 我们可以利用这些信息说:'卖家把它打折了。你应该回来看看。这个正在被抢购一空。只剩一件了。你已表现出了意向,也许你想回来买下它。'
cadd2d963da8.original: So what can we do with that information? We can then say, 'The seller put it on sale. You should come back and check it out. This is selling out. There's only one of this item left. You showed some intent, you might want to come back and get it.'

e0f392aef811.text: 我们的库存消耗速度远超补货能力,客户还在不断增加。我们还有约6天就无法为已经下单的客户提供服务。所以我们需要关闭网站,暂停业务增长。
e0f392aef811.original: We are depleting inventory far quicker than our ability to replenish and the customers keep coming. We have about six days before we get to a place where we won't be able to serve those who've already made a commitment to Bobbie. So we need to turn off our site and stop growing the business.

854c587443bf.text: 我们不得不做这件事。我们在2016年左右称之为'连接枢纽转型',我们需要说服Kevin和Mikey,优先服务名人并不是正确的做法,因为这基本上是自损而不利他人,因为普通用户体验并不理想。
854c587443bf.original: We had to do this thing. We called it the connections pivot, right in like 2016... where we had to convince Kevin and Mikey that it was actually not the right thing to do to prioritize celebrities to everybody because we were basically biting your nose to spite your face, because the regular person wasn't having a great experience.

f17c6cbd4c13.text: 即使某些情况并不常见,也并不意味着它们不重要。当发生导致客户流失的情况时,你就失去了所有后续订单,这不一定被观察到。
f17c6cbd4c13.original: Just because something doesn't happen frequently doesn't mean that it's not important. When you have things that cause churn, you're losing all of that consumer's subsequent orders, and that is not necessarily observed.

001e0d0ecf90.text: 这不是工程里程碑或设计里程碑,而是学习里程碑。所以我们构建某些东西的同时,也不断扩大了我们的构建范围。
001e0d0ecf90.original: It's not a engineering milestone or a design milestone, it's a learning milestone. So we build something and along the way we actually grow the scope of what we build.

edc7d03c8c05.text: 在交付速度和发现速度之间总存在权衡,这实际上引出了我们如何将两者结合的下一层问题。因为人们往往认为这是非此即彼的。
edc7d03c8c05.original: There's always like a trade-off between speed of delivery and speed of discovery, and that actually leads to the next layer of how do we combine the two? Because people tend to think it's an either/or.

c6624a1cd2cf.text: 我希望看到有人能够获取这些输入,并说出'这是路径。这就是我为什么会选择这条路径'的理由。然后是一些小的里程碑,让你判断'这是否有效?这是否没有效?'并据此做出不同的决策。
c6624a1cd2cf.original: I want to see someone be able to get those inputs, be able to say, 'This is the path. This is how I learned why I put this path together.' And then... what are the little milestones that make you say, 'Hey, is this working? Is this not working?' And then make you either make a different decision.

2999ea8983f0.text: 继续下注。同时开始进行一些探索,以便最终这些下注能更加精准。
2999ea8983f0.original: Keep making bets. In parallel, start doing some discovery so that eventually those bets get better.

99c985d3b87e.text: 你永远在交付,永远在发现。你培养的发现习惯越好,这些下注随着时间也会越来越准确。
99c985d3b87e.original: You're always delivering and you're always discovering. The more you build this discovery habit, the better those bets are going to get with time.

1414b16c006d.text: 明确由谁对结果负责的人也应该是决策者。我发现很多文献说产品团队应该是集体性的,最好的想法来自于每个人,这我认为是好意的,每个人当然都应该贡献想法。但是没有明确谁负责和谁做决定,这通常会大大拖慢执行。
1414b16c006d.original: Being very clear that whoever is accountable for the results should also be the decider. I found that a lot of literature out there says that product teams should be this communal best ideas come from everywhere group, which I think is well-intentioned and absolutely everyone should contribute ideas, but I think not having it be super clear who is accountable and who is deciding often slows down execution a lot.

98fee0095754.text: 一旦某个人做出了决定,就应该相信并跟随。没有升级的途径。如果你不是直接负责人,而是团队的一员,他们做出了决定,那就是时候加入并推进这个决定了。
98fee0095754.context: DRI是'直接负责个人'的缩写,指被指定为某个项目或倡议的最终决策者的单一个人。
98fee0095754.original: Once that person makes the call, it's disagree and commit time. There's no escalation path. If you're not the DRI and you're on the team and they made the call, all right. It's time to sign up and go forward on that decision.
98fee0095754.originalContext: DRI stands for "Directly Responsible Individual" - the single person designated as the final decision-maker for a project or initiative.

932b828cc368.text: 任何一件工作最多只能有三次审查,不能让其他人一直阻挡一个审批人。如果一个会议有超过10个人,我们会要求主持人把其他人踢出去,并写好决策记录。
932b828cc368.original: No more than three reviews on a given piece of work where people are blocking one approver. If a meeting has more than 10 people on it, we ask the person hosting the meeting to kick out the other people and write better decision notes.

ef5d4b821f48.text: 我们非常积极地确定谁负责什么级别的审查,并推动限制每个会议的人数以及某个工作的子任务审查数量。这做到了给予各工作小组更多的主动权和执行力。
ef5d4b821f48.original: We got really aggressive about, functionally, who is in charge and at what level for a given review, and pushed to say to actually have limits on the number of people per meeting, on the number of sub-task reviews for a given body of work. What this did is it created a lot more agency and pace within given working teams.

dbb16dba7270.text: 如果每个人都了解我们为什么这么做,要解决什么问题,那么人们就可以做出很棒的决定。这是你真正能扩展的唯一方式。
dbb16dba7270.original: If everyone has an understanding of why we're doing this, what problem we're solving, then people can make really great decisions. It's the only way you can really scale.

620d1d9a97e7.text: 业务中存在的流程唯一目的是降低风险。流程是为了减少系统输出的不稳定性。流程的弊端是会抑制创新。
620d1d9a97e7.context: 在金融界,alpha代表超额收益/创新,beta代表波动性/不可预测性。
620d1d9a97e7.original: Processes in a business exist for the sole purpose of lowering beta. Processes are for decreasing volatility in the output of the system. The downside of a process is that it suppresses alpha.
620d1d9a97e7.originalContext: Alpha refers to outperformance/innovation in finance; beta refers to volatility/unpredictability.

7971a1ac96e4.text: 流程本质上是减少差异的。你引入它是因为担心组织内部差异太大。你希望人们达到某个标准。但代价是,在提升下限的同时,也会拉低顶尖员工和最具创造力的思维者的水平。
7971a1ac96e4.original: Process, by definition, is variance reducing. You're introducing it, because you worry that the variance in your org is too high. You want people to sort of meet a certain standard. And the cost of that is obviously, while you are reducing the standard and bringing folks up to the average, you're also bringing other folks down to the average. And oftentimes, the folks you're bringing down are your highest performers, your most creative thinkers.

372326767722.text: 在一个封闭系统中,熵会随时间增加。公司的早期阶段是为了生存。第二阶段是防止停滞。第三阶段则是与复杂性作斗争。
372326767722.original: Within a closed system, entropy increases over time. In the early stages of a company, you're essentially fighting to survive. In the second phase of a company, you're trying not to stagnate. But then the third stage is you're fighting complexity.

1d1de0f359ad.text: 我开始称之为'最小可行流程'。我会给大家一个模板,但说'使用这个模板,但如果你想突破它,请随意这么做'。我现在会在模板的开头写这样的话:'如果这个模板不适合你的需求,不要使用它。但请知道这只是最基础的东西,我们只是设立了一个下限,你可以超越它。'
1d1de0f359ad.original: I've started referring to this as the MVP, the minimum viable process. So if I give folks a template, I'm like, 'Look, use the template. But if you want to break out of it, please absolutely do.' And I've started writing this at the top of templates now. 'If this doesn't work for what you're trying to explain, don't use it. But just know that this is the minimum viable thing. We're setting the bar here, but go higher if you can, please.'

a1fd5a4427f8.text: 一个有授权的产品团队能做到特性团队所能做的,甚至更多。有人会问,为什么特性团队就不够好?我的回答是,你究竟为什么而来?难道你真的不在乎你的客户对你的产品有什么想法吗?
a1fd5a4427f8.context: 自主的产品团队可以做到功能团队所做的一切,甚至更多。作者偶尔也会将某些任务分给功能团队。
a1fd5a4427f8.original: An empowered product team can do everything a feature team can do and more. And once in a while I do hear somebody say, why isn't it good enough to be a feature team? How do you answer that really? To me, it is like, why are you in this business? Do you really not care what your customers think about your product?
a1fd5a4427f8.originalContext: Feature teams are given pre-defined requirements to build, while empowered product teams have autonomy to discover and decide what problems to solve for customers.

c043feefbd9a.text: 这不是时间的估算，而是一种偏好,这是一种完全不同的方法。估算是指我们认为需要多长时间?相反，我们有偏好。我们对任何单个功能的偏好都不超过六周。本质上这就是我们愿意投入的预算。
c043feefbd9a.original: This is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite, which is a radically different approach. An estimate is like how long do we think it's going to take? We instead have appetites. Our appetite for any individual feature is no more than six weeks. Essentially that's our budget we're willing to spend.

890f6cba3279.text: 工作会扩展到可利用的时间。所以对我们来说这就是一种偏好。

If I can say, 'It's going to have this, this, this, this, this, and this,' and that's how we're going to let people see the empty spaces, that's a good indicator that it's clear enough that it's shaped well.
9fe17449fbcb.originalContext: In this product development framework, "shaping" means defining a feature's scope and approach, while "empty spaces" refers to available time slots in a calendar feature they were designing.

9beef06d108c.text: 使用自己的产品非常重要。我到达时公司是memo文化,我说我们应该变成ppt文化,因为可以用Figma制作这些ppt。这样做让你遇到很多问题并熟悉Figma的使用。
9beef06d108c.original: It's so important that you're using your own products. And I think we're in a very lucky position where all of us can get creative around using Figma in some way... even for PMs, one of the first things I did when I arrived was we were a little bit more of a memo culture, and I was like, you know what? We should be a deck culture because we can build those decks in Figma, and just that act alone allows you to encounter a lot of issues and for you to get familiar with it.

9b70b2189efb.text: 使用自己的产品非常重要。我到达时公司是memo文化,我说我们应该变成ppt文化,因为可以用Figma制作这些ppt。
9b70b2189efb.original: It's so important that you're using your own products. One of the first things I did when I arrived was we were a memo culture, and I was like, you know what? We should be a deck culture because we can build those decks in Figma.

6c8929479ad7.text: Dylan说'大家停下手头的所有工作,我们必须修复这个问题。'经过一番服务器和其他方面的检查,他们发现问题出在Philippe的MacBook上。
6c8929479ad7.original: Dylan was like, 'Everybody drop everything. We have to fix this.' And after some looking at the servers and things, they were like, 'Nothing's wrong,' and then they realized it was a problem with Philippe's MacBook.

46643ad540ee.text: 你在设计产品方面总是错误的。我的另一条准则就是你一直都是错的。所以你必须去尝试,把它展示给人们看,自己也要试用一下,才能真正理解它。我看不出有谁能完全凭自己的头脑设计出一款完美的产品。
46643ad540ee.original: You're always wrong about products. That's one of my other rules is you're just always wrong. And so you have to try it. You have to put it in front of people. You have to try it yourself before you'll understand it. No one can really design products in their head completely as far as I can tell.

3161bb3396e9.text: 我们有一个原则叫'快速发布以学习'。快速发布、尽早发布、频繁发布。这其中包含了失败的可能性。它不会总是对的,相反,更多时候会出错。
3161bb3396e9.original: We have a principle called Ship to Learn. Ship fast, ship early, ship often. So, in that idea is the idea of failure. It's not going to go right. And, it's going to go wrong more often than not.

66f6d74859ec.text: 很多时候,学习最快的方式就是发布。
66f6d74859ec.original: Many times, the fastest way to learn is to ship.

6c6b602c93d5.text: 我们有一种叫'迭代部署'的理念,核心思想是我们都在共同学习这些模型。因此,即使你不知道完整的能力,也很值得在公众面前发布,并一起继续迭代。
6c6b602c93d5.original: We have this philosophy, we call iterative deployment, and the idea is we're all learning about these models together. So there's a real sense in which it's way better to ship something even when you don't know the full set of capabilities and iterate together in public.

697c7cabffa3.text: 有时候需要回退并改变事情,但这又是一个学习的机会。
697c7cabffa3.original: Sometimes you need to roll back and change things, but it's another opportunity to learn.

2b09e9c34c4f.text: 如果你快速失败,你仍有足够的时间去尝试另一次,构建产品的另一个版本。尝试的次数越多,成功的可能性就越大。
2b09e9c34c4f.original: If you fail fast, you still have plenty of time to try another attempt and build another version of the product. The more attempts that you have, you simply increase the likelihood of being successful.

0ee0981eba8e.text: 当你有出色的战略,但执行力欠佳时,你最终也不会获胜,因为你的战略从未真正进入市场。更糟糕的是,你也一无所获。
0ee0981eba8e.original: When you have great strategy, perfect strategy but poor execution, you don't win because your strategy never makes it to the market. And what's even worse is that you have learned nothing.

a912d153e04e.text: 这是AI的一个规律,在发布之后你才会知道需要完善哪些。
a912d153e04e.original: This is a pattern with AI, you won't know what to polish until after you ship.

b3f70006808c.text: 你想做的就是第一个撞到砖墙的人。在一个竞争激烈的市场上,这尤其如此。原因在于,如果你认为自己是一家以创新为中心的公司,并相信你正在打造一些其他地方根本不存在的体验,为其他人树立了榜样,那么速度就是决定成功与否的最关键因素,至少就我的经验而言。
b3f70006808c.original: What you want to do is that you want to be the first one to hit the brick wall. This is particularly true when you are in a market that is competitive. The reason for that is that if you consider yourself as an innovation-centric company and you believe that you are building experiences that fundamentally don't exist anywhere else and you're sort of paving the way for the rest of the folks to basically get inspired with how you are building these experiences, speed is the single biggest determinant, in my experience, in terms of who ends up being more successful versus not.

23edaf89bdaf.text: 完美并不存在,不如追求'够好'就好。因为在发布时,你才能从用户那里学到很多无法预料的东西。
23edaf89bdaf.original: It's really to help me combat this perfectionism because perfect doesn't exist and you should instead go with good enough because when you ship, that's the moment when you get to learn a lot from your users and you just can't anticipate it.

39451d3e330d.text: 完美是良好的最大敌人。你不需要完美,只需要做到够好就能赢得市场。
39451d3e330d.original: The biggest enemy of good enough is perfect. You don't need to be perfect. You need to be good enough in order to win the market.

618fb66dcde1.text: 你计划的时间和真正发布的时间是不一样的,完美往往会阻碍我们做出好的东西。
618fb66dcde1.original: Time you're planning is not the time you're shipping, and the best is the enemy of the good.

88a81129a9f6.text: 列出MVP所需的功能清单,然后将其减半,再减半。大多数人对必需功能的判断通常相差一到两个数量级。
88a81129a9f6.original: Write out the list of features that are necessary in your MVP. Cut it in half and cut it in half again and build that. Most people's natural idea of what is necessary is so laughably wrong. People are naturally off by usually one or two orders of magnitude.

95e83fef9cf3.text: 如果它还不足够羞愧,那就还没够。第一个版本一定要足够羞愧。
95e83fef9cf3.original: If it's not embarrassing, you've gone too far. Got to be embarrassing. The first thing, that was embarrassing.
95e83fef9cf3.originalContext: Laura is discussing rapid experimentation strategy where "the first thing" refers to their embarrassing MVP solution of kicking users out of the onboarding portal to a docs page.

c4e867947fb8.text: 质量不等同于奢华或完美。质量意味着达到了规格要求,达到了就够了。如果觉得规格不够好,就制定更好的规格。
c4e867947fb8.original: Quality is not luxury. Quality is not perfection. Quality means meeting spec, and if you meet spec, you're done. If you don't think the spec is good enough, make a better spec.

4bb12d44566a.text: 在需要做出选择时,要多思考而不是着急发布。大多数实验应该先做思维实验。
4bb12d44566a.original: When you have to make a choice, think more and ship better. Most experiments should be thought experiments.

940a3f9096dd.text: 我告诉我的管理层,我的期望是他们每次都将速度提升一步。如果你认为某件事应该在今年完成,那就必须在上半年完成。
940a3f9096dd.original: I communicate to my leaders that my expectation is they bring in the clock speed one click faster. If you think something needs to be done this year, it needs to be done this half.

e1db46fd7463.text: 我们不按年、季度或周工作,而是按天工作。每一天都很重要,所以永远不要把明天的事拖到后天做。
e1db46fd7463.original: We don't work in years, quarters, weeks, we work in days. Each day matters and so never put out something tomorrow that you know can get done today.

b68db8f56436.text: 如果你想提高公司的速度,那就要做出更快的决策。快速决策来自于一种行动偏好。
b68db8f56436.original: If you want to improve the speed of a company, then make faster decisions. And fast decisions come from a bias of action.

e3aa040c2430.text: 做对事情很好,但速度也很必要。因为如果有10家初创公司在做同一件事,他们中的一些会冒险并做出早期决策,而且会是对的。
e3aa040c2430.original: Being right is good, but being quick is necessary. Because if there are 10 startups working on an idea, some of them will gamble and make an early bet and be right.

1c6104c73b86.text: 一个好的指标是,每次新的办公时间都有非常令人兴奋的新内容,而不是我们两周或四周前讨论过的同样的事情。他们已经完成了那些事情。
1c6104c73b86.context: 办公时间是创业公司与投资者/顾问定期进行的进展会议。'他们'指的是正在接受评估的创业团队。
1c6104c73b86.original: One good indicator is if each new Office Hour there is really exciting new stuff, right? We're not talking about the same thing we talked about two weeks ago or four weeks ago. They've already done that stuff.
1c6104c73b86.originalContext: Office Hours are regular startup progress meetings with investors/advisors. "They" refers to the startup teams being evaluated.

35fd7a3ce4a2.text: 每个人都说,'对,年轻的时候要努力工作加班无所谓。'我的想法是,'如果你每分钟的工作效率更高呢?'
35fd7a3ce4a2.original: Everyone says, 'Oh yeah, work hard and do more hours when you're young, whatever.' I'm like, 'What if you just did more per minute?'

8a10b1d3139c.text: 人们认为这是一种取舍,因为当他们考虑速度时,他们过度关注于匆忙或潦草。他们应该更多地关注于真正的能力。
8a10b1d3139c.original: People talk about this as if there were a trade-off because when they think about speed, the thing they over-index on is rushing or being sloppy. What they should be indexing on is being really competent.

6170510e0ae0.text: 每周你都会有一个固定的节奏,周一进行会议,周一晚上做些事情,周二向某人展示,周二晚上对其进行迭代。每周你都会有四五个这样的循环过程。
6170510e0ae0.original: Every week, you would have a cadence where it's like Monday, you go in. You do your meetings. Monday night, you build something. Tuesday, you show it to somebody. Tuesday night, you iterate on it. So you get four of these, five of these cycles every single week.

810d3032c1e7.text: 不要那样做。要更快地进入市场。我希望我们早点这么做。
810d3032c1e7.original: Don't do that. Get to market faster. I wish we had.

24d7f9020e3b.text: 我们真的很抗拒做一个大版本1。不要设计一个大而复杂的功能作为版本1,而是做最简单的功能概念,看看它是否有市场,然后逐步迭代增加。
24d7f9020e3b.original: We really resist the urge to do the big V1. Rather than design the big complex feature for V1, just do the simplest encapsulation of what that feature can be, see if it has legs, and then just add to it iteratively over time.

6572983e574f.text: 当时聊天是最简单的方式。我对它的爆红程度感到很惊讶,更惊讶的是有这么多公司进行了模仿。
6572983e574f.context: OpenAI的ChatGPT负责人尼克·特利指的是ChatGPT的聊天界面,他们在10天内就将其发布,并被其他人工智能公司广泛复制。
6572983e574f.original: Chat was the simplest way to ship at the time. I'm baffled by how much it took off, even more baffled by how many people have copied.
6572983e574f.originalContext: Nick Turley from OpenAI is referring to ChatGPT's chat interface, which they shipped in 10 days and has been widely copied by other AI companies.

46d2ab8dce47.text: 我们的目标是建造一个超级助手。它本来只是一个黑客马拉松的代码库。
46d2ab8dce47.original: We set out to build a super assistant. It was supposed to be a hackathon code base.

5aabdf452a26.text: 尽快发布它。所有关于确保尽快推出产品的建议都是完全正确的。你越快推出,就能获得越多反馈。
5aabdf452a26.original: Get it out as fast as you possibly can. Everything they tell you about making sure that you get a product out really quickly is totally true. The faster you get it out, the more feedback you get.

17916a6e0763.text: 在做彻底自动化之前先模拟一下,通过假门测试、烟雾测试、'魔法师'测试来验证想法。例如,我们在早期版本的邮箱标签功能中就是这么做的 - 我们展示给用户一个看起来可以工作的标签功能界面,但实际上只是一个HTML模拟。
17916a6e0763.original: You fake it, you do a fake door test, you do a smoke test, Wizard of Oz tests. We used a lot of those in the tabbed inbox by the way, one of the first early versions was actually we showed the tabbed inbox working to people. But it wasn't really Gmail, it was just a facade of HTML.

58b808266f44.text: 我们没有试图制定完美的计划、完美的产品需求文档、完美的高管演示,而是直接构建原型,让同事们使用并获取反馈。
58b808266f44.original: Instead of trying to come up with the perfect plan, the perfect PRD, the perfect pitch to executives we're like, 'Let's just build a prototype and put it in front of our colleagues and get them using it.'

3e337fabb686.text: 她完全是手动操作的,扮演着人工智能聊天机器人的角色。
3e337fabb686.original: She was completely manual. She was the one behind the email address posing as the AI, but doing it herself.

d19ef99edc97.text: 对于MVP来说,这是没有意义的。不要浪费数据科学家的时间和强大的训练机器的时间。
d19ef99edc97.original: Don't do it for your MVP. It makes zero sense. Do not waste time of data scientists that can train models with using powerful machines that are going take weeks to train.

0027e771efc0.text: 我们一直致力于降低使用摩擦。我们雇佣了几个大学实习生,让他们手动完成那些对用户来说很神奇的自动化任务,来满足用户的需求。
0027e771efc0.original: We were obsessed with reducing friction, this was our constant battle. And so we hired a couple of college interns and we brought them in and we were like, people are going to push this magical one button in the Anchor app and they're going to say, I want to distribute my podcast, and your job is going to be to do all that same manual stuff manually, but to them it's going to feel magical and it happened automatically.

cec03fba9a09.text: 从Anchor的最初日子开始,我们就一直秉持'构建不可扩展的东西'的原则。我们是一个非常小的团队,试图做一件很大的事情,又筹到了很少的资金,所以我们一直在想办法去实现我们的增长目标。
cec03fba9a09.original: One of our principles from the very early days of Anchor was build things that don't scale, where we were like, we're a ridiculously tiny team. We're trying to do this really big thing. We had raised very little money, and so we were always just trying to figure out how can we hack into whatever growth we're trying to make happen.

60e76bbc2c1b.text: 要缩短时间,当时间压力变大时,工程师、产品经理、设计师往往会降低质量,而不是减少范围。但实际上可以减少范围。
60e76bbc2c1b.original: The way to cut down on time is when time is being pressured downward, a lot of times engineers, PMs, designers, they will cut on quality rather than cutting on scope. And actually you can cut on scope.

f62986341ed0.text: 我们会仔细审视每个需要花时间开发的元素,问自己:如果去掉这个,产品还有用吗?我们不断重复这个过程,直到只剩下最核心的功能,不能再削减了。
f62986341ed0.original: We look at every element that's going to take any time to build and we just say, what if we remove this? Is the product still useful? And we keep repeating that until we remove whatever's left and we say it's going to be useless at this point.

4974e3159580.text: 如果连那个最核心的功能都是无用的,那么其他任何构建在上面的东西也都是无用的。
4974e3159580.context: 这里的'那个'指的是在删减非必要元素后剩下的最小可用核心功能。
4974e3159580.original: If that's not useful, then anything else built on top of that is also useless.
4974e3159580.originalContext: "That" refers to the stripped-down core feature after cutting all non-essential elements from the original design.

df06cba6c257.text: 什么事情都要从小做起。如果试图一次性把整个'大海'都煮沸来泡一杯茶,你永远也完不成这个任务。所以,如果你只是要泡一杯茶,那就专注于泡这杯茶就好,不需要把所有的水都煮沸。
df06cba6c257.original: Start small with everything. If you try to boil the ocean to make a cup of tea, you'll never get there. So if you're making a cup of tea, just make the cup of tea. You don't need to boil all the water that there is.

77a5bfae3762.text: 先造一台滑板,而不是先做轮子和轴。如果你要做一辆最小可行产品汽车,不要先做轮子和轴,而是先做一台滑板。然后再从滑板升级到自行车,再到摩托车,最后才是汽车。
77a5bfae3762.original: Build the scooter, not the axle. So if you're trying to build the minimum viable product for a car, don't build just the wheels and the axle, build the scooter first. And then from there, you build the bicycle, and the motorcycle, and then the car.

619a07c5c478.text: 对于新产品发布,你只能在质量、功能和截止日期中选择两个。软件的优势在于可以不断迭代改进,不像实体产品必须一开始就做到质量完美。
619a07c5c478.original: For a new launch, you got quality, features, deadline, choose two. The beautiful thing about software is you can keep iterating on it. So it's not like a physical product where you have to always have quality in there, otherwise it's never going to have quality.

c2eed64bc207.text: 很多团队正在努力的是,他们无法可预测和重复地发布东西。我的经验是,更普遍的挣扎是,东西进展缓慢,看不到尽头,我感到筋疲力尽。
c2eed64bc207.original: What most teams are struggling with is that they don't have predictable repeatable shipping of things. At least from my experience, the bigger really widespread struggle is, stuff isn't moving, it's dragging. I can't see the end. I'm losing my... I'm feeling burned out.

cdfa0a4e3a1a.text: 对于我这些年来合作或指导过的公司来说,关注结果是正确的。你想确保做正确的事情,以正确的目标。但有些人,包括我自己在某些时候,过于专注于结果,忽略了产出也是一个指标。
cdfa0a4e3a1a.original: And many of the companies that I've either worked with or advised, coached over the past few years, it was all about outcomes. Everyone was, 'Outcomes, outcomes, outcomes,' which is right. You want to make sure you're doing the right thing with the right goal, and that's fine. And some folks, myself included at certain points, swung way too far on the outcomes train and forgot that output is an indicator of that.

b7ebcc0f835a.text: 如果你的团队擅长做出决策、撰写文档以及设置产品、设计和实验方案等成功产品开发所需的一切,那很棒。但如果你也未能够足够快地将许多东西推向市场,那意义就不大了。
b7ebcc0f835a.original: If you have a team that's doing all of the ideation and figuring out how to make decisions quickly and getting the right documentation and setting up the right product briefs and design briefs and experiment briefs, all the things that we know go into to successful product development, that's great, but if you're also not shipping a lot of things to market quickly enough, then it just doesn't matter that much.

cc66940ae140.text: 你仍然应该将你的正式上线与软发布分开。开发人员应该能够在特定日期上线某些内容,这个日期是为他们方便而定的。
cc66940ae140.original: You should still be separating your hard launch from your soft launch. So what you should be doing is basically saying your developers are able to launch something on a particular date and it's the date that's convenient for them.

7b3141c05eb0.text: 哪种结果更好?频繁上线一些没有多大影响的东西,还是少量上线但确保以最佳方式上线并规避了很多风险,从而一年后您的成功率和速度更高?
7b3141c05eb0.original: What is a better outcome? Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't unimpactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way and de-risking a lot of other things so that a year later your win rate's higher and your velocity is higher?

9b24aa590d39.text: 不应该让一个团队负责三件事,而应该由三个团队各自负责一件事。
9b24aa590d39.original: Instead of one team doing three things, three teams should do one thing.

c7a38ee60ead.text: 有一句话说得好,最快拖慢一个项目的方法就是增加参与的人数。
c7a38ee60ead.original: There's a great saying that the best way to slow a project down is add more people to it.

f3428bc83c20.text: 五个团队各做一件事,而不是一个团队做五件事。
f3428bc83c20.original: Five teams should do one thing rather than one team do five things.

43dcd4887846.text: 不要将太多资源集中在这些大项目上。让它们由小团队负责。同时尽快获得客户反馈,不要等到完美后再推出。这样可以降低风险。
43dcd4887846.original: Don't put too many resources against these bigger swings. Have them be small teams. And then also, just get customer feedback as quickly as possible. Don't wait until the thing is perfect. And that way, you can limit the risk.

3530e46322c3.text: 我们最初真的是非常小规模地开展这些项目。我提到过,在最初的六个月里,每个产品只有一两个人在开发。通常是一个工程师和一个设计师,或者一个工程师和一个产品经理。只有在明显有市场前景后,他们才获得更多资金支持。
3530e46322c3.original: We started really small with all of these initiatives. So I think I mentioned, we really had one or two people working on each of these products for the first six months. So it was one engineer and one designer, or one engineer and one PM. And they really didn't get funding until it was clear that there was something there.

fb4648a5c379.text: 在《纽约时报》,当我思考我们最出色的产品是如何诞生的时候,就是把新闻业者和产品爱好者聚集在一起。这意味着《纽约时报》的产品经理需要了解艺术与科学的结合。

aa51df6c544a.text: 你无法建立一款产品,除非你知道如何谈论这个产品。你只有成为市场的专家,才能成为产品制作的专家。

957c2fb33d15.text: 如今对于消费类产品而言,设计已然成为构建强大吸引力的关键所在。设计欠佳的产品几乎无法获得成功。精湛的工艺和出色的设计能力已是必须达到的水准。

33f2dbffd014.text: 我认为现在这已经是一件很基础的事情了。从一开始,你就需要拥有相当出色的设计水平,人们才会注意到你并认真对待你。
33f2dbffd014.original: I think today it's almost a very basic thing now. Pretty much from the very beginning, you need pretty high level design for people to even pay attention or consider you seriously.

616e254c3394.text: 我们一直在寻找对此颇为重视的人才。对我们这样的企业而言,我们非常重视设计,因为我们看到,只有当人们真正使用我们的产品时,协作才能真正发生。如果存在摩擦或体验不太理想,我觉得这会让人感到非常烦恼。

583cc50f30f2.text: 我的说法很直接,大多数团队在设计投入方面都有所欠缺。也许当你达到一定规模后情况会有所不同,但我真诚地认为,大多数团队都没有真正体验过拥有极高设计比例所带来的工作质量和思维品质的提升。

d2468caaf9ca.text: 有时,我们强加给用户的任何工作,我们都应该持怀疑态度。我们真的需要证明这值得他们花时间,然后衡量他们是否真的这样做。

b946249ebbda.text: 我认为回答你的这个问题,有一些非常明确的原则是我们学到的。其中有一个我非常喜欢,但并不是我的原则,我认为这是直接来自克里斯·迪克森的,就是容错用户界面的原则。所以我无法说在机器学习初期有多少次,当我们说从人工策展转向推荐系统时,我看到一个设计草图,上面只有一个大的播放按钮,因为这显然是最简单的用户界面。但是如果你不了解机器学习的性能,你就无法为之设计。

7eeedebe81c0.text: 你和我使用多年的产品,与我们为他人构建的产品其实完全不同。像是重度用户使用产品,有大量积累的背景知识和使用经验,这样的产品体验很难复制到初次使用产品的新用户身上,Gmail或YouTube就是很好的例子。
7eeedebe81c0.original: A product that you and I use that we've been using for years isn't actually the product that we're building for other people. Like a power user who's using a product has... 0b6aa0960390.text: 令我费解的是,有那么多产品经理从未真正体验过自己的产品,更别说完整走一遍新手注册流程了。我们都习惯了使用成熟的产品,但是如果没有产品,新手的体验会是什么样的呢?
0b6aa0960390.original: It baffles me the number of PMs who never go through their products and go through the onboarding flow. Because we're all in this state of using the product. But actually, that first step where I don't have the product, what does that look like?

4d2f31022c14.text: 做好面向消费者的产品其实非常困难。很多人认为这很容易,因为我们每个人都是消费者。我们觉得自己是好用户,把朋友家人也当作典型用户,以为只要为自己和身边人构建就可以了。但事实并非如此,要做好一款产品需要很长的时间。

9f812c12d2be.text: 在一个如此多元化的社区中工作,你会发现很多与自己不同的群体。比如我在特立尼达长大的经历告诉我,人们的手机使用模式远比我们想象的复杂。我们总是以为每个人都有一部手机,但事实并非如此。

1af09c9a9fa6.text: 流畅性对开发者来说是一个非常重要的概念,你希望尽可能长时间地保持他们的专注状态。GitHub的拉取请求就是一个很好的例子。某人可以注册 Snyk 并连接他们的代码仓库。突然之间,我们就在保护、增强这些代码仓库,可能会有成百上千的开发者在 GitHub 中使用这些代码,从而从 Snyk 中获益,而无需亲自注册。
1af09c9a9fa6.context: Snyk 是一款开发者安全工具,可与 GitHub（一个代码托管平台）集成,自动扫描和保护代码仓库免受漏洞影响。
1af09c9a9fa6.original: Flow is just this incredibly important concept for developers and you want to strive to keep them in that flow for as long as possible. The GitHub kind of pool requests are a great example of that. Someone can sign up for Snyk and they could theoretically be the only user of Snyk and connect their repos. All of a sudden we're protecting, securing those repos, a hundred, a thousand developers could be working in GitHub with that code, all benefiting from Snyk without necessarily needing to sign up.
1af09c9a9fa6.originalContext: Snyk is a developer security tool that integrates with GitHub (a code hosting platform) to automatically scan and protect code repositories from vulnerabilities.

093ea9ec569d.original: I often say to find your audience's cultural erogenous zones. So what it means is people have things that they either care about or don't, and you're not going to change that. So it's a huge lift to try to change someone's worldview or their passions. It's a light lift to take the thing you want to talk about and just shape it into, to fit into their worldview or their passions.

951fa0b5ed8c.text: 要做到这一点实在太难了,你必须拥有超人般的天赋,我这辈子都没见过有人做到。你创造出一个如此强大的信息和故事,以至于一个原本毫不关心的人突然将其变成自己的热情所在。相比之下,了解他们的热情所在,然后说服他们如果他们关心那些,他们就应该关心你的事情,因为两者之间存在联系,这要容易得多。
951fa0b5ed8c.original: It is so hard and you'd have to be superhumanly gifted to the extent that I can't recall seeing in my entire life, where you create a message and a story so powerful that someone who didn't care at all before suddenly makes that their passion. It's so much easier to take what they're passionate about and understand it, and then convince them that if they care about that then they should care about your thing because of this connection.

e835c602acd9.text: 与其去违背人性直觉,试图让他们分享他们原本不会分享的内容,不如更多地利用用户已经自发进行截屏的时刻,让这些时刻变得更好。

d7d0c6b7926a.original: I think when you're running a marketplace, you tend to sit in your ivory tower a little bit looking at stats and thinking, 'If only we could get people to do X, it'd be better for everyone.' eaa43b708c38.text: 一旦用户坚持七天,损失厌恶就会启动,用户留存率会大幅提高。从一天到两天的连续使用,用户留存率有巨大跃升,从两天到三天略有降低但仍然很高,一直到第七天。
eaa43b708c38.original: Once you get to seven days, loss aversion kicks in, and you retain. Going from a one to a two-day streak, huge jump in retention, two to three day streak, slightly less but still huge and it's up until day seven.

4754a37dee21.text: 在用户刚开始建立连续使用时,给予更多灵活性。但当用户养成了长期连续使用习惯后,就不需要给予太多灵活性。

a277d92b37a0.original: Build for your best user, not your worst user. I think it's actually really easy to get stuck, or to focus on, 'What if there's abuse of this product?' Or think about all the ways in which the product won't be used well. And then you end up sort of shaping the product in these really weird funky ways to make up for that.

9d0265552dbc.text: 我们在Home上测试其中一些时,我们把它从90/10切换到了10/90。也就是说,10%是回放,90%是发现。虽然人们想要发现,但他们可能不想要90%的发现,而是90%的回放。

31361c550a3c.text: 我们一次又一次地从用户那里听到,他们说他们被困在一个品位泡沫里。所以我很喜欢我的Spotify,我很喜欢这个,但是我有点厌倦电子舞曲了,Spotify也没有推荐完全新的东西。如果你考虑这个问题,它可能听起来类似于推荐问题,但实际上它与此完全不同,因为当你在电子舞曲播放列表里推荐另一首电子舞曲时,你有大量来自该用户的信号,表明他们喜欢电子舞曲。但是,如果你要推荐一个完全新的流派,根本就没有任何信号。
31361c550a3c.original: What we hear from users again and again, though, is that they say that they get trapped in a taste bubble. So I love my Spotify, I love this, but I'm a little bit bored with EDM now and Spotify's not suggesting something completely new. And if you think about that problem, it may sound similar to the recommendation problem, it's just another recommendation problem, but it's actually fundamentally different because when you're recommending another EDM track inside the EDM playlist, you have a lot of signal from that user that they like EDM. But if you're going to recommend a completely new genre, by definition, you have no idea.
