8e614694e629.original: Seeing the sales team and the go-to-market team as this really great asset that can help you as a product manager get closer to the customer. Sales and the go-to-market teams in general could be your biggest asset to helping you get your job done well.

fe0050cbdbd4.text: 他们止不住谈论它,这就是对产品的热衷。他们会与团队成员或其他公司的人分享自己的发现。这种对产品的热爱和分享的愿望,正是你正在做对的一个很好的迹象。
fe0050cbdbd4.original: It's can they not stop talking about it and that's the chatter about a product, they want to share it with their teammates or to other people at different companies. That just top of mind love and wanting to share what they've found with others is really a great sign that you're onto something.

819e492a1296.text: 每个听众都或多或少了解产品,或者有产品背景。我就不多说了,但你能否与用户或潜在客户交谈,他们是否正在构建一些真正特殊、独特的东西?你能否感受到他们的热情,并确定这将是一个出色的产品。
819e492a1296.original: Everyone who's listening hopefully either is interested in products or has a product background. So I won't say too much there, but can you talk to users or potential customers, are they building something that's really special, unique? Can you hear that, spark that enthusiasm and figure out if this is going to be special.

43eb1df61e3f.text: 你最好的客户对你的定价并不敏感,因为他们明白其中的道理。他们从根本上理解这个产品。
43eb1df61e3f.original: Your best customers aren't price sensitive for what you're shooting for because they get it. They fundamentally understand it.

f480a1fb9a5e.text: 在跨越鸿沟之前,你合作的客户会说'我们相信你的理念'。在跨越鸿沟之后,他们会说'我不太确定你的理念,但我们需要你的产品'。
f480a1fb9a5e.context: 『跨越鸿沟』指的是Geoffrey Moore提出的框架,描述从早期的理想主义客户过渡到主流的务实客户的艰难过程。
f480a1fb9a5e.original: Before the chasm, the customers you work with are people who say, 'We believe what you believe.' After the chasm, they say, 'I'm not sure about that, but we need what you have.'
f480a1fb9a5e.originalContext: "The chasm" refers to Geoffrey Moore's framework describing the difficult transition from early visionary customers to mainstream pragmatic customers.

ea4326e086be.text: 首先,关上笔记本电脑。不要打开它,然后说:'我们在这里是因为我们一直在和您行业的一些人合作,我们认为您公司可能存在一个非常严重的文档管理或Wi-Fi接入等问题,这是真的吗?'
ea4326e086be.original: First of all, shut the God damn laptop. Just don't open it and start with... 'We're here because we've been working with some people in your industry and we understand there's this really serious problem around document management or around Wi-Fi access or whatever it is, and we believe that your company might have it, is that true?'

7a1377994771.text: 没有人关心我们的产品...他们关心的是他们自己、他们的需求、他们的想法和他们的问题。类别是关于客户及其想求、需求、问题和机会的。
7a1377994771.original: No one cares about our product... You know what they care about? Them, their needs, their wants, their problems. And categories are about customers and their wants, needs, problems and opportunities.

42e2904958bb.text: 不要向客户或潜在客户推销产品。人们不想被推销。
42e2904958bb.original: Don't pitch your customer or your prospective customer as you're trying to figure this out. People don't want to be pitched.

7bce2b5a7976.text: 这是行为科学工具箱,我们研究的是人们实际做了什么,而不是他们说他们会做什么。
7bce2b5a7976.original: This is the toolkit in behavioral science where we study not what people say they will do, but what they actually do.

7151af9f0932.text: 别担心一次性服务1000个客户,需要三周的时间。你可以挑选10个客户打电话,在打完前五个电话之前,就可以预测后面的第六、七、八、九、十个客户会说什么。
7151af9f0932.original: Don't worry about serving 1000 customers, taking three weeks. You pick up the phone, call 10 of them and nine times out of 10, by the time you've made your fifth call, you could predict what's customer six, seven, eight, nine and 10 are going to tell you.

052565e7186c.text: 如果你与足够多的人交谈,并且能够预测70%到80%下一个人会说什么,那说明你已经与足够多的人交谈,清楚地听到了模式。
052565e7186c.original: If you talk to enough people and you can predict 70 to 80% of what the next person is going to say to you, because you've just talked to so many people and you've heard the pattern so clearly, that's when you've talked to enough people.

62e6c7bcd042.text: 在整个客户群体中,90%的人并非早期使用者。不管你有什么新奇酷炫的东西,他们都不太感兴趣。那10%才是真正的早期使用者,才是你真正想要触达的人。但这意味着你要接触10个人才能找到1个感兴趣的人。
62e6c7bcd042.original: If you take the average customer group in the world, 90% are not early adopters. It doesn't matter if you have something new and cool, they're just not interested. Those 10 percents are the early adopters. They're The ones that you actually want to reach. But that means you have to reach 10 to find one.

23a929ce59d4.text: 如果你没有假设,你会花很多时间进行研究,收集大量定性、轶事或定量数据,但你不会知道如何解读它们,因为它们并没有验证或否定你的假设,因为根本就没有假设。
23a929ce59d4.original: If you don't have a hypothesis, you're going to spend a lot of time researching, you're going to get a lot of data back, qualitative, anecdotal or quantitative and you're not going to know what to make of it because it's not either validating or invalidating your hypothesis because there isn't a hypothesis.

3c1bb62fdb95.text: 当客户觉得有必要额外主动提出某个问题时,这就是一份难能可贵的礼物。我会立即从会议中脱身,只为给他们一个反馈。
3c1bb62fdb95.original: The moment the customer felt compelled enough to go out of their way to talk about some problem, that's a unbelievable gift. I will leave a meeting to just get one message back to them.

bfd18bcbb7e1.text: 对我这样的产品高管来说,没有什么比收到客户的投诉更值得珍惜的了。投诉是一份礼物,如果你正在收听这个播客,并且是Rippling的客户,觉得有什么我们需要知道的,即使我可能已经知道了,也不要因此而放弃给我反馈的机会。
bfd18bcbb7e1.original: There's no greater gift to me as a product executive than receiving an escalation from a customer. Escalations are a gift, and it's like, if you're a listener right now on this podcast and you are a Rippling customer and you have shit that you think we should know, the fact that I might already know it is not a reason for you to withhold the gift of your feedback.

0ae2aecda9ea.text: 在产品内部创造更多收集反馈的机会。我从Stripe获得了灵感...我们日复一日地构建产品,直接聆听用户的想法。
0ae2aecda9ea.original: Create a lot of opportunities for people to give you feedback inside the product. I drew inspiration from Stripe... we were building day in and day out, just streaming users' thoughts right into our consciousness.

ba3752d8f447.text: 我们将support@pandora.com设为all@pandora.com的别名。所以如果你向Pandora发送客户服务请求,公司内的每个人都会收到它。因为我们在第一年决定没有客户服务团队,所以期望whoever first看到请求的人都应该做出回应。你写给我们的,可能会得到创始人、我自己或者是编写该功能的工程师,甚至是CEO的回复。
ba3752d8f447.original: When we launched the support@pandora.com was an alias for all@pandora.com. So if you sent a customer service request to Pandora, every single person in the company received it. And because we made a decision to have no customer support team in the first year, the expectation was that whoever sees the request first should respond to it. And so you would write to us and you would get the founder or you'd get me or you'd get the engineer who wrote the feature or you'd get the CEO.

9e3e43d6f774.text: 你希望招募一群真正是你产品的良好潜在用户或客户,但却无一丝个人利益。他们完全不关心你的产品是否成功。他们只是为了测试它而来。
9e3e43d6f774.original: You want to recruit a bunch of people that are legitimately good prospective users or customers of your product, but have zero skin in the game. They do not care at all whether or not your product succeeds. They're just in it to test it.

9076a2f43fb3.text: 我们将所有来自朋友的反馈都打折扣到零。这对我们没有任何意义。我们甚至不会记录下来。我们只对目标客户莎拉感兴趣。
9076a2f43fb3.original: We discount all of that feedback from our friends to zero. That is not of interest to us. We don't even write it down. We are only interested in Sarah, our target customer.

793d4e143363.text: 你必须有意识地不去采纳很多早期用户的反馈意见,而这恰恰是在认真倾听并构建人们想要的产品的同时进行的。不能全是人们的意见。
793d4e143363.original: You have to deliberately not act on the feedback of many of your early users, and this is at the same time as listening to people intensely and building what people want. It can't be all people.

16b58bcd6796.text: 设计伙伴是很棒的。从设计伙伴到全面推广客户,这是最难完成的一环。
16b58bcd6796.original: Design partners are incredible. They're the hardest logos to upsell, meaning go from design partner to full rollout customer.

573170a69c01.text: 关于ROI模型,正确的思路是与客户从一开始就共同创建,这意味着要就假设和输入达成一致并进行验证。
573170a69c01.original: The right way to think about an ROI model is to actually co-create it with your customers from day one, which means agree and validate on the assumptions and the inputs.

e01718e2e414.text: 在Stripe,我们认为产品开发就是要找到正确的一群早期用户与之共同创造产品。所以我们会有共享的Slack频道,定期向他们展示产品并获取反馈。只有当这个原始的Alpha群体非常满意产品时,我们才会考虑向更广泛的受众推出。
e01718e2e414.original: The way we think about product development at Stripe, it really is to find the correct set of early users to kind of co-create the product with. So we had shared Slack channels, we'd actually show them product on a very regular basis, get their feedback on it. And only when that original kind of Alpha group was super, super happy with the product did we then think it might be ready to go to a broader audience.

698caa865b54.text: 如果你有一种机制去倾听用户、尽快让他们接触产品并获取反馈,运转这个反馈循环,你就几乎不会出错。只要这个反馈循环运转良好,真的很难出错。
698caa865b54.original: If you have a mechanism to listen to users, get something in their hands quite quickly and then get their feedback on it to run it back through a feedback loop, you're very unlikely to go wrong. It's actually very hard to go wrong if you have that feedback loop working really well.

74becdcc715d.text: 我最近有50次对话,但即使是第一次对话,只要我有一个假设并展示了一两个原型,我学到的都比之前多得多。这就像天差地别。
74becdcc715d.original: I've had 50 conversations over the past month, but I learned so much more from even the first conversation when I had a hypothesis and I had a prototype, or a couple prototypes, to show them. It's like night and day.

50d9eb479bcf.text: 您想把他们的想法反映回来。这就是向他们展示您理解他们所面临的问题,并且您的产品正好能满足他们需求的方式。
50d9eb479bcf.context: 乔治安娜·劳迪在谈论在产品信息传达和营销沟通中反映客户语言。
50d9eb479bcf.original: You want to reflect them back to them. That is what is going to show them that you understand the problem that they have and that your product has exactly what it is that they need.
50d9eb479bcf.originalContext: Georgiana Laudi is speaking about reflecting customers' language back to them in product messaging and marketing communications.

c187ea7ac589.text: 如果您实在不适合任何其他类别,那您可能需要确定哪种类别更适合自己,并将之包装呈现。这主要需要您不断与客户交流,倾听他们谈论事物的方式。最终一切都来自您从他们那里听到的内容,以及哪些内容更能引起共鸣。
c187ea7ac589.original: If you really don't fit into any other category, then you probably do need to figure out what the category is and package that. And that's going to be done mostly by continuing to talk to customers and listening to how they talk about things. It all comes from what you hear from them ultimately and what will resonate.

4280e312bc96.text: 我所有最好的营销和定位策略,实际上都来自于与客户进行了数以百万的交流,倾听他们如何解决问题,我们的系统如何帮助他们解决问题,他们在做什么,以及他们如何谈论这些事物。
4280e312bc96.original: All of my best marketing and positioning literally comes from having a million conversations with customers and listening to how they solve problems and how our system helps them solve problems and what they're doing and how they talk about stuff.

a51dc35088fd.text: 在担任支持岗位轮岗期间,有一些主题性的问题一直在重复出现。人们会问:'您们是否能处理订阅付款或定期付款?'而我会说:'当然可以,但您不应该知道这一点,因为我们并没有告知您。'
a51dc35088fd.original: When I was doing the support rotation, there were thematic things that kept coming up. People were asking, 'Hey, do you process subscription payments or recurring payments?' And I was like, 'Of course you could, but there's no reason you should know that because we don't tell you anywhere.'

985b64a71efe.text: 如果一个客户有其他方法可以解决他们的问题,他们就不会疯狂到选择与初创公司合作。
985b64a71efe.original: If a customer has the ability to do something other than what you do to solve their problem, they won't be crazy enough to do business with a startup.

f0ef69e12337.text: 餐厅会告诉你一堆事情,比如人员排班问题,租金问题。但这并没有真正深入了解他们日常最关注的事情。当建立新产品时,人们最容易忽视的就是买家对产品的紧迫需求。
f0ef69e12337.original: If you walked into a restaurant, they would tell you a bunch of things. They would say, 'Oh, labor schedule is an issue.' They would say, 'My rent is an issue.' But that doesn't actually get into their head on what's truly important day-to-day. The biggest thing people miss when they're building new products is the urgency of the buyer part of it.

e65ac58e9d2b.text: 我所说的最佳客户是那些从你现有的产品中获得大量价值的客户,很明显,他们会付费。他们很高兴,不太需要维护。而且非常重要的是,他们最近才订阅你的产品,还记得没有这个产品之前的生活。
e65ac58e9d2b.original: What I mean by best customers is those that get a ton of value from your product as it exists today, pay obviously. They're happy. They're low maintenance. And very importantly, they signed up for your product recently enough that they remember what life was like before.

5f18f20d387d.text: 你需要能够创造需求,而不仅仅是去发现它们。
5f18f20d387d.original: You need to be able to create needs rather than just discover them.

66bd91c3ca9e.text: Dylan的直觉建立在与数以千计、上百万个客户的交流之上。我的工作就是把这些直觉转化为逻辑,让大家也能理解这背后的原因。
66bd91c3ca9e.original: Dylan is very based on intuition and instinct. That intuition is actually built off of thousands and hundreds of thousands of customer interactions where he might look at something and be like, 'This isn't going to land well.' Part of my job is to build out that logic for him so people can understand that at scale.

5e15da127f47.text: Dylan非常关心每一个用户对Figma的感受。他会主动询问我的合作伙伴最大的问题是什么。这就是他展现出的极致的客户至上精神,也是他直觉的源泉。
5e15da127f47.original: Dylan actually really cares very deeply about any given user and how they're feeling about Figma. He met my partner and immediately wanted to ask what the biggest problems were. That's the level of customer obsession that he exhibits and then informs his intuitions.

1cf937964b47.text: 我认为保持对用户的永不满足的好奇心,并抓住每个机会与用户交流,这是很重要的。我会参加晚宴,并积极询问身边的人如何使用Figma和FigJam。
1cf937964b47.original: I think that it's just by having this insatiable curiosity and talking to users at every chance you get. So, I would go to dinners and grill the people around me on how they use Figma and how they use FigJam.

d07429d1f576.text: 在我担任产品经理之前,我被要求亲自拜访30位客户,15位在美国,15位在欧洲。这是我的导师给我的规定。事实证明,这30位客户的拜访完全改变了我的认知,原来我对客户的了解远远不够。
d07429d1f576.original: I was not allowed to take the product manager role until I had visited 30 customers in person, 15 in the US, 15 in Europe. That was just the person who was coaching me. That was their rule. And all I know is those 30 customers changed my life because I thought I knew our customers and I really didn't.

60fef7d16f17.text: 花更多时间在问题上,而不是解决方案。
60fef7d16f17.original: Spend more time on the problem than the solution.

0cc8a0f7acfc.text: 优秀产品的核心在于真正了解问题领域或机会领域,花时间准确定义问题,然后再着手解决。
0cc8a0f7acfc.original: I think that the heart of good product is really getting comfortable in the problem space or the opportunity space, really taking the time to frame a problem well, and to really get into what's needed before we jump to solutions.

0cfb18a53596.text: 从问题开始,沉浸其中并被它指引,然后再去寻找解决方案。
0cfb18a53596.original: Working backwards is all about the problem and starting there and obsessing about the problem and being guided by it to then go into the solution.

ac16c833b2f2.text: 我们不会考虑你想要构建的东西,而是会专注于用户和现实世界中的人及其问题。
ac16c833b2f2.original: We are not going to think at all about the thing that you want to build, but instead we're going to be focused on users and people in the real world and their problems.

4eeeafeaea8a.text: 每个人都很容易跳到解决方案,这是一个很难改正的习惯。作为产品经理,这也是一个常见的错误。
4eeeafeaea8a.original: I think something that is really hard to untrain, but I think every human does it, is you jump to solutions. And so one of the biggest things I see, not just in my course, but also just as a PM and some of the mistakes that you make as a PM is the idea of you get really attached to a solution.

b28e964564cf.text: 团队最大的错误是过于热衷于解决问题的方案,而不是尽全力去理解遭受问题困扰的客户。
b28e964564cf.original: The biggest mistakes that teams make is they become very passionate about a solution to a problem they're trying to solve as opposed to do everything they can to develop empathy for the customer that's suffering the problem.

f714f9445a6e.text: 当团队做错时,就是不能倒推思考。他们有想要构建的东西,然后才去寻找问题,这是在事后拼凑问题和用户。
f714f9445a6e.context: "倒推思考"是亚马逊的产品开发方法论,团队先撰写期望的客户成果的新闻稿和常见问题解答,然后再开始构建。
f714f9445a6e.original: When teams that do it wrong is they don't do that. They don't work backwards. They have something they want to build... And so you're adding the problem after the solution. You're retrofitting the problem, retrofitting the customer.

f0dbcd657be2.text: 最常见的征兆就是,他们在谈论一些想要组合现有的各种元素,而不是真正倒推思考。
f0dbcd657be2.context: '向后工作'是亚马逊的产品开发方法论,团队从编写期望的客户成果的新闻稿和常见问题解答开始,然后再进行构建。
f0dbcd657be2.original: The most common thing that I see that tips me off is when they talk about something, there's different pieces in the pantry and we have these ingredients, we could put them together... But that's not really working backwards.
f0dbcd657be2.originalContext: "Working backwards" is Amazon's product development methodology where teams start by writing a press release and FAQ for the desired customer outcome before building anything.

aa0e7ee31bbe.text: 机会是指未满足的需求、痛点或愿望,这很好。但我可以告诉你,98%的人在描述机会时都是在描述解决方案。
aa0e7ee31bbe.original: I can tell you that opportunity is an unmet need pain point or desire, and that's great. But I can tell you that 98% of people that write opportunities write them as solutions.

d27a12bcdb7a.text: 我认为还有一个步骤可以做,就是他们为什么会有这个问题呢?也许这里有一个机会去解决引发这个问题的根源,从而产生更大的产品影响。
d27a12bcdb7a.original: I think there's one more step you can take, which is, why do they have that problem in the first place? And maybe there's something there, and that could be an opportunity to make a bigger product impact by fixing that underlying condition that created the problem in the first place.

de8104243d68.text: 客户要求一个功能,你可以问,为什么他们需要这个功能,然后追溯到问题的根源。但你还可以再多走一步 - 他们为什么会有这个问题?也许通过解决这个根源问题,你可以产生更大的产品影响。
de8104243d68.original: A customer is asking for a feature, but then you would say, okay, why are they asking for it, and back up to the problem. But there's one more step you can take - why do they have that problem in the first place? Maybe there's an opportunity to make a bigger product impact by fixing that underlying condition.

9c71477f2dac.text: 什么让这件事变得很难?客户会告诉我,'哦,我们想开拓澳大利亚市场。这是一个我们还没开发的市场。'我会说,'好的,那我们为什么要谈论这个?你是CEO,直接让人去做就好了。是什么让这件事变得很难?'
9c71477f2dac.original: What makes it hard? Client will tell me, 'Oh, we want to open up business in Australia. It's a market we haven't tapped.' And I'll say, 'Okay, so why are you and I talking about that? You're the CEO. Just tell somebody to do it. What makes it hard?'

d7df095c2bd8.text: 你实际上是从一个问题或者相反的愿景开始的,但它们是相连的。大多数伟大的公司和产品都源于一个问题,但从这个问题中演变出'更好的方式'。
d7df095c2bd8.original: You actually start with a problem or the inverse of that, which is a vision, but they're connected. Most great companies, most great products come out of a problem, but out of the problem becomes like, 'Here's a better way.'

6573bfe727ac.text: 我认为我从他那里学到的最大启发就是原型的力量。尽管他是一个如此出色的产品思考者,但他总是说:'我无法告诉你这是否会奏效。我必须亲自感受它,去尝试它。一个模型并不能告诉你它的使用感受会是什么。'

499e1ede442b.text: 成功转型的人通常有几个特点:好奇心强,对产品和解决客户问题充满热情,有时还会通过自己的副业项目来磨练产品经理的技能。
499e1ede442b.original: The folks who have successfully transferred over, they tend to have a couple of characteristics. 1ff224bc228b.text: 我认为产品经理越来越需要具备一定的技术能力。此前也曾有一段时间产品经理被定位为全能型,但现在又回归到产品经理需要更多技术背景的趋势。同时,设计师也需要更多的业务思维,把设计作为实现目标的手段,而工程师也正变得更加关注产品和用户。
1ff224bc228b.original: I think product managers are increasingly I think a bit more technical or expected to be. And I think engineers are increasingly becoming what more product-focused, more user-focused.

f31871ea7510.text: 你需要拥有一定的广度,但这种广度可以是针对同一个问题的不同行业,或者是针对同一行业的不同问题。这是两种思考深度的方式。
f31871ea7510.original: You need to have some breadth, right, but it's like same problem, different industry. It's one way to think about depth that's focused. Different problem, same industry is another way to think about it.

3f1e47bafe23.text: 我看到很多产品经理犯的一个错误就是只关注输出或只关注结果。当你转向关注结果时,仍然很重要的是继续磨练你在输出方面的技能。
3f1e47bafe23.original: The mistake that I see a lot of product managers make is they start operating in either output or outcomes. And when you are transitioning to outcomes, it's very important that you continue to still hone your craft on outputs.

e49844e168bd.text: 不是AI会取代人类,而是使用AI工具的增强型人类,在就业市场上会更具竞争力。
e49844e168bd.original: It's not AI that's going to replace humans. It's other humans that are being augmented and using AI tools that are going to be more competitive in a job market and stuff like that.

3ce27e8a8519.text: 简单地说,就是要玩这项技术。随着职业发展,我们很容易陷入固有思维,这是很大的风险。
3ce27e8a8519.original: Quite simply in one word, play. We all have to be playing with this technology. The risk of becoming more experienced in your career is you get stuck in your ways.

77c5aae6e1de.text: 到2030年,完成工作所需的技能将变化70%。不管你是否考虑换工作,你的工作都在发生变化。
77c5aae6e1de.original: When we look at the skills required to do your job, by 2030, it will change by 70%. So whether or not you're looking to change your job, your job is changing.

9c1ec3c23385.text: 优秀人才总是有一种不断提升自己技能的倾向,以及成为技术前沿的内在需求。我们也看到这一点正在LinkedIn发生。
9c1ec3c23385.original: Top talent has this tendency of continuously trying to get better at their craft and this innate need to be at the cutting edge of how you build, and I think we're seeing this here as well.
9c1ec3c23385.originalContext: Cohen is discussing LinkedIn's AI-first transformation and how top engineering talent at LinkedIn are embracing these new AI-powered development approaches.

4a696b2f739c.text: 你个人的利益与组织需求高度一致。因为我们需要你去改变。我们希望成为一个更敏捷、适应性强、有韧性的组织,以应对变革的步伐,而你本人也希望为自己的职业发展而努力。
4a696b2f739c.original: The incentives for you are so aligned with your organization of what we're asking for, right? Because we need you to change. We want to be a more agile, adaptive, resilient organization that can deal with the pace of change, but you want as well for your own career.

47456c067cde.text: 以前在简历上列举Google搜索技能,是因为你从小就成长在Google时代。
47456c067cde.original: You used to put a Google Search on a skill on your resume because you grew up with Google.

352934d795f6.text: 对那些对此感兴趣或想成为未来经济主力的人来说,要深入研究这些工具,因为成为使用它们的顶级10%,将在未来几个月和几年里为你带来绝对的差异。
352934d795f6.original: The best thing for people who are interested in this or interested in just being a part of the future economies, get your hands very dirty with these tools because being in the top 10% in using them is going to absolutely set you apart in the coming months and years.
352934d795f6.originalContext: "These tools" refers to AI-powered software development platforms like Lovable, which generate functional code from natural language instructions.

180f6fbf84eb.text: 如果你花一周时间达到某个结果,最好的学习方式是:我想做这件事,然后我想用AI来完成它。这样做一周,你就处于全球人口顶级1%。
180f6fbf84eb.original: If you spend a full week on trying to reach an outcome, the best way to learn is I want to do this thing and then I want to use AI to do that thing. And you've spent a full week, you are in the top 1% in the global population.
180f6fbf84eb.originalContext: "This thing" and "that thing" refer to identifying a specific problem you want to solve, then using AI tools to solve it.

b3658f796d1e.text: 学习编码的投资回报率每6个月翻一番。
b3658f796d1e.original: The return on investment for learn to code is doubling every six months.

b38f86b8d46e.text: 因为每次我和他坐下来告诉他,'好,这就是讲故事的方法,这就是标题的思考方式',他都会录下来,放到提示里,所以他在两个月内取得了一年的进步,再也不会犯同样的错误。
b38f86b8d46e.original: He made a year's worth of progress in two months because every time I sat down with him and told him, 'Okay, here's how you tell a story, here's how you think about a headline,' he recorded all of it, put it into a prompt, and he never made the same mistake twice.

b600bb6ca164.text: 如果你去上编程训练营,他们会从'什么是Git?'开始教起。这是在倒置这个过程,先给你工具,再给你问题。我认为这些你都不需要担心。
b600bb6ca164.original: If you go to a coding bootcamp, they're going to start with what is Git? You're inverting the process, you're giving the tool before the actual problem. I think all of that stuff, you don't have to worry about.

3d3da9761ec5.text: 初级开发人员刚开始时,我们通常希望他们能够编写简单的代码。但如果现在有一个AI系统在帮助他们编写代码,他们可以从一开始就花更多时间去理解系统、环境,或者他们正在构建的产品,而不是学习如何编码,因为现在他们有这个AI助手。
3d3da9761ec5.original: Junior developers, when they start, usually we expect them to be able to write simple code. But if now there is an AI system that is helping them writing code, they can spend more time from the get-go understanding the system, understanding the environment that they're building, or understanding that product that they're building, which today they don't have time because they're still learning how to code.

b1f49dbc739f.text: 如果你基本上只是一个待办事项管理员,好运保住你的工作,因为这已经有人在做了。迟早这项工作会得到很好的支持。
b1f49dbc739f.original: If you are fundamentally a backlog administrator, good luck protecting that because already people are doing that. It's only a matter of time before that becomes pretty well-supported.

d5c5f82f7f2b.text: 清晰明确的产品周期执行成效,对我来说可能是最好的评判一个人是否准备好承担更多责任的指标。你基本上想给他们更多,因为他们已经表现出有规律地做好事情的能力。
d5c5f82f7f2b.original: Clear demonstrated impact from an end to end product cycle to me is probably one of the better indicators of readiness for someone to take on more. You basically want to give them more, because now they have a pattern of doing things properly.

e8f08725e67d.text: 我认为被忽视的一点是,要把手头的工作做好。尤其是产品经理,他们通常很有抱负,总是盯着下一个职位,但如果你现在的工作做得不好,就不会得到下一个机会。
e8f08725e67d.original: One of the things that I think is overlooked is do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point. People have a tendency... Especially product managers are very ambitious and they want to get to the next level and they're always eyeing the next job, but you're not going to get the next job unless you do really well at the job that you're in.

933dc1c348b0.text: 人们愿意与他们合作吗?随着人们升职晋级,下属是否愿意为他们工作?归根结底,这是一个选择。如果你身边有一群聪明人,他们选择跟随或与这个人合作,这本身就有着巨大的价值。
933dc1c348b0.original: Do people want to work with them? Do people at some point, as they go up and become more senior, do people want to work for them? Ultimately people make choices. And if you have a bunch of smart people and they're making smart choices and they're choosing this person to follow or to be with and work with them, there is a ton of value in that.

71452f2243a9.text: 在产品工作的头六个月内,可能不需要太关注战略。这六个月主要是与客户交流、深入了解产品相关的情况。你应该说'我会学习公司现有的战略,做好研究,但我会落实这个战略'。
71452f2243a9.original: For your first six months on a product, probably don't worry about strategy. For your six months really, you should be talking to customers, researching your product stuff. Really starting off by saying, 'I'm going to learn the strategy, whatever strategy my company already has, and I'm going to do my research, but I'm going to deliver on that strategy.'

9fe21ea18c4d.text: 很多时候,你被指派解决一个问题,如果给出一个非常创新的解决方案可能反而不好。在这种情况下,只需要做一件简单的事情,把它做好。这会让你赢得信任,未来可以承担更大的责任,但要晋升到高级产品经理,你只需要做一份稳扎稳打的工作就够了。
9fe21ea18c4d.original: A lot of times you've been assigned a problem where a huge creative solution is a bad idea. If you're in one of the situations, just do the simple thing, get it done really well. And that'll earn you the trust to be able to take on bigger things in the future, but you don't need to be outstanding to make it past the APM promotions. You just need to be doing a solid, good job.

a4cc4ddabac7.text: 我认为产品经理的核心责任就是产生影响力,也就是说如果一个团队一直在打造用户喜爱的产品,并且改变了业务的方向,其他事情都只是一些输入因素而已。
a4cc4ddabac7.context: 诺亚在讨论产品经理的核心职责,并进一步说明了卓越的执行力是产品经理的基本要求。
a4cc4ddabac7.original: I think impact solves all PM issues, which is if a team is consistently building things people love and changing the director of the business, everything else is just an input.
a4cc4ddabac7.originalContext: Noah is discussing core responsibilities of product managers, building on his point that impeccable execution is a baseline requirement for PMs.

232f111bc294.text: 这里让人非常沮丧的是,你会发现即使人们意识到现状并不理想,但他们转向的大多数资源仍在延续着同样的模式。所以这些认证,在我看来是无关紧要的,但大多数人并不知道。你想象一下,作为一个全新的产品经理,你在网上看到的90%的内容都来自于产品功能团队,或者更糟。
232f111bc294.context: "同样的模式"指的是产品功能团队,在那里产品经理被给予既定的路线图,而不是发现客户问题并提出解决方案。
232f111bc294.original: What's so frustrating here is you have all these people that realize things aren't good yet most places they turn are just propagating that same model. So these certifications, which in my opinion are bogus, but most people don't know. And just imagine you're a brand new product manager. You look online probably what, 90% of the content out there is from the feature team world or worst.
232f111bc294.originalContext: "That same model" refers to feature teams where product managers are given predetermined roadmaps rather than discovering customer problems and solutions.

256c61896aa7.text: 大多数产品经理都不应该做产品经理。他们应该更多地思考这是否真的是适合自己的领域,因为我觉得很多来自其他领域的人进入这个领域,却没有完全意识到这需要什么样的能力。
256c61896aa7.original: Most product managers should not even be product managers. They should think a little bit more around whether this is actually the right field for them because I think a lot of people from other areas have entered the field without fully realizing what it takes.

bd5bf4e2c3d9.text: 他们转向的大多数资源仍在延续着同样的模式。所以这些认证,在我看来是无关紧要的,但大多数人并不知道。你想象一下,作为一个全新的产品经理,你在网上看到的90%的内容都来自于产品功能团队,或者更糟。
bd5bf4e2c3d9.context: "同样的模式"指的是传统的产品功能团队方法,在那里产品经理被给予路线图,而不是解决客户问题。
bd5bf4e2c3d9.original: Most places they turn are just propagating that same model. So these certifications, which in my opinion are bogus, but most people don't know. And just imagine you're a brand new product manager. You look online probably what, 90% of the content out there is from the feature team world or worst.
bd5bf4e2c3d9.originalContext: "That same model" refers to the traditional feature team approach where product managers are given roadmaps rather than solving customer problems.

9f537d9981ab.text: 这个产品负责人角色并没有从我们所知的产品管理中产生。它是为了帮助开发人员确定优先事项而出现的。
9f537d9981ab.original: This product owner role did not emerge from product management as we know it today. It was a way to help the developers prioritize what to work on.

c42a99eaaf1c.text: 如果你在某人的简介中看到CSPO,那就是认证的Scrum产品负责人。这通常是一个为期两天的研讨会,他们参加了这个研讨会,然后获得了认证。
c42a99eaaf1c.context: CSPO代表Certified Scrum Product Owner,这是Scrum敏捷软件开发框架提供的一种认证。
c42a99eaaf1c.original: If you ever see somebody with a CSPO on the end of their profile, it's a certified Scrum product owner. It's typically a two-day workshop that they went to and then got certified.
c42a99eaaf1c.originalContext: CSPO stands for Certified Scrum Product Owner, a certification offered through the Scrum framework for agile software development.

33fd183a6e97.text: 产品管理作为一个学科仍然相当不发达。我们才从事这个工作15到20年,所以目前产品管理的状态并没有真正抓住最重要的东西,最有价值的东西。
33fd183a6e97.original: Product management is still such a relatively undeveloped discipline. We're like 15 to 20 years into this, and so there's something about the current state of product management that isn't getting at the truly important things, the truly value-added things.

3ff8fad71f03.text: 你的超能力在于真正吸取这些洞见并赋予它们生命,密切关注客户。不会有任何领导者或高管对能突出客户痛点的有价值洞见不感兴趣的。
3ff8fad71f03.original: Your superpower is in really pulling those insights in and bringing them to life, staying close to the customer. There's not a single leader or executive that isn't going to be stoked to hear about valuable customer insights that highlight problems they might not be seeing.

1f61359be1f7.text: 以社区笔记举例。如果我一直在领导一个大型的消费类产品团队,我会产出什么?16页以上的 OKR 吗?可能只会有一堆文档。我认为建立社区笔记对这个世界产生了更大的影响。
1f61359be1f7.context: 社区笔记是 Twitter/X 的众包事实核查功能,让用户为可能具有误导性的推文添加背景信息。
1f61359be1f7.original: Look at Community Notes for example. If I had stayed running a large consumer PM team, what would I have produced? 16 more pages of OKRs? I don't know, a bunch of documents? I think building Community Notes has had way bigger impact on the world.
1f61359be1f7.originalContext: Community Notes is Twitter/X's crowdsourced fact-checking feature that lets users add context to potentially misleading tweets.

3c948b773b1a.text: 要实现影响力,需要同时关注环境和自身技能的一系列变量。
3c948b773b1a.original: Impact is only achievable by looking at a set of variables related to the environment, a set of variables related to your skills.

81c418ab3f31.text: 有一种迷思可能会阻碍人们的道路。即管理的人越多或覆盖范围越大,影响力就越大。我绝对不认为这是真的。
81c418ab3f31.original: I think there's one myth that can get in people's ways. The idea that the more people you manage or the larger your scope is, the more impact you have. I definitely do not think that is true.

9bcc04c83284.text: 每一次内心的声音都是错误的。那个总是对你进行批评和不停重复的内心声音。我说的就是那个声音,它总是错误的。
9bcc04c83284.original: Every single time the voice in your head is wrong. That critical voice in your head. To be specific, I'm talking about the voice in your head that is critical and repeats. There's the voice that says the same thing over and over again. You got to work out more, you got to work out more, you got to work out more. Whatever that is, it's always wrong.

ffd871517373.text: 我们有一种倾向,就是会编造一些故事来匹配我们当下的状态。这就是当我们以那种方式呼吸时所发生的情况。
ffd871517373.context: "那种方式"指的是激活神经系统的呼吸模式,比如通过嘴巴快速浅呼吸到上胸部。
ffd871517373.original: We have a tendency to kind of confabulate or make up stories that match the state that we are in. And so that's kind of what happens when we're breathing in that way.
ffd871517373.originalContext: "That way" refers to breathing patterns that activate the nervous system, such as rapid, shallow breathing through the mouth into the upper chest.

77f78c1e64fb.text: 如果你在逃避某种感受,比如不喜欢感受冲突或愤怒,那么你就会下意识地做出决定来避免感受那样的情绪。这会成为一个巨大的偏见和问题,因为人们做出决定是因为害怕感受某种方式。
77f78c1e64fb.original: If you are avoiding feeling a certain way, let's say, that they don't enjoy feeling conflict or anger, then they will make decisions subconsciously to avoid feeling that way. And it becomes a huge bias and a huge problem because people make decisions because they're afraid of feeling a certain way.

99d915318503.text: 我认为处理内心声音的最好方式是每天都尝试一个实验,用一种新的方式来回应内心的声音。我最喜欢的回应是:'哦,我看到你真的很害怕。不要担心,我就在这里陪着你,我会支持你的。'
99d915318503.original: I think the best way to work with the voice in the head is to pick an experiment every day and respond to the voice in the head in a new way every day. One of my favorite responses is, 'Oh, I see that you're really scared. Don't worry. I'm right here with you. I got you.'
99d915318503.originalContext: Hudson, an executive coach, uses "voice in the head" to refer to your inner critic or negative self-talk that undermines confidence and performance.

08a228eb256d.text: 如果你真正理解了问题所在,你就知道解决方案。你所要做的就是通过一系列实验来充分理解你内心的声音,整个问题就会消失。
08a228eb256d.context: "内心的声音"指的是你的内心批评者 - 那些创造怀疑和恐惧的内部负面自我对话。
08a228eb256d.original: If you really fully understand the problem, you know the solution. All you have to do is really fully understand the voice in your head through a series of experiments and the whole thing goes away.
08a228eb256d.originalContext: "Voice in your head" refers to your inner critic - the internal negative self-talk that creates doubt and fear.

68a31c3727a0.text: 通常在实现预期目标之前还有一些需要先解决的问题,这些问题需要先被充分理解,我称之为理解的边界。
68a31c3727a0.context: 这里指在设定和实现以目标为导向的目标之前,需要先做一些前置的理解工作。
68a31c3727a0.original: Oftentimes there's things that come before that that need to be addressed ahead of time so that you can really understand what the plan for meeting those outcomes is going to look like. And so I refer to that as the frontier of understanding.
68a31c3727a0.originalContext: "That" and "those" refer to prerequisite understanding work that must happen before teams can effectively set and achieve outcome-based goals.

8073f8528cd8.text: 如果我们先理解了实现的难度,而不是先看到了最终效果的吸引力,也许我们就不会去做了。这说明了'为什么不'和'要是'的重要性。我们真的很幸运,先看到了在浏览器上协作编辑文档的价值,因为如果先理解了实现协作的难度,我们可能就会认为'不值得去做了'。
8073f8528cd8.original: If we'd gotten it in the other order, we might not have done it. It's another good example of why not and what if, right? Where we got really lucky that we saw the what if part, that we saw how cool a document in a browser that you could collaborate on would be, because if we understood how hard the collaboration piece would've been first without understanding that value, we might've been like, 'Eh, it's not worth it. It's going to be so hard to solve that problem.'

4a845c85d3eb.text: 如果想要做出好的决策,我们需要权衡各种选择方案的利弊。在产品领域也是如此。
4a845c85d3eb.original: If you want to make good decisions, we need options and we need to evaluate the pros and cons of each. The same is true in the product world.

1187be6296d3.text: 大脑就像一个大学校园,里面有不同的学院部门。大多数人过于依赖自己的历史系,但如果把问题交给更有实验性、开放性的科学系,或者更有创意的艺术系,就能得到更好的答案。
1187be6296d3.original: The brain is like a college campus that has different departments in it. Most people rely on their history department way too much. If you instead send things to the more experimental, open-minded science department, the more creative art department, you get dramatically better answers.

bacf14979d09.text: 我给新产品经理的最佳建议就是要成为一名消费者。下载新产品,尝试使用各种产品,因为这样做会让你成为一名更出色的产品构建者。
bacf14979d09.original: My top advice for new PMs, it's just to be a consumer. To download new products, to try them out, to use all the things and try them because I think it actually makes you a better product builder.

caf865a7365f.text: 三个月的休假比人们想象的要更容易实现。如今,公司非常希望挽留员工,并且更愿意接受这样的安排。
caf865a7365f.original: A three month sabbatical is much more attainable than people think. Companies are desperate to keep people and are much more open to things like this these days.

df571bf2b50f.text: 我发现,要完全放松下来需要6到8周时间。
df571bf2b50f.context: 保羅·米勒德正在討論在休息或長期假期期間需要6-8週的時間才能從工作中徹底解脫。
df571bf2b50f.original: I've found it takes six to eight weeks just to unwind.
df571bf2b50f.originalContext: Paul Millerd was discussing how long it takes to mentally detach from work during a sabbatical or extended break.

2b2bdaeaf6a1.text: 很多人辞职时,忘记了解雇掌管他们头脑中的老板。他们没有意识到自己可以休下整个下午,和孩子们一起度过。
2b2bdaeaf6a1.context: 保罗·米勒德在讨论在休假或长期休息期间需要多长时间才能从工作中心理上脱离出来。
2b2bdaeaf6a1.original: A lot of times when people quit their jobs, they forget to fire the manager in their head. They don't realize they can take the afternoon off to spend it with their kids.

95345b320f6e.text: 有时你需要...比如说一个艺术家,你必须远离这幅画。然后你实际上会获得更多衍生品,越来越慢。
95345b320f6e.context: 布莱恩在谈论工作生活平衡策略时,解释了如何深入参与细节最初会增加工作量,但最终会腾出更多时间。

5aa447bcde53.text: 令人意外的实验是指,实验前的预估结果和实际结果差异很大,差值的绝对值很大。
5aa447bcde53.original: A surprising experiment is one where the estimated result beforehand and the actual result differ by a lot. So that absolute value of the difference is large.

3200c9b0af2a.text: 如果你过于悲观,可能就会错过实验中出现的令人惊喜的结果。你可能会勉强地做一些实验,但内心觉得'这太糟糕了,我今天必须做4个实验,因为我想当一个创业者,但是这真的太痛苦和沮丧了'。这样你就很难注意到,虽然这个东西没有起作用,但它的失败方式却很有趣。
3200c9b0af2a.original: If you're very pessimistic, you might miss the surprising result that pops out of an experiment. You might force yourself to do a bunch of experiments grudgingly, but you're like, 'You know what? I hate this. I'm doing four experiments today because I have to do it because I want to be an entrepreneur, but it sucks and everything's miserable and black.' And then you won't notice that, oh, this thing didn't work, but it didn't work in an interesting way.

500f334f33c9.text: 让我们假设我们已经运行了那个实验。你认为会是什么结果?或者让我们假设我们进行了那项用户调研。能够想象这些结果的产品经理,我认为会帮助我们更有效率,因为如果我们都觉得结果会是那样,而且这种结果也不会促使我们采取任何行动,那么为什么还要做呢?
500f334f33c9.original: Let's just pretend we ran that experiment. What do you think it'll come back with? Or let's pretend we ran that user study. And the PMs who have the ability to imagine those outcomes, I think, it helps us be much more efficient, too, because we're like, well, if we all think that it's going to go there and that's not going to compel us to take any action, why do it at all?

20fe2c55644e.text: 特威曼法则的一般说法是,任何看起来有趣或不同的数字通常都是错误的。如果结果看起来太好了,不太可能是真的,你的正常实验移动幅度不到1%,但突然有了10%的移动,那就不要着急庆祝了。
20fe2c55644e.original: Twyman's law, the general statement is if any figure that looks interesting or different is usually wrong. If the result looks too good to be true, your normal movement of an experiment is under 1% and you suddenly have a 10% movement, hold the celebratory dinner.

30e5db8ee8a2.text: 很多人将1减去P值作为处理组优于对照组的概率。这是错误的。
30e5db8ee8a2.context: P值是一个统计指标,在A/B测试中用于确定实验结果是否具有统计学意义,通常设定为0.05(5%)。
30e5db8ee8a2.original: Many people assign one minus P value as the probability that your treatment is better than control. That is wrong.
30e5db8ee8a2.originalContext: A P value is a statistical measure used in A/B testing to determine if experimental results are statistically significant, commonly set at 0.05 (5%).

3942371c50cf.text: 在Airbnb,成功率只有8%,但如果你得到一个统计学上显著的结果,P值小于0.05,那么这可能是一个假阳性结果的概率是26%,而不是5%。
3942371c50cf.context: 成功率指的是Airbnb历史上A/B测试呈现积极结果的百分比。
3942371c50cf.original: At Airbnb, where the success rate is only 8%, if you get a statistically significant result with a P value less than 0.05, there is a 26% chance that this is a false positive result. It's not 5%, it's 26%.
3942371c50cf.originalContext: The "success rate" refers to the historical percentage of A/B tests at Airbnb that showed positive results.

7ae34bd600c3.text: 我实际上常常称AI为平庸的智能,它可以帮助我快速建立平台基础。然后我再添加自己的人类思维和创造力,将其推向更高水平。但至少我可以利用AI来非常迅速地完成这个基础工作。

a4685f72332e.text: 这些项目的很多动力来自于恐惧。它不是来自于让我们为人们打造一个很棒的产品,让我们真正了解人们在与家人朋友交流时所面临的挣扎。
a4685f72332e.original: A lot of the motivation for those projects came from a place of fear. It didn't come from a place of let's make a great product for people, let's really understand the things people struggle with when communicating with family and friends.

ca786d245f00.text: 我认为人们都有这样一个深层次的东西,如果某样东西会颠覆他们的世界观,就会感到受到威胁,于是就会不得不做出艰难的选择:要么他们错了,要么它错了。而人类擅长编织故事,对于想要证明某样东西对错的人来说,编写自己的故事就变得很容易。
ca786d245f00.original: I think there's this really deep thing that people have where if something is disruptive of your worldview, it feels threatening, and you have this very stark choice to make that's either you're wrong or it's wrong. And humans are storytellers. It's very easy for us to tell stories about why something is right or wrong if we're motivated to.

ab19df1be726.text: 每个新想法一开始看起来都很蠢。不幸的是,那些真的很蠢的想法也一开始看起来很蠢。这并不能完全作为一个完美的过滤器。但是,它们越具有颠覆性,初看起来就越蠢笨。你总是要留意人们对它的评价,如果他们说这只是玩具,或者太不实际、太愚蠢,或者我完全不明白,那这通常都是一个很好的信号,说明它实际上是真正有威胁的东西。
ab19df1be726.original: Every new idea looks dumb at first. Unfortunately, the dumb ideas also look dumb at first. It's not a perfect [filter]. But the more disruptive they are, the more dumb you're going to feel they are. You always listen for stuff like if they say it's a toy or if it's practical or it's stupid or I don't get it or whatever, those are often... Toy is a good keyword. If you hear people saying something's a toy, that's often a really good signifier that it's actually something real and threatening.

862fb1c98116.text: 热爱和厌恶之间的这种两极分化,通常是你正在构建的东西是否有影响力的一个标志。如果它只得到了现代人漠不关心、略有好感或略有不快的反馈,那很可能只是一个增量型产品,并没有真正颠覆任何东西。但如果你看看ChatGPT,全世界要么惊叹'太棒了',要么大喊'太可怕了',很少有人持中立态度,那就是一个非常好的信号,说明它确实是一个真正有影响力和颠覆性的东西。
862fb1c98116.original: And that bifurcation of love it, hate it, is really how you have an idea of whether you have impact in what you're building. If you get more of the bell curve of modern indifference and maybe mild like and mild dislike, that's an incremental product. That's not really disrupting anything. But if you look at something like ChatGPT where the entire world is like, 'This is amazing.' Or, 'This is terrible.' And there's not a whole lot in between, that's a very good signifier of it being truly impactful and disruptive.

32d06e36afd6.text: 有时候无知是一种幸福,你只需要发现新的事物。我们决定一次性投资一大批公司,原本计划之后采用异步投资的常规模式,但后来发现这种批量投资方式确实有一种魔力。
32d06e36afd6.context: "批量投资"是指Y Combinator采用同时资助多家初创公司的方式,而非传统的"异步投资"方式,即一家一家地投资。
32d06e36afd6.original: Sometimes ignorance is sort of bliss and you just discover new things. We decided to fund a whole bunch at once, and then the plan was to go to asynchronous investing like normal investors, but we realized that there was something magical about this batch thing.
32d06e36afd6.originalContext: "Batch investing" refers to Y Combinator's approach of funding multiple startups simultaneously in cohorts, versus traditional "asynchronous investing" where investors fund companies one at a time.

487c255e23d8.text: 每种艺术形式和每项创新的核心都是张力。当我们推出一个新产品时,我们说这个东西可以实现X功能,这就会引发人们对未来生活的想象。如果他们爱上了这种可能性,现在就产生了张力。
487c255e23d8.original: Tension is at the heart of every art form and every innovation. What we do when we launch a new product, we say, we have this thing that can do X, and now the person is imagining what their life might be like if that were true. If they fall in love with that possibility, now there's tension.

17525a8c909a.text: 对我来说,财富就是信息不对称。世界上最好的公司都拥有不公平的信息优势。
17525a8c909a.original: To me, wealth is nothing but information asymmetry. All the best companies in the world have unfair information asymmetry.

6b654f4b5e7a.text: 每家公司的成功都建立在创始人的独特个性特质之上。Rippling的成功和Notion的成功差之千里,但在两种情况下,公司的成功都源于创始人的独特个性。
6b654f4b5e7a.context: Rippling是一家HR/薪资软件公司;Notion是一款著名的花费多年才找到产品市场契合的生产力/工作空间工具。
6b654f4b5e7a.original: Every company succeeds on the foundations of the idiosyncrasies of the founder. The idiosyncrasies of the founder. Rippling succeeds for almost the polar opposite reasons that Notion succeeds, but in both cases, the companies succeed on the idiosyncrasies of the founder.
6b654f4b5e7a.originalContext: Rippling is an HR/payroll software company; Notion is a productivity/workspace tool that famously took years to find product-market fit.

823faa4a0a83.text: 有时候,例外就是规则,当你要做一些真正具有变革性的事情时,靠寻常的方式是达不到的,没有什么特别的事情会通过普通的方式实现。
823faa4a0a83.original: Sometimes, exceptions are the rule when it comes to doing something truly transformative and nothing extraordinary is ever achieved through ordinary means.

fd960afe2e07.text: 人工通用智能只是必要条件,但还不够。大部分价值仍需要大量建设者的辛勤耕耘,将这种新能量转化为人类想要使用的东西。
fd960afe2e07.original: AGI is just necessary but not sufficient. A lot of the value is still going to require a bunch of hustle from a lot of builders to really turn that new source of energy and channel it into something that we humans want to use.

b08368e0aee9.text: 紧跟当下的可能性。这是你可以采取的一系列动作,它们就在眼前,如果你去执行,几乎可以肯定会奏效。
b08368e0aee9.original: The adjacent possible is a set of actions that you do, that you can do. They are right in front of you that if you do them, they would work, almost certainly work.

08fb6f4553d7.text: 放大你的亮点。找到什么起作用了,就去做更多。几乎总是,我们至少会有一些微小的亮点。我们就放大这些,继续前进,再找到一些新的亮点,然后再放大。
08fb6f4553d7.original: Scale your bright spots. Find what's working and do more of that. Almost all the time, we always had at least a small glimmer of a bright spot. And then we'd scale that and then we'd continue forward and we'd find some more and we'd scale those.

9d369f99caf8.text: 如果你发现某些方式效果很好,那就应该把重点放在上面,直到达到某个程度。也就是说,'好了,我们已经掌握了这个领域或者已经处理得差不多了',然后再扩展到新的领域。
9d369f99caf8.original: If you see that something is working really well, then it's almost like you should focus on doing that more until you hit some point. It's like, 'Okay, now we do have that category captured or handled as much as we want,' and we should expand to new area.

6f85d2c295f4.text: 我实际上要说服他们不要过早地分散注意力......把所有精力集中在这上面......不要被多元化分散注意力。我们会做到的。把重点更多地放在这上面,实现这些增长率,把这个打造起来。
6f85d2c295f4.context: Yuriy在建议初创公司(「他们」)专注于一个有效的增长渠道(「这个」),而不是过早地进行多元化,直到他们达到目标。
6f85d2c295f4.original: I actually have to talk them out, focusing on diversification too early... Put all of your energy... Don't get distracted with diversification. We'll get there. Lean more into this, hit this growth rates, stand this up.
6f85d2c295f4.originalContext: Yuriy is advising early-stage companies ("them") to focus on their one working growth channel ("this") rather than diversifying too early.

77331f882791.text: 我关注的是什么让你兴奋,而不是关注你认为会推动数据指标的东西。因为每次我邀请一位嘉宾,我都在想'我真的认为这个人会推动指标'。结果并没有。然后我采访一些鲜为人知的人,我就收到这样的电子邮件:'哇,那期节目真的很棒。'
77331f882791.context: Chris Hutchins讨论了他在《All the Hacks》播客中选择嘉宾的策略,而不是关注他认为会推动指标的人。
77331f882791.original: I focus on what gets you excited, not focus on what you think will move the metrics. Because every time I have a guest where I'm like, 'I really think this person's going to move the metrics.' It doesn't. And then I interview someone who no one has ever heard of, and I get these emails like, 'Wow, that was such a good episode.'
77331f882791.originalContext: Chris Hutchins hosts "All the Hacks" podcast and is discussing his guest selection strategy with interviewer Lenny.

c5f6b31e9ead.text: 除非你看到有人主动拉着产品往外拽,否则你不应该花钱。你应该默认为'不'。
c5f6b31e9ead.original: Unless you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money. You should be like, default, no.

3e87d7a6e083.text: 如果你能把决策拆分成更小的决策,我会说'这一步肯定是合理的'。它几乎肯定会收支平衡,或者最坏的情况也不会太昂贵。然后它可能会带来其他的事情,你就可以去做了。
3e87d7a6e083.original: If you can slice up your decisions into smaller and smaller decisions, I'm like, 'This next step definitely makes sense.' It will almost certainly pay for itself or the very least won't be too expensive. And then it might allow these other things to happen and you take it.

2cd88a535be3.text: 你不能通过优化来实现产品市场适配。我不管在早期阶段,如果某些东西优化了5%,那也没什么大不了的。
2cd88a535be3.original: You can't optimize your way to product market fit. I don't care at the early stages if something's optimized by 5% from an email.

022a6d53c61e.text: 如果没有首先做好定位工作,我是不会写一行代码的。
022a6d53c61e.original: I'll never write a line of code without doing positioning first.

e52a541e4866.text: 如果问10个客户或10个员工你们公司或产品是做什么的,得到的回答各不相同,那就说明你们存在定位问题。
e52a541e4866.original: You have a positioning problem if I ask 10 of your customers or 10 of your employees what the company does or what the product does. And I get multiple answers.

6e90bb1448ae.text: Slack创始团队早期做的最好的事之一就是让我们理解,这是一款工作用的工具。这让后续很多小决策瞬间变得显而易见。
6e90bb1448ae.original: One of the best things, honestly, that the early founding team at Slack did and were able to give to those of us who followed them was the understanding that this is a tool for work. And that made thousands of small decisions instant and obvious.

fa11bee3e902.text: 我们应该给用户一种思考整个市场的方式,以Help Scout为例,'看,这里有共享收件箱,还有帮助台软件,然后就是我们。不管供应商是谁,我都会把他们归到这些类别之一。'
fa11bee3e902.original: What we should be doing is giving them a way to think about the whole market and say, in the case of Help Scout, 'Look, there's shared inbox and then there's help desk software and then there's us. And I don't care who the vendor is, I'm going to put them in one of those buckets.'

735b02986a74.text: 现在的定位实质上就是:如何用一种独特的方式讲述我的产品故事...如果你是在这个背景下做定位,那你就已经决定要争夺由别人设计的24%的市场需求。
735b02986a74.original: What positioning today has become is essentially how do I tell a story about my shit in a unique way... If you're doing positioning in that context, you just decided you're fighting for 24% of the demand designed by somebody else.
735b02986a74.originalContext: The "24%" refers to the typical market share available to non-dominant players, since one company usually captures about 76% of category economics.

d1235a7c02a9.text: 一个真正的所有者从来不会说这不是我的工作。
d1235a7c02a9.original: An owner never says that's not my job.

2b06900bcd60.text: 在Deel,我们有'小手'的概念,这意味着不管你在组织中的角色如何,你都需要愿意深入到细节中,做那些繁琐的工作,而不会回避它们。
2b06900bcd60.original: At Deel we have this concept called 'little hands'. It basically means that no matter who you are, where you sit within the organization, you need to be willing to get into the little things and do the nitty-gritty work and not shy away from it.

ccb63f3df06c.text: 没有什么是他们之上的。我看到过无论是布莱恩(Brian Chesky)关注主页上的图像细节,还是杰夫·贝索斯(Jeff Bezos)著名地接收客户的电子邮件,阅读其中许多,并转发它们,他以问号邮件而闻名,为了节省时间,他会只向一个领导者转发一个问号,你就必须在24小时内找到解决方案并反馈回来。
ccb63f3df06c.original: Nothing is above them. I've seen whether it's Brian caring about the full bleed image on the homepage, whether it's Jeff Bezos who famously would receive customer emails, read many of them, forward them, and he's famous for question mark emails where for his time's sake he would just forward an email to a leader with a question mark and you would just have to figure it out and then report back in 24 hours with the resolution thereof.
ccb63f3df06c.originalContext: Brian refers to Brian Chesky, CEO of Airbnb, where Jason Shah previously worked as a product leader.

d1361dcff369.text: 我有这样的经验法则:如果我哪怕只一次想过要解雇某人,我就应该立即解雇他们。当有人表现出色时,我无法想象会解雇他们,这简直是不可能的,如果失去他们我会一团糟。
d1361dcff369.original: The kind of heuristic I have is if I ever think, should I fire this person even once, I should fire them immediately. When someone's a superstar, I can't imagine firing them. I think it's impossible, I'd be lost without them.

c5f7195e443d.text: 每次你新招聘一个人,都要在30天后问自己一个问题:如果现在重新决定,我还会雇用这个人吗?如果答案是否定的,立即解雇他们。
c5f7195e443d.original: Every time that you hire someone new, mark your calendars for 30 days down the road and ask yourself one question, knowing what I know today, would I hire this person? If the answer is no, fire them immediately.

0b85b9ceafc4.text: 如果每个人都知道在新人入职后的一个月内,只要问一句'如果现在重新决定,我还会雇用这个人吗?'结果是否定的,就应该立即解雇他们。他们已经注定要失败,而且会对你、团队其他成员和他们自己造成伤害。
0b85b9ceafc4.context: 这里的'答案'指的是问题'如果现在重新决定,我还会雇用这个人吗?'
0b85b9ceafc4.original: If everyone knows within a month and every time that you hire someone new... If the answer is no, fire them immediately. They're already set on a trajectory of not being successful and they're creating damage to you, to the rest of the team and to themselves.
0b85b9ceafc4.originalContext: "The answer" refers to the question "Would I hire this person again knowing what I know now?" asked 30 days after hiring.

bb0497ce0b8b.text: 解雇员工与招聘员工一样重要。擅于识别某人是否不合适或注定无法胜任,实际上是一种技能。
bb0497ce0b8b.original: Firing people is as important as hiring people. Getting good at identifying when someone does not belong or someone is not going to work out is actually a skill.

fa3da82ff626.text: 如果让你再次为同样的角色考虑雇用这个人,你会热情推荐吗?
fa3da82ff626.original: Would you enthusiastically rehire this person for the same role?

298e70557131.text: 从根本上说,最自私的做法就是不向别人提供反馈。当你心里有一些可以帮助某人进步的想法,却因为会让你不舒服而选择不告诉他们,这样你就是在为自己的舒适感着想,这是非常自私的。
298e70557131.original: Fundamentally, the most selfish thing you can do is withhold feedback from someone. When you think a thought that would help someone improve and you avoid giving it to them because it would make you uncomfortable. Well, you're optimizing for your own comfort, and it's fundamentally selfish.

68249700f7ad.text: 我们面试的目的是说服人们不要加入The Browser Company。如果我与某人进行面试,我不会去推销,而是说:'你有什么想问的吗?任何你想问的?我会非常诚实地告诉你,大多数人都不应该想在这里工作。'
68249700f7ad.original: Our goal of interviews is to convince people not to join The Browser Company. If I have an interview with someone, I don't pitch them and say, 'What do you want to ask me? Anything you want? I'll be super honest, most people shouldn't want to work here.'

9767b2e5e8aa.text: 引发组织难以驾驭的核心动力在于,即使每个人都积极擅长自己的工作、主动协作并勤奋努力,但随着人数增多,确定大家都同意并致力于的那个子集项目也变得愈发困难和昂贵。
9767b2e5e8aa.original: The core dynamic that makes organizations hard to navigate as they get larger, even if you assume everyone is actively good at what they do, actively collaborative and actively hardworking, is this emergent force or coordination of finding the subset of projects to work on when everyone's super busy that everyone agrees and commits to and actually works on together. And finding this coordination cost grows with the square of the number of people who are working on that thing.

7db890d5b389.text: 在公司规模很小的时候,你可以像驾驶跑车一样来引领它,作为创始人,你可以主导方向,所有人都会认可。但随着公司规模增大,就好像从跑车变成了大货车,如果你还用跑车的方式来驾驶,不仅会危险自己,也会危及他人,还会使发动机报废。
7db890d5b389.original: When the company is very small, you can drive it, you can steer it like a sports car. As a founder, you are allowed to steer. Everyone acknowledges you are allowed to steer. They're never, 'Why is he steering it that way?' So you, a founder, can help navigate an organization around an obstacle the organization cannot see or comprehend itself. The problem is as you steer, as you grow into the size, your organization goes from a sports car and you grow into the size of a big rig, if you drive a big rig like a sports car, you're going to be a danger to yourself and others on the road and you're going to grind the engine.

495c0620c3db.text: 从高级经理到总监的区别在于领导方式和所做的工作。高级经理可以凭借出色的职能胜任,但总监则需要更多的影响力、协调能力,要放手让下属自主工作,而不是亲自参与所有细节。
495c0620c3db.original: The difference between a senior manager and a director is how you lead and the work you're doing. You can get as far as senior manager by being really strong in your function, but as a director it becomes much more about influence, coordination with others, and letting go of being in all the details yourself.

ea426c76ca5b.text: 我个人是不会参与任何重要决策的。一个有能力的组织每天都在做成千上万的决定,最重要的是要招聘到可以信任并给予大量自主权的合适人才。
ea426c76ca5b.original: I personally will not be involved in really any of the decisions that matter and happen. There are thousands of decisions that an organization of any skill is making every single day. The most important thing is to really focus on hiring the right people, and that means hiring people that you can trust with a tremendous amount of autonomy.

d29a7c6b9d0d.text: 他们真的需要不断引进有经验的2倍或3倍级别的领导,因为下一阶段的增长会来得比你想象的更快。
d29a7c6b9d0d.original: They really need to keep hiring 2X and 3X leaders who have seen the next stage of growth, because it's going to be here before you know it.

abc4d19a1c2e.text: 我们发现,公司内部真正关键的分界线通常在副总裁级别。Daniel作为首席执行官,我和其他高管在C-level,然后就是拥有大量自主权的数十到数百名副总裁级别的人。
abc4d19a1c2e.context: 斯沃德斯特伦姆是 Spotify 的首席产品和技术官,他表示这种情况在大多数公司中都是普遍存在的。
abc4d19a1c2e.original: What we've found, which I don't think is very contrarian at all, I think this is the case in most companies, is around the VP level. So if you have Daniel, then you have the C level, myself and others, then you have the VP level, that is a good mix of instead of having one person in the company think, so only Daniel then and the rest just do, you have on the VP level in the company this many tens to maybe hundreds of people that have a lot of autonomy to think.
abc4d19a1c2e.originalContext: Daniel Ek is Spotify's CEO and co-founder; the speaker (Gustav Söderström) is Spotify's Chief Product and Technology Officer.

c59889c55ad4.text: 每年增长100%以上是个坏主意。50%的增长速度是最理想的,100%勉强可以承受。超过翻番就意味着要承担巨大痛苦。
c59889c55ad4.original: Growing more than 100% every year is a bad idea. The happiest growth rate is 50%, 100% is manageable. Anything more than doubling and you are signing yourself up for a world of pain.

8787d6259ccd.text: 如果把自主权过度下放到组织的末端,再加上当时我们有一支非常年轻的团队,那很可能只会产生无序混乱。你可能会有一百个小组各自为政,互不协调。
8787d6259ccd.context: Daniel Ek是Spotify的首席执行官和联合创始人,发言人Gustav Söderström是Spotify的首席产品和技术官。
8787d6259ccd.original: The problem with that is if you put autonomy very far towards the leaves of the organization, and also if you combine that with having a very junior organization, which we did back then, there's a fair chance that you're just going to produce heat. You're going to have a hundred squads with a hundred strategies running in a hundred directions.

b650dc64fd93.text: 我们如何让这份工作适合这个人,而不是试图找一个人来适应这份工作?因为当你找到好人才时,他们虽然很合适,但并不完美。然后你就放弃他们了。事实上,你可能想做的是找一种方法让这个人进来,并想办法重塑这份工作,让它适合这个人。
b650dc64fd93.original: How do I get the job to fit the person as opposed to trying to find the person to fit the job? Because when you find good people, it's like, yeah, they fit, but they're just not perfect. And then you let them go. And the reality is what you probably want to do is actually find a way to get that person in and figure out how to actually reshape the job to fit that person.

7f68e93a6d1b.text: 大多数情况下,留存有两种类型:战略性留存和战术性留存。战略性留存是作为出色的产品负责人和产品团队所做的一切,比如确定理想客户画像、产品价值实现时间、路线图规划、合适的功能、确定关键度量指标、对每一个细节的深思熟虑等。但由于你过于专注和偏重于这些,常常会忽略了我们所谓的战术性留存,如支付失败、合同优化、注销流程、脱离流程等。

40c1e5d11453.text: 我们分析了200万个注销流程,发现当有人点击注销按钮时,你只有18到30秒的时间。我们发现,你应该问两个问题:一是'你为什么要离开?'用选择题,别让他们自由回答,因为99%的回答都不太好;二是'你最喜欢产品的哪些地方?'这样做的原因是,此时用户已经下定决心要注销了,一旦你问他们喜欢什么,就能唤起他们的怀旧情绪,从而刹住他们的'离开列车'。
40c1e5d11453.original: I looked at two million cancellation flows. We built some products for this, that's why I have this data, just to be clear. But looked at two million cancellation flows and we found you have about 18 to 30 seconds when someone hits that cancel button, we found you should ask two questions. One, 'Why are you leaving?' Multiple choice. Don't do the free response. You get one out of 100 great responses, and the 99 are not great. And then the other question we found works really, really well is, 'What did you like about the product?' And the reason that works so effectively is because that person's on a freight train to basically cancel. They're like, 'I'm already done. Oh yeah, this is why I'm leaving.' And a lot of these things like what you just saw, which was kind of like a quick front-end feature request or a bug fix or adding testing and documentation or things like that. One of the things that makes a loop really nice obviously is a quick way to iterate and test.
9aee67e0bd9a.originalContext: Devin is an AI software engineering agent, and "what you just saw" refers to a live demo where Devin added a newsletter link to their website.

c1b780af43f2.text: 如果它给人一种强烈的负面感觉,那就不是一个可行的产品。那么我们如何设计产品,以应对这种不稳定且不完全准确的特性呢?
c1b780af43f2.original: If it punches in the face, that's not a viable product. And so how do you design your products assuming that this thing will be squishy and not fully accurate and fully work?
c1b780af43f2.originalContext: "This thing" refers to LLMs (Large Language Models), which Komoroske describes as "squishy computers" that don't do exactly what you tell them.

73cb842f1995.text: 弄清楚如何将其简化,使得代理可以真正理解什么是成功,什么是失败,这就是关键所在。
73cb842f1995.original: Figuring out how to boil it down so that an agent can really understand what success and failure looks like is a lot of the game.

e19aa80a7ae7.text: 我们不能再像以前那样盲目地使用它(DORA框架的四个关键指标),因为现在使用 AI 的反馈循环要早得多,不仅局限于本地构建和测试阶段,而是贯穿始终,有时甚至在开发管道的中间阶段。
e19aa80a7ae7.original: We can't just use that blindly now when we're using AI, as an example, because we have feedback loops much earlier and not even just at the local build and test phase. We have feedback loops throughout, and even sometimes in the middle of some of the pipeline.
e19aa80a7ae7.originalContext: "That" refers to the DORA framework's four key metrics mentioned earlier. "Pipeline" refers to software development and deployment pipelines.

1fd4fcd6d89a.text: 我们不能只输入一条命令就盲目地接受返回的结果。我们必须对其进行评估:是否出现了幻觉?可靠性如何?是否符合我们通常编写的风格?
1fd4fcd6d89a.original: We can't just put in a command and guess something back and accept it. We really need to evaluate it. Are we seeing hallucinations? What's the reliability? Does it meet the style that we would typically write?

3d95a575dcf0.text: B2B软件买家想要的是对市场的洞见,以及帮助权衡选择。但我们往往做不到这一点,只是简单地说'这是我们的东西,你自己来决定吧'。
3d95a575dcf0.original: What B2B software buyers want in a sales interaction is perspectives on the market and help weighing their options. And we don't do that. We're just like, 'Here's our stuff. You figure it out, it's up to you.'

66e0c9cd3ed4.text: 如果客户犹豫不决,再加上FOMO效应只会让情况更糟。这样他们反而更不可能完成交易。
66e0c9cd3ed4.original: If a customer is indecisive, throwing FOMO into the mix makes it worse. So they're less likely to close the deal if you throw that in.

cf872b3f0731.text: 在典型的B2B采购流程中,我们通常会有一个'项目冠军'。这个人被指派负责选择,比如选择会计软件或者CRM系统,然后向团队推荐。
cf872b3f0731.original: In a typical B2B purchase process, we've got someone in that buying team is what we would call the champion. So that person is the person who's been tasked with, hey, pick us the accounting software or pick us the CRM, you figure it out.

4a66bbe09ea3.text: 我总是告诉工程师们,拥有技术债务对我们来说是一种幸运,因为这意味着人们正在使用这款产品。
4a66bbe09ea3.original: And I try to remind the engineers, we would be so lucky to have tech debt because that means people are using the product.

e74578342d94.text: 作为一家初创公司,我认为你的任务就是承担技术债务,因为这是你能比大公司更快地运营的方式。
e74578342d94.original: I actually think as a startup your job is to take on technical debt because that is how you operate faster than a bigger company.

8357ff030824.text: 很长一段时间以来,Simon一直很擅长避免过早优化,所以Notion一直都运行在一个PostgreSQL数据库实例上...所以有一个末日倒计时,当我们彻底用完在Notion中存储一切的空间时,Notion就会完全关闭。
8357ff030824.context: 西蒙是Notion的首席技术官,他倡导避免过早优化,这差点导致Notion公司关闭,因为它一直运行在单一的PostgreSQL数据库实例上。
8357ff030824.original: For the longest time, Simon's really good at don't do premature optimization, so for the longest time, we Notion runs on one instance of Postgres database... So there's a doomsday clock that when we're going to truly run out of this space to store everything in Notion and Notion got a complete shutdown.
8357ff030824.originalContext: Simon is Notion's CTO who advocated against premature optimization, leading Notion to run on a single PostgreSQL database instance that nearly caused the company to shut down.

c0e47f4a7a29.text: 你有一个技术债务的运行时间。一旦你用完了,一旦你承担了太多的债务...你就会陷入麻烦。
c0e47f4a7a29.original: You have a technical debt runway. Once you run out, once you've taken on too much debt... you'll get in trouble.

5acb86bb5fba.text: 40到60%的B2B采购过程最终无结果。挖掘这些数据,大部分不是因为他们认为现有的方案更好而不做新的决定。事实并非如此。实际上,大多数是因为他们无法自信地做出选择。
5acb86bb5fba.original: 40 to 60% of B2B purchase processes end in no decision. If you scratch on that data, the majority of those aren't saying, 'Well, I'm not making a decision to buy something new because the old thing we were doing is better.' That's not true at all. In fact, the majority of those is they couldn't figure out how to make a choice confidently.

767304017359.text: 大多数B2B软件买家都是第一次购买这类产品。他们的上级要求他们'找一个CRM并评估所有的CRM,然后做出决定'。
767304017359.original: Most of the folks in B2B software, most of the time, your buyer has never purchased software like yours before. This is the first time they've done it. And their bosses come to them and said, 'Hey, figure this out. Go find us a CRM and look at all the CRMs and figure it out.'

468c7b3af3d0.text: 交易的推动者还有一个次要任务,就是如何在不被解雇的情况下做出决定?我们需要帮助他们完成这个任务,否则我们就无法得到我们想要的,也就是交易金额。
468c7b3af3d0.original: There is this secondary job that the champion of the deal is, and that's how do I make a decision without getting fired? And so we got to help them accomplish that job, otherwise we don't get what we want, which is the money.

88cd8dd27b23.text: 产品工作的圣杯就是参考客户。这是指使用过你的解决方案或产品并对其情有独钟的人,愿意向他人推荐。
88cd8dd27b23.original: The holy grail of product work is really a reference customer. This is somebody that has used your solution or your product, loves it enough to tell people about it.

ce133de92660.text: 出于这个原因,我认为我们可以略过'空盒子问题',因为当人们通过线上线下观察彼此时,就能获得大量学习。
ce133de92660.context: 所谓'空盒子问题'指的是通用平台面临的挑战,用户不知道如何使用这种工具。
ce133de92660.original: For that reason, I think we get to skip the empty box problem a little bit because so much learning is happening out of product as people are watching each other either in IRL or online.
ce133de92660.originalContext: The "empty box problem" refers to the challenge horizontal platforms face when users don't know what to do with a general-purpose tool.

a3db80707905.text: 我认为产品有两个部分:一是构建未来,朝着使命和使命支柱发展;另一个是聆听社区的意见,构建他们所需的东西。
a3db80707905.original: I think there's two parts to product. One is building the future and towards the mission and the mission pillars. And the other is actually listening to our community and building what they want.

e25e25183101.text: 优势和弱点并非非黑即白的二元对立。它就像一个滚动调节器,在某些情况下是优势,在其他情况下则是劣势。
e25e25183101.context: 朱尔斯提到人的优势可能会变成弱点,取决于具体情况,"strengthen"是一个错误,应该是"strengths"。
e25e25183101.original: Strengthen and weakness, it's not a binary thing. It's like the same thing, but it's a dial. In some context it's good, in other contexts it's serving you.
e25e25183101.originalContext: Jules is discussing how personal strengths can become weaknesses depending on the situation, with "strengthen" being a typo for "strengths."

4f155f2a8c92.text: 不要放弃你热爱的产品建设和设计细节。即使公司需要做扩大规模、市场推广和运营等其他事情,也不要丢失你热爱的本质。
4f155f2a8c92.original: Don't step away from the details that both you love. If your passion is building product and product design, even if it feels like at times the company needs to do all this other stuff like scale up, go to market, and operations... Don't lose the essence of the thing that you love doing.

a5029a0be09b.text: 你需要针对自己的擅长之处进行优化。如果你才25岁,职业生涯还很早期,很难说'好,这些就是我的弱点,我需要去改善它们'。
a5029a0be09b.original: You need to optimize for what you're great at. If you're 25 years old early in your career, it's very hard at that point to say, 'Oh, here are all my weaknesses and I need to improve on those.'

f04c319c2e37.text: 新公司往往是因为你之前公司的价值观而聘用你,但不一定是你的行为方式。
f04c319c2e37.original: Most likely the new place hires you because of the values of the organization you left, but not the behaviors.

84fd4cefe074.text: 你不擅长某件事,和公司在某个特定时期不需要那件事是不同的。你也可能擅长某件事,但不符合公司当前的需求。
84fd4cefe074.original: There is a difference between you not being good at something and a business or company not needing that thing at a particular moment in time, or you being very good at something but not in the way that a company needs.

93ac197e46a5.text: 拥有多位导师是更好的选择。你应该每月与不同的3-4位导师见面一次。
93ac197e46a5.original: It's actually better to have a stable of mentors. You want to have three or four. And ideally, what you do is you meet with each one of them once a month on a different Friday of the month.

606eefb36180.text: 在日常工作中,优秀的产品经理会像六岁孩子一样提出很多"为什么"。
606eefb36180.original: Day-to-day, good PMs will be asking 'why' as much as my six-year-old son does, which is a lot.

5abf740b79d5.text: 我在选择产品经理时,以及在回顾过去与优秀同事的合作经历中,都发现一个共同的特质就是永不满足的好奇心 - 一种对了解事物的无休止的渴望,以及毫无畏惧地承认自己不懂并坚持探寻答案的意愿。
5abf740b79d5.original: One of the traits that I look for in PMs that I hire onto my teams, and also when I think back to the people that I've learned a lot from working with over the years, one of the common behaviors or traits is relentless curiosity, this insatiable desire to understand things and a lack of fear in admitting when they don't understand things and being uncompromising and getting the answers so that they do understand.

fbf2cd9c41da.text: 我认为这种自以为无所不知、过于自信的幻象会让人流于倡导而非探究。
fbf2cd9c41da.original: I would say this illusion that you have to be all-knowing and super confident sets you up to be in a place of advocacy instead of inquiry.

cf010b0c6cc6.text: 如果你能倾听并知道从何处寻找答案,那本身就是一种非常理想的状态。
cf010b0c6cc6.original: If you listen and you know where to go to get the answers, that in itself is like a tremendous place to be.

99e4eec20e77.text: 我提出这些问题的目的并非是去烦扰他人,而是想真正理解其中的内容。
99e4eec20e77.context: "那里"指的是Thawar提出其他人认为愚蠢的问题的情况,"那个人"指的是批评他提问的同事。
99e4eec20e77.original: My goal there is not to annoy the person, but it's to understand the content.
99e4eec20e77.originalContext: "There" refers to situations where Thawar asks questions that others consider stupid, and "the person" refers to colleagues who criticize his questions.

70a8f22432f8.text: 要打造出优秀的 AI 产品,你需要在构建评估系统方面非常擅长。这是你可以参与的最高 ROI 的活动。
70a8f22432f8.context: "评估系统"是指用于测试和衡量 AI 模型在产品应用中性能的系统。
70a8f22432f8.original: To build great AI products, you need to be really good at building evals. It's the highest ROI activity you can engage in.
70a8f22432f8.originalContext: "Evals" refers to evaluation systems used to test and measure AI model performance in product applications.

3b612b69765e.text: 每个做这件事的人都会上瘾。当你在建造 AI 应用程序时,你会学到很多。
3b612b69765e.context: "这件事"指的是构建评估系统 - 用于测量 AI 应用程序性能和质量的系统化测试。
3b612b69765e.original: Everyone that does this immediately gets addicted to it. When you're building an AI application, you just learn a lot.
3b612b69765e.originalContext: "This" refers to building evaluations (evals) - systematic tests to measure AI application performance and quality.

583b32f99cf0.text: 戴上产品经理的帽子,深入研究,这真的很好吗?这就是乐趣所在。你在看数据。就像,好的,你在注释一些东西。实际上,我昨天刚在看一个客户的数据,完全是同样的过程。这确实很有趣。
583b32f99cf0.context: "同样的过程"指的是错误分析 - 系统地审查 AI 应用程序的输出,以识别问题。"注释一些东西"意味着将数据示例标记为正确或错误。
583b32f99cf0.original: Put your product hat on and get into, is this really good? That's where the fun part is. You're looking at data. It's like, okay, you're annotating things. Actually, I was just looking at a client's data yesterday, the same exact process. It's a lot of fun, actually.
583b32f99cf0.originalContext: "The same exact process" refers to error analysis - systematically reviewing AI application outputs to identify problems. "Annotating things" means labeling data examples as correct or incorrect.

9c0167096b16.text: 戴上产品经理的帽子,深入研究,这真的很好吗?这就是乐趣所在。
9c0167096b16.original: Put your product hat on and get into, is this really good? That's where the fun part is.

3df29427c119.text: 每当你说是于某件事，就意味着你已经在说否于另一件事。
3df29427c119.original: Every time you say yes to something, by definition you're saying no to something else.

666f99789839.text: 你所面临的任务并不完全相等。事实上，在这样的角色中，你最终会做三种不同类型的任务。
666f99789839.original: All your tasks are not created equal. There are actually three type of tasks that you end up doing in such a role.

08902e5b3312.text: 能够管理好我的精力水平，并找到如何合理安排时间以维持我的精力,这真的让我能够在任何情况下保持积极乐观的心态。
08902e5b3312.original: Being able to manage my energy levels and figuring out how to schedule my time for my energy has really allowed me also to figure out how to have that abundant mindset in all situations.

d1bc1cee8eb2.text: 我们发现非常重视人工智能的工程团队每周报告节省8到10个小时。每当我听到这样的数据,我认为这是这种情况的最坏情况。这现在是新的基线。事实是,价值每天都在变化,所以你需要与之同步前进。
d1bc1cee8eb2.original: We find engineering teams that are very, very AI forward are reporting about eight to 10 hours saved per week. Whenever I hear a stat like this, I think an important element is this is the worst it will ever be. This is now the baseline. The truth is the value is changing every day, so you need to ride that wave along with it.

cc2eec8cd647.text: 非技术人员使用人工智能代理和编程工具来构建东西,这真的令人惊讶和非常amazing。能够拥抱这些工具,优化自己的工作日和特定任务的人,才是从这些工具中获得最大影响的人。
cc2eec8cd647.original: The non-technical people using AI agents and programming tools to build things is really what's been surprising and really amazing. The people that are able to embrace it to optimize for their particular work day and their particular set of tasks are really who are showing the most impact from these tools.

f9fd5e142254.text: 通常,我会花3到4天的时间与任何人合作进行初步的错误分析。这是一次性成本。一旦我发现如何将其集成到单元测试中,或者我有一个自动运行样本的脚本,之后可能每周只需要30分钟。
f9fd5e142254.context: "这"指的是Shreya之前在对话中描述的用于评估人工智能产品的错误分析过程。
f9fd5e142254.original: Usually, I'll spend three to four days really working with whoever to do initial rounds of error analysis. This is one-time cost. Once I figured out how to integrate that in unit tests, or I have a script that automatically runs it on samples, I would say maybe 30 minutes a week after that.
f9fd5e142254.originalContext: "This" refers to the error analysis process for AI product evaluation that Shreya described earlier in the conversation.

56c2fd08521b.text: 他讨厌他们的想法,保罗试图让布赖恩、乔和内特改变它。但我记得特别是乔拿出了麦片盒子,奥巴马 O's 和 Cap'n McCain's,我就想,哇,他们会尽自己所能努力让这家公司成功。
56c2fd08521b.context: 布赖恩、乔和内特是 Airbnb 的创始人,当他们经济困难时,创造了新奇的麦片盒子(奥巴马 O's 和 Cap'n McCain's)来筹钱。
56c2fd08521b.original: He hated their idea, and Paul tried to get Brian and Joe and Nate to change it. But I remember specifically Joe brought out the cereal boxes, the Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's, and I just thought, oh my God, they're going to work hard to do whatever they can to make this company succeed.
56c2fd08521b.originalContext: Brian, Joe, and Nate are Airbnb's founders who created novelty cereal boxes (Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's) to raise money when struggling financially.

79607f9574d5.text: 高主动性就是找到一种方法来得到你想要的,而不需要等待条件完美或怪罪环境。
79607f9574d5.original: High agency is about finding a way to get what you want without waiting for conditions to be perfect or otherwise blaming the circumstances.

a135a1981e78.text: 你需要有那种绝望。你必须烧掉那艘船。我们发现那些仍然有工资和医疗保险的创始人,一旦遇到困难,就不会辞职。
a135a1981e78.original: You sort of need that desperation. You have to burn the boat. We found that founders who were still getting a paycheck and health insurance, once the going got tough, they did not quit their job.

5583e524f5af.text: 你需要有一种疯狂的、几乎像现实扭曲场的东西,你听不到 no 这个词,或者至少你会把它翻译成'还没'。
5583e524f5af.original: You need to have insane, almost like reality distortion field where you don't hear the word no, or at the very least, you translate it into a not yet.

47254ce9df41.text: 从不让自己的技能阻碍你去出去做一个推销,然后把它变成现实,这是非常重要的。
47254ce9df41.original: Never letting your own skills stop you from going out there making a pitch and then turning that into reality is really important.

6a7f64ef7bc8.text: 像对待Linear或JIRA工单一样与这个东西交谈。像对你团队里的开发人员说话一样与它交谈。
6a7f64ef7bc8.context: 这个"东西"指的是Simons公司构建的Bolt人工智能编码助手。
6a7f64ef7bc8.original: Talk to this thing like you do a Linear ticket, or a JIRA ticket. Talk to this like you would, like you're talking to one of the developers on your team.
6a7f64ef7bc8.originalContext: "This thing" refers to Bolt, the AI coding assistant that Simons' company built.

9a6a5b568b64.text: 与人工智能交互,明确表达预期并指出哪些部分正常哪些部分不正常比与人类交互更为重要。
9a6a5b568b64.original: Explaining exactly what you expect and what you're not getting is even more important with AI than with the humans.

1da6bcc074ae.text: 不要说它不起作用,只需准确解释你的期望以及哪些部分正常哪些部分异常。
1da6bcc074ae.original: Don't say it doesn't work. Just explain exactly what you're expecting and which parts are working and which parts are not working.

9946b52c0393.text: 我有一个俗气的Chrome扩展程序,每次打开新标签页它都会问,'你现在要做的事情,怎么能利用人工智能来完成呢?'
9946b52c0393.original: I have a cheesy Chrome extension. Literally whenever I open a new tab, it just says, how can you use AI to do what you're going to do right now?

74adbefd2606.text: 你不想与这些模型对抗。这就像计算器问世时,你不想让人们做所有这些算术运算,而是告诉他们,'使用这些工具,看看你能做些什么吧。'
74adbefd2606.original: You don't want to fight against them using the models. It's similar to when the calculator came out, you don't want to give people all of this arithmetic work of how do you get them to do it and not use the calculator. You want to tell them, 'Use the tools and let's see what you can do.'

4b7227300abf.text: 您实际上必须做好准备才能表现出自发性。这看似矛盾,但如果您想想运动或爵士音乐,您就会明白当然需要提前准备和练习。
4b7227300abf.original: You actually have to prepare to be spontaneous. And that's counterintuitive, but when you think about it in athletics or jazz music, it's like of course you would prepare and practice.

c7dd8e588719.text: 我发现保持简洁的唯一解决方案就是做好充分准备。这不是一个很吸引人的解决方案,但我进入会议、对话或路演时越清楚,就越能简洁明了地把重点突出出来。
c7dd8e588719.original: The only solution I found consistently to being concise is preparation. It's not a very glamorous solution by any means, but the clearer I am going into a meeting, going into a conversation, going into a pitch, the better I am at being concise and being able to bring the conversation back to the most important points.
