0c1e87767bd5.text: 真正的问题是,人们想知道他们会遇到什么。我们需要更好地展示这些房源...你的擅长领域是什么?比如说对于Airbnb,我们在运营方面并不太擅长。
0c1e87767bd5.context: 背景:发言人讨论短期租赁/酒店平台领域的挑战,其中"这些房源"指的是在平台上列出的租赁属性。
0c1e87767bd5.original: The real problem is people want to know what they're getting themselves into. We need to represent the homes a lot better... What's in your wheelhouse? So for example, Airbnb, we weren't that strong in operations.
0c1e87767bd5.originalContext: Context: The speaker is discussing challenges in the vacation rental/hospitality platform space, where "the homes" refers to rental properties listed on platforms.

ed4e8cf63b61.text: 我们如何找到我们想成为什么样的人,而不是我们目前不是或希望成为或看到其他参与者在这个领域所做的?
ed4e8cf63b61.original: How do we figure out what we want to be when we grow up versus what we currently aren't or wish that we were or see other players in the space being?

662f4f4fa972.text: 不同已经不够,因为很容易就能打造一些与现有不同的东西,只需要看看现有的就可以了。更好也是不够的,因为也很容易说'我会让这个东西更好,并且收取更高的价格'。必须比现有的更好,并且对最终用户来说是有价值的。
662f4f4fa972.original: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today, because you just have to look at what exists today and build something else. Being better is not enough, because it's also easy to say, 'Hey, I'm going to make this thing better, and just charge you more money for it.' It has to be better than what exists today in a way that matters to the end user.

5ef79ad1be0f.text: 我认为采用一个产品、购买一个产品或转换到一个产品的人,有两个驱动力。一个是新解决方案的吸引力,这就是差异化。但另一方面,还有一个准入门槛或者说基本要求。
5ef79ad1be0f.original: I think people who adopt a product, or buy a product, or switch to a product, there's two driving forces. One is the attraction of the new solution, and that's basically differentiation. But, on the other side, there's a entry requirement or table stakes.

af41341436e9.text: 要想让一个产品产生影响,它必须至少比现有的要好2到3倍,人们才会说'你知道吗?这个产品提供了足够的价值,值得我可能改变成本'。
af41341436e9.context: 这里的'X'指的是比现有产品好2-3倍或更有效
af41341436e9.original: For a product to make a difference, it has to be at least two, three more X for people to say, 'You know what? This is offering enough value for me to maybe make a switch in cost.'
af41341436e9.originalContext: The "X" refers to times better or more effective - meaning a product needs to be 2-3 times better than alternatives.

7797bdf8a4ac.text: 一旦你成为一种比较对象,一旦你成为他们正在测试的三个选项之一,你就已经有点失去了。这完全是关于差异化的。
7797bdf8a4ac.original: As soon as you become a comparison, as soon as you become one of three that they're testing out, you've already sort of lost. It's all about differentiation.

428264c628a0.text: 有功能特性,然后还有为什么我应该首先使用这个东西。
428264c628a0.original: There's feature and functionality and then there's like why should I use this thing in the first place?

cbc320d6c054.text: 我们已经不再处于'勉强够用就行'的时代了。勉强够用是不够的,这已经是平庸了。如果你想在软件游戏中获胜,你需要通过设计来实现差异化。细节很重要。
cbc320d6c054.original: We're no longer in this era of good enough is fine. Good enough is not enough. It's mediocre. If you want to win in the game of software, you need to differentiate through design. Craft matters.

02054b319326.text: 新的语言会创造新的思维,语言的划分点会创造思维的划分点,进而创造感知价值的划分点。
02054b319326.original: New languaging creates new thinking, and a demarcation point in language creates a demarcation point in thinking, which can create a demarcation point in perceived value.

61c5c728d5d2.text: 创造出行业语言的公司就赢得了市场。
61c5c728d5d2.original: The company that creates the languaging for the category wins.

64af69afb8f6.text: 最关键的是命名它,命名那个'旧的游戏'。你看到的那些例子,软件、云计算、交易、订阅意见、现实。这种简洁明了的命名是关键所在。
64af69afb8f6.context: "旧的游戏"指的是他的战略性故事框架,而那些例子(软件、云计算、交易、订阅等)是他在成功公司的定位演示文稿中分析的转变。
64af69afb8f6.original: What's really, I think key is naming it, naming that old game. The examples you saw, software, cloud, transactions, subscription opinions, reality. This very, very concise naming is really key.
64af69afb8f6.originalContext: "The old game" refers to his strategic narrative framework, and the examples (software, cloud, transactions, subscription, etc.) are shifts he analyzed in successful company positioning decks.

45602026fc68.text: 我们一直在看每一个我们写的副本,问自己'这可能是其他公司写的吗?这是不是任何其他公司,还是只有Duolingo?是什么让它成为Duolingo特有的?'
45602026fc68.original: We constantly looked at every copy we wrote and asked, 'Could this have been written by other companies? Could this have been any other company or is it Duolingo? What makes this Duolingo?'

a2a793d98e8b.text: 这三个词是行不通的。看看Gong,其实其他公司已经在使用'收入情报'这个术语了。但是有了Gong,它突然成为一个'事物',因为我认为他们有这个'从意见到现实'的故事支撑着它。
a2a793d98e8b.context: "这三个词"指的是公司创造来定义其市场定位的行业术语。"从意见到现实的故事"是Raskin提出的战略性故事框架,展示从主观到客观见解的转变。
a2a793d98e8b.original: These three words aren't going to do it. Take Gong, I mean already other companies were using this term revenue intelligence. With Gong, it suddenly becomes a thing because I think they have this opinions-to-reality story behind it.
a2a793d98e8b.originalContext: "These three words" refers to category names that companies create to define their market position. "Opinions-to-reality story" is Raskin's framework for strategic narratives showing transformation from subjective to objective insights.

8b1ba1f4f375.text: 建立一个很棒的产品是必要的,但并不充分。实际上,关键在于那些打造了出色分销渠道的人。
8b1ba1f4f375.original: Building a great product is one of those things that's necessary, but not sufficient. And actually the separation is between those that build really great distribution.

8a708ce2afa5.text: 人类数据唯一的护城河就是获取受众的渠道。
8a708ce2afa5.original: The only moat in human data is access to an audience.

d21a7205a62f.text: 无偿提供是一个关键因素。我认为任何人都能够打造出类似的东西。可能在建模方面不会像它那么出色,但我认为也能引起轰动。
d21a7205a62f.original: Making it free was a big deal. I think anyone could have built something like this. It might not have been quite as good on the modeling side, but I think it would've taken off.
d21a7205a62f.originalContext: Nick Turley is discussing OpenAI's decision to make ChatGPT free at launch, with "this" referring to ChatGPT and "modeling" referring to AI language models.

8baa3e0a11f8.text: 不要称之为'战略',而要称之为'行动议程'。开始努力确定可以实际解决的一个或两个关键挑战,以及我们将如何应对?我们将采取哪些一致的行动来应对这些挑战?
8baa3e0a11f8.original: Don't call it strategy, call it an action agenda. Begin to try to identify the one or two key challenges that can actually be addressed and what are we going to do about it? What are the coherent actions we're going to do to take these on?

13da72512f5c.text: 产品战略栈的目标是帮助人们将通常混在一起的术语,如目标、路线图和策略,分成真正明确定义的部分。
13da72512f5c.original: The goal of the product strategy stack is to help people take a set of terms that are normally conflated together, like goals, roadmap, strategy, and separate them into really clearly defined parts.

e2ded6dc96b2.text: 将战略讨论和OKR讨论分开是至关重要的。这听起来很明显,但这确实是一个非常常见的错误。一个很简单的问题就是,我们是否有一个独立的战略过程或战略仪式,与OKR设置和指标设置以及目标设置是分开的?
e2ded6dc96b2.original: It's critical to disconnect strategy discussions from OKR discussions. And it sounds really obvious, but it's I think a very common mistake. And I think a really simple question to ask yourself is do we have a separate strategy process or strategy ritual that is distinct from OKR setting and metric setting and goal setting?

d3edbf7498a9.text: 不应该将路线图包括在策略文件中,因为策略文件应该与路线图是分开的。它应该是你的路线图的配套文件。
d3edbf7498a9.original: It's important not to include a roadmap as part of a strategy doc, because a strategy doc is meant to be separate from the roadmap. It's meant to be a companion to your roadmap.

f7bd3250ab2c.text: 如果你真的有一个大家都认同的真正的产品策略,那么我们通常在年度规划中做的很多无用功实际上就会消失。
f7bd3250ab2c.original: If you have a real product strategy, a real one that everybody is aligned with, that you have got pre-alignment on, then a lot of this nonsense we tend to do with annual planning actually goes away.

cc9a521589be.text: 我认为人们太频繁地从目标开始,然后创建路线图,结果就是目标占据了主导地位,没有任何背景和最终推动这些目标的原则。
cc9a521589be.original: I think what happens too often when people start with goals and then create the roadmap is that the goal takes precedence and there's no context, there's no principles that are ultimately driving that.

229917e08880.text: 我认为由于我们并不完全了解未来很快就会出现什么样的能力,也不知道从技术角度来说什么会奏效,以及什么样的东西即使技术上可行也可能无法着陆,对我们来说更重要的是保持谦逊,大量依靠经验学习,并快速尝试新事物。
229917e08880.original: I think because we don't exactly know what capabilities will even come up soon and we don't know what's going to work technically, and then we also don't know what's going to land even if it works technically, it's much more important for us to be very humble and learn a lot more empirically and just try things quickly.

3bf4f0dc065a.text: 在我之前工作的每一个地方,你都大致知道正在使用什么样的技术,但在 AI 领域并非如此。每隔两个月,计算机就能做到之前做不到的事,这要求你从根本上重新思考你正在做的事情。
3bf4f0dc065a.original: Everywhere I've ever worked before this, you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI. Every two months, computers can do something they've never been able to do before and you need to completely think differently about what you're doing.

d98355335204.text: 你希望能对这种变化保持弹性。当能力下降时,你要能够迅速行动。因此,保持敏捷,不被路线图束缚住,能够立即转变优先事项,这将变得非常重要。
d98355335204.context: "那种变化"指的是 AI 能力的快速变化,"当能力下降"意味着像 Anthropic 这样的公司发布新的 AI 功能。
d98355335204.original: You want to be resilient to that change. When capabilities drop, you want to be able to jump on it really quickly. So being agile, not being stuck with roadmaps, being able to just say, oh, we're just going to switch priorities right away, is going to be super important.
d98355335204.originalContext: "That change" refers to rapid shifts in AI capabilities, and "when capabilities drop" means when new AI features are released by companies like Anthropic.

5ac9d74030ae.text: 放下你已经建立的东西。回到你试图解决的目标,然后利用这项新技术,看看如何更好地达成这个目标。
5ac9d74030ae.original: Let go of what you've built. Go back to the objectives you were trying to solve and now with this technology, how can you do that objective better?

dc6b912bd1d5.text: 我们会考虑这是什么季节?第一季可能是 AI 的原型制作,然后就是关于模型和推理模型,现在是智能代理的时代。这可能持续一年,也可能持续六个月,甚至三个月。
dc6b912bd1d5.original: We think about it as what season are we in? Season one might've been prototyping of AI and then it was all around models and reasoning models, and now it's the advent of agents. That can last a year, that can last six months, that can last three months.

967b60050468.text: 不要为今天而建,要为未来六个月,一年而建。那些现在只有 20% 有效的东西,将来会 100% 有效。
967b60050468.original: Don't build for today, build for six months from now, build for a year from now. The things that aren't quite working that are working 20% of the time, will start working 100% of the time.

15d50b05d9a2.text: 前期有很多你无法预知的东西。所以如果一开始就追求虚假的精确性,那只是在自我安慰,让你觉得没有不确定性。但事实是,不确定性随处可见,时时存在。
15d50b05d9a2.original: There's tons of stuff you can't know ahead of time. So if you're getting a false precision at the beginner, that's a comfort blanket. That's just helping you feel like there isn't uncertainty. There's uncertainty everywhere all the time.

3f1931603b2a.text: 越是远期规划,就越是在凭空臆测。我们都明白这一点。
3f1931603b2a.original: The further out you plan, the more you're making it up. We know this.

4729e47be819.text: 决定笔记分享内容的代码必须公开。支撑这些的所有数据和评级也必须公开。人们应该能够获取代码和数据,并复制整个服务。
4729e47be819.context: "笔记"指的是 Twitter 的众包事实核查功能 Community Notes,它为可能误导性的推文添加上下文。
4729e47be819.original: The code that decides what notes share has to be out in the open. All of the data and ratings that make it happen have to be out in the open. People should be able to take the code and data and replicate the whole service.
4729e47be819.originalContext: "Notes" refers to Community Notes, Twitter's crowdsourced fact-checking feature that adds context to potentially misleading tweets.

27199d52dc1f.text: 我们没有任何按钮可以改变笔记的状态。所以如果一条笔记显示出来是因为人们评级认为有帮助,它就会一直显示。我们无法改变这一点。
27199d52dc1f.original: We don't have a button that will change the status of a note. So if a note is showing because the people have rated it and found it helpful, it is going to show. We can't change that.

cf5887232af2.text: 每个帖子都有资格获得笔记。我们不应该豁免埃隆。我们不应该豁免政府人物。我们应该像对待所有人一样... 甚至广告客户也可以获得笔记。
cf5887232af2.context: Community Notes 是 X/Twitter 的众包事实核查功能,用户可以为可能误导性的帖子添加上下文性更正。
cf5887232af2.original: Every post is eligible for notes. We shouldn't exempt Elon. We shouldn't exempt government figures. We should be like everyone... Even advertisers can get notes.
cf5887232af2.originalContext: Community Notes is X/Twitter's crowdsourced fact-checking feature where users can add contextual corrections to potentially misleading posts.

97d395a8d3e0.text: 我给自己教了一个新的短语,叫做'害怕纽约时报的头条'。要意识到,如果亚马逊发生任何问题,它会立即登上所有新闻网站的头条。
97d395a8d3e0.original: I taught myself a new phrase which was fear the New York Times headline. Be aware that if Amazon is down, it goes up on every news website immediately.

2efc39c04503.text: 切换模式与学习、发展和成就感密切相关。你可能想与其他人合作。正如塔克曼模型所述,有 forming（聚集）、storming（冲突）、norming（建立规则）和 performing（有效工作）这几个阶段。不过,有时候我们会停留在一个团队太久,陷入停滞期。
2efc39c04503.original: Switching pattern is really tied to learning and development and fulfillment. It could be that you want to work with other people. Like forming, storming, norming, performing, Tuckman's model, he forgot the phase called stagnating. Sometimes it feels like we're in a team for too long.

fe7e3769c774.text: 塔克曼模型描述了团队发展的阶段:forming（聚集）、storming（冲突）、norming（建立规则）和 performing（有效工作)。
fe7e3769c774.original: Sometimes you have that awesome team situation. It's an enjoyable experience. People are learning. You're looking forward to it every day. But the thing is, maybe that's a small startup that grows and you need to grow because you have a bigger vision and it needs to be more than these 10 people.

b4886c9307f4.text: 指的是在不同团队之间轮换团队成员。
b4886c9307f4.original: Even if you did, it would soon be obsolete because we did a really good job and now we've grown 2X or something and the process needs to change. The main thing I care about is are we just getting better every week, every month, certainly every year.

1ad32c7fa2b6.text: 有时候你会有一个很棒的团队,这是一种令人愉悦的体验。大家都在学习,每天都期待。但是,也许这是一家小型初创公司,随着公司的成长和愿景的扩大,需要扩大团队,不能只有这10个人。
1ad32c7fa2b6.original: Reteaming is hard. Reorgs are hard. You can't lump them all into one thing with oh, it's all great all the time. No, it's not. If we could just build the software, deliver to the customer, get the product market fit, hey, have we delighted them or not? If only it could be that easy. No, we have the people layer, so let's focus there too.

cb02210b7174.text: 太多创始人都在为他们想要如何经营公司而道歉。他们试图在自己想要的运营方式和他们所领导的人员想要的方式之间找到一个平衡点。这只会让所有人都感到痛苦。因为每个人真正想要的是清晰性。每个人真正想要的是能够迅速朝着同一个方向前进。
cb02210b7174.original: Way too many founders apologize for how they want to run the company. They find some midpoint between how they want to run a company and how the people they lead want to run the company. That's a good way to make everyone miserable. Because what everyone really wants is clarity. And what everyone really wants is to be able to row in the same direction really quickly.

7ed18a8b270f.text: 成为创始人是一种状态,是一种态度。成为CEO则是一项技艺。更多的创始人能够接受这两者是分开的,同时也都同样重要于建立一家成长型创业公司,我们所有人都将受益。
7ed18a8b270f.original: To be a founder is a state of being, it's an attitude. To be a CEO is a craft. The more founders who can accept that those are two separate things and they're both equally important to build an ascendant startup, the better all of us will be.

6ef96fb02289.text: 很多CEO之所以做得很好,是因为他们很好地遵循了创始人的'法则'。这些原则是给予我的,我会坚持下去并把它变得更大。
6ef96fb02289.original: A lot of CEOs have done well because they follow the 'dharma' of the founders quite well. These are the principles that were given to me and I'm going to sustain this and make it even bigger.

9c229441f98c.text: "创始人模式"让我很生气。这真的感觉就像是一个借口。我们在给创始人一种许可,不去学习这份工作。
9c229441f98c.context: "创始人模式"指的是一个流行的管理概念,建议创始人应该保持亲自动手,而不是像传统管理者那样授权。
9c229441f98c.original: Founder mode gets me angry. It really felt like an excuse. We were giving founders a permission to not learn the job.
9c229441f98c.originalContext: "Founder mode" refers to a popular management concept suggesting founders should stay hands-on rather than delegating like traditional managers.

0b68823e005c.text: 优秀公司都有一个很小的黄金仪式清单。这些黄金仪式有三个特点:第一,它们都有特定名称;第二,每个员工在第一个周五就能知道它们;第三,它们都有标准模板。
0b68823e005c.original: Great companies has a very small list of golden rituals. And there are three rules of golden rituals. Number one, they're named. Number two, every employee knows them by their first Friday and, number three, they're templated.

4f565f7e947e.text: 如果你想创造一个牢牢存在于人们大脑中的时刻,并成为一种时代精神或者他们抓住不放的东西,你就必须创造一个有意义的实体,然后用你的意义来充实它。
4f565f7e947e.original: If you want to create a moment that sticks in people's brains and sort of becomes a zeitgeist or something that they latch onto, you got to create an entity, a vessel for meaning, and then you got to fill that vessel with your meaning.

c0e76ea25a21.text: 给平凡的事物赋予品牌力量是非常成功的。将日常的法律审批过程称为
c0e76ea25a21.original: The power of branding the mundane is so successful. Having a secret shopping meeting is very different to potentially coming in and listening to legal report out in your claims mishaps.

282bd1a94eba.original: I think as much as possible is getting to the point where you have alignment on the principles for what it means to build a great product of that company. Not just about if the intuition and tasting gut, but how do you distill that to principles that become the language of the company so that everybody else can start thinking through a similar frame.

16a6654e5ebd.text: 抵御熵增的唯一良药就是注入活力。作为高管和领导者,你每天都必须不懈地与熵增抗争。
16a6654e5ebd.original: The only antidote to entropy, the only antidote to decay in a system is energy. You got to inject energy. Your job as an executive, as a leader, is to fight that entropy tooth and nail every single day.

854edd8f97f6.text: 我学到了乐观是一种可再生资源。他能产生如此强大的活力,并用乐观激发每个人对使命的奉献精神,这是不可思议的,也是公司文化如此重要的一部分。
854edd8f97f6.original: I've learned that optimism is a renewable resource. His ability to generate energy and to use his optimism to renew everybody's dedication to the mission is unbelievable and I think it's such an important part of the culture.

de1e5f1d2bbf.text: 我的动力来源是对现状的不满足。我的根本信念是,所有那些关于技术导致 dystopia（反乌托邦）的言论都是错误的。你知道什么是 dystopia 吗?与未来 20 年相比,今天才是真正的 dystopia。

ca2e5b307330.context: Sean Ellis 评分通过询问客户'如果这个产品消失了,你会有多失望?'来衡量产品市场适配,40% 的客户回答'非常失望'表示达到了适配。
ca2e5b307330.original: If at least 40% of your customers are not very disappointed, you haven't reached product market fit. We've generally moved it up to 50% because Brazilians are inherently polite.
ca2e5b307330.originalContext: The Sean Ellis score measures product-market fit by asking customers "How disappointed would you be if this product went away?" with 40% saying "very disappointed" indicating fit.

ed40701d0a02.text: 对于 B2B 业务,我想要 6 到 8 个客户案例作为达到产品市场适配的指标;对于 B2C 业务,我想要 15 到 25 个客户案例。
ed40701d0a02.original: For B2B, I want six to eight references, for B2C, I want maybe 15 to 25 references as an indication that we've achieved product market fit.

020cbe269bd7.text: 我认为过度关注指标的时候,通常是在试图说服自己它已经达标,而实际上并未达标。
020cbe269bd7.context: 背景:Mike 在讨论衡量 AI 助手成功的挑战,因为传统的参与度指标并不适用 - 'it'指的是产品是否真正很好地服务了用户。
020cbe269bd7.original: I think so much of when you get really metrics obsessed is when you're trying to convince yourself that it is when it's not.
020cbe269bd7.originalContext: Context: Mike is discussing the challenge of measuring AI assistant success when traditional engagement metrics don't apply - "it" refers to whether the product is truly serving users well.

81b5ba6fbe4d.text: 对于大多数公司来说,落在5%到15%区间的激活率要比高百分比区间的更好,因为这通常意味着与长期留存存在更强相关性,你正在竭尽全力让大部分用户达到目前还无法实现的状态。
81b5ba6fbe4d.context: 在增长指标中,"激活率"衡量了完成关键入职步骤(表明他们已体验到产品核心价值)的新用户占比。
81b5ba6fbe4d.original: An activation rate that falls in a lower percentage range, maybe for most companies five to 15%, is better than one that falls in a higher percentage range because it means that there's likely much higher correlation with long-term retention and you're really working hard to get most of your users to reach a state that they're not reaching today.
81b5ba6fbe4d.originalContext: In growth metrics, "activation rate" measures the percentage of new users who complete key onboarding actions that indicate they've experienced the product's core value.

34b32f93d97a.text: 对我们来说,激活意味着团队养成了使用Snyk的习惯。我所说的使用,实际上是获得核心价值,即修复漏洞。这不仅仅是登录,甚至不仅仅是发现漏洞,而是修复漏洞。
34b32f93d97a.original: For us, activation is indicative of the team forming a habit around the usage of Snyk. And when I say the usage, I actually mean deriving core value, which is ultimately fixing vulnerabilities. It's not just logging in. It's not even just finding vulnerabilities, it's fixing vulnerabilities.

b36c27092b9a.text: 我认为大部分价值在后者,就是对目标有极大的清晰度,这让每个人都能朝着优化同一目标而努力。
b36c27092b9a.context: 「后者」指的是对目标有极高的清晰度,而不是具体选择的指标(如 10 天内7个朋友)。
b36c27092b9a.original: I think the majority of the value is in the latter, is just having extreme clarity around the goal and that allowed everybody to work towards optimizing the same goal.
b36c27092b9a.originalContext: "The latter" refers to having extreme clarity around the goal, as opposed to the specific metric chosen (like 7 friends in 10 days).

dd5bf88df8b1.text: 我们引入了一些新指标,其中一个是针对个人的纯留存指标,比如你在第二周还在使用吗?第四周还在使用吗?另一个指标是我们内部称之为'B(大写)',这大致是一个复杂程度得分。
dd5bf88df8b1.context: 「大写的Build」是 Airtable 内部用来衡量用户创建内容复杂程度的指标。
dd5bf88df8b1.original: We introduced a few more metrics, and one of them with purely a retention metric for an individual. Are you week two retained? Are you week four retained? The other was what we called Build with a capital B, and this was roughly a sophistication score.
dd5bf88df8b1.originalContext: "Build with a capital B" was Airtable's internal name for a metric measuring how sophisticated or advanced a user's created content was.

86549834e4cf.text: 入职流程的一个作用就是培养用户使用产品的习惯,从而提高留存。我见过公司通过进行这些变更,将曲线向外推移10、15,甚至20个百分点。
86549834e4cf.original: One of the things that onboarding really drives is habit formation with the product, which leads to retention. I have seen companies shift their curve outward by 10, 15, 20 percentage points from making those changes.

4c37c7ad8d3f.text: 如果做得对,转化率有时实际上应该略有下降。你可能会有更少的人顺利完成全程,但我认为这没关系,因为很多人可能本来就不适合你的产品。
4c37c7ad8d3f.original: If you're doing it right, sometimes conversion should actually decrease a little bit. You might actually have fewer people getting all the way through successfully, but I think that's okay because a lot of those people were probably not the right people for your product.

44e57dae9624.text: 所以如果使用频率正确,每周一次,如果用户在回来使用,如果是免费产品,那么第一周留存率至少要达到60%。如果是付费产品,我通常会看它在20%到30%之间。
44e57dae9624.context: Crystal正在讨论每周留存率基准 - 即用户注册后第二周重复使用的百分比。
44e57dae9624.original: So assuming that the frequency is correct, so you have a weekly frequency, if users are coming back, if it's a free product, 60%. It has to be at least 60%. If it's a paid product, I usually look at that more as maybe 20 to 30%.
44e57dae9624.originalContext: Crystal is discussing weekly retention benchmarks - the percentage of users who return in their second week after signing up.

e86dc680ff28.text: 当你的第一天留存率在30%到40%左右时,对于一个消费应用来说这已经很不错了。如果低于这个水平,有时我可能会质疑用户的使用意图。
e86dc680ff28.original: When you have your D one retention somewhere around the 30 or 40% mark, that's quite solid I think for a consumer app. If it's much lower than that, then sometimes I might question the intent of the user.

634dede3430a.text: 如果你的规模还很小,你的朋友和家人的留存率最好接近80%,因为如果连最关心你的人都无法被说服使用你的产品,那么这个产品可能也很难解决其他人的需求。
634dede3430a.context: "80%"指的是早期创业公司测试产品时,朋友和家人第一周的留存率。
634dede3430a.original: If you are much smaller, your friends and family that better be near close to 80% no matter what, because if you can't even convince the people who care about you to use the product, it probably isn't going to solve the job for anyone else.
634dede3430a.originalContext: The "80%" refers to week-one user retention rates for early-stage startups testing their product with friends and family.

929d67ccdbc8.text: 要做到这一点的关键在于,首先你的产品需要有足够高的使用频率。如果你一个月只使用一次,很难养成使用习惯...我曾在Acorns工作过。它起初是一个投资应用程序,整个业务模式是被动投资,你购买一些ETF,然后基本上不需要检查,只需要不断添加资金,10年后会很不错。这实际上是正确的投资理念,但是当我担任增长负责人时,这给我带来了很大挑战,因为想想看,'设置并忘记'。他们甚至不需要再次回到产品就能取得成功。
929d67ccdbc8.original: The key to do that is, first of all, your product need to have a high enough frequency. If you are using this once per month, it's not likely you can build this into a habit... I worked at Acorns. We started as an investment app, and the whole thing is passive investment, passive investing. You bought some ETFs, and then you basically don't even need to check, and you just keep adding money and it will grow, and after 10 years is awesome. It's actually the right investment philosophy, but when I worked as a head of growth, it made a big challenge for me, because think about set and forget it. They don't even need to go back to a product to be successful.

dd9a36251524.text: 大多数我们在工作场所采用的工具都是协作性的,可以帮助你的团队做得更好,帮助你更好地协作,而AI恰恰相反。它使你个人表现得更出色。
dd9a36251524.original: Most of the tools that we adopt in the workplace are collaborative where it helps your team be better, helps you collaborate better, and AI is the opposite. It makes you individually better.

830d101267b9.text: 这不仅仅是一个笑话。你正在与部分使用AI的年轻公司竞争。这些年轻的AI原生公司在创意工作和职位描述中都使用AI工具,而不是遵循传统的编码实践。
830d101267b9.context: "感受编码"指的是年轻的人工智能原生公司在开发工作流中更多地使用人工智能工具,而不是遵循传统的编码实践。
830d101267b9.original: That's more than a joke. You're competing with young companies that are in part AI. The younger companies are vibe coding and using AI for their creative work and for their job descriptions.
830d101267b9.originalContext: "Vibe coding" refers to how younger AI-native companies use AI tools intuitively throughout their development workflow, rather than following traditional coding practices.

e2fc0847cdd7.text: 我们团队中的大多数人每次都在与多达五个Devin一起工作,所以Devin每个月会将几百个拉取请求合并到Devin代码库中。我们整个团队只有15名工程师左右。
e2fc0847cdd7.context: 德文是认知实验室开发的一款人工智能软件工程助手,可以自主编写代码并提交拉取请求。
e2fc0847cdd7.original: Most folks on the team are definitely working with up to five Devins at once, and so Devin merges like several hundred pull requests into production in the Devin code bases every month. Our whole team is only like 15 engineers a year.
e2fc0847cdd7.originalContext: Devin is an AI software engineering agent built by Cognition Labs that can autonomously write code and submit pull requests.

621f26cd52ab.text: 我们现在的人员比以前多,但他们所做的工作性质更加战略性。这更多是关于建模、验证、提出正确的问题,围绕创意杠杆。而不再是实施和在Google搜索上调整出价等底层工作。
621f26cd52ab.original: We have more people now than we've ever had, but the nature of the work that they do is more strategic. It's more about modeling, validation, asking the right questions, being focused around creative levers. And less so the trench work of implementation and bid modifiers at the keyword level on Google search.

0e006dfa198c.text: 你也需要有一种迭代的感觉。想象一下,如果你在与一家设计公司或代理公司合作,你会来回沟通,说'再试试别的'。我经常在v0版本中通过说'试试别的'来突破困境,这真令人惊讶。
0e006dfa198c.context: v0是Vercel开发的一款基于文本提示生成Web应用程序和用户界面的人工智能工具。
0e006dfa198c.original: You also have to have a sense of iteration, I guess. Think of it this way, if you were working with a design firm or an agency that you've hired, you will go back and forth and say, 'Try something else.' It's amazing how many times I've gotten unstuck in v0 by just saying, 'Just try something else.'
0e006dfa198c.originalContext: v0 is Vercel's AI-powered tool that generates web applications and user interfaces from text prompts.

79839d1d56f3.text: 不管投入多少时间,都远远小于之后节省的时间。这将帮助您节省公司决策的时间,也将帮助您节省网站撰写的时间。如果做对了,网站内容几乎就能自己写出来。
79839d1d56f3.context: "这个"和"它"指的是Jackson描述的品牌策略过程,包括定义公司目的、定位和信息元素。
79839d1d56f3.original: Whatever time it takes you actually is going to save you so much time down the road. It's going to help you save time on company decision making. It's going to help you save time, writing your website. Literally your web copy almost writes itself, if you get this all done right.
79839d1d56f3.originalContext: "This" and "it" refer to the brand strategy process Jackson described, which includes defining company purpose, positioning, and messaging elements.

3a229578f571.text: 我会让你慢下来,以便更快地前进。
3a229578f571.original: I'm going to slow you down to go fast.

0493fc24c4f8.text: 你必须提前策划好棋步。你必须先深思熟虑,然后再去行动,建立可以让你持续更快进步的系统。
0493fc24c4f8.original: You have to plan your chess moves out in advance. You have to really think before you act and build systems that were going to let you go sustainably faster.

610b74dc0771.text: 我们建议在项目的最初阶段,你要彻底清空日程表。核心团队要一起集中10个小时左右,经历一系列活动,这样我们就能一起做出所有关键决策。
610b74dc0771.original: The very beginning of your project, we recommend this kind of crazy idea that you clear your calendar. So the core team come together for 10 hours roughly and go through a sequence of activities so that we can make all of the key decisions together.

6f86f91c3e2b.text: 如果你做好了预演分析,就不需要进行糟糕的总结回顾。当然你也许仍会做总结回顾来学习,但很大概率不会是糟糕的总结回顾。
6f86f91c3e2b.original: If you do a pre-mortem right, you will not have to do an ugly post-mortem. You might still do a post-mortem to learn, but odds are very high that it is not going to be a bad post-mortem.

4aa5224375c3.text: 每周我都会尝试查看至少相当于整个新产品的部分工作模型，这使我能够与团队识别公司内部正在发生的各种瓶颈。
4aa5224375c3.original: Every week I would try to see the equivalent of at least a semi assembly of the entire new product we were working on, which allowed me to identify with teams the different bottlenecks happening in the company.

636c0c1d0045.original: We still have our founders, Nick and Vlad, very hands-on going down to details for every product and every part of the business. Every week they have product reviews with every team.

1220bd734307.text: 来表示工作原型或演示构建,类似于汽车公司在开发过程中创造部分车辆原型。
1220bd734307.original: OpenAI has such a slack heavy culture and it really... The instantaneous real time communication on Slack is so crucial. And I just love being able to tag in different people from different teams and get everybody coalesced.

279ed3d6425d.text: 我们仍然有创始人 Nick 和 Vlad 非常亲自参与每个产品和业务的细节。每周他们都会与每个团队进行产品评审。
279ed3d6425d.original: We all meet every day. Pretty much the entire team gets on a call, and we just kind of front to back... There's 0% fidelity loss in that. Everything, every day, is being audited front to back.

3f8b0f258fc3.text: OpenAI 有如此活跃的 Slack 文化,即时的实时沟通真的至关重要。我很喜欢能够标记不同团队的人并汇集大家。
3f8b0f258fc3.original: I implemented a system to manage that kind of intake with four different touch points: weekly demo days, working sessions, breaking news dress rehearsals, and office hours.

2e3f69b1e0d4.text: 老实说,我们预计到年底这一比例将超过一半。
2e3f69b1e0d4.context: "它"指的是Cognition Labs中Devin（一名AI软件工程师）创建的拉取请求与人类工程师创建的比例。
2e3f69b1e0d4.original: Honestly, we expect it to be a decent bit more than half by the end of the year.
2e3f69b1e0d4.originalContext: "It" refers to the percentage of pull requests created by Devin (an AI software engineer) versus human engineers at Cognition Labs.

bfd40f7e7080.text: 我们刚推出GPT 3.5 6周,就实际有了Fin的测试版。
bfd40f7e7080.context: Fin是Intercom的AI客户服务代理,在从传统聊天式客户支持转型后,成为他们增长最快的产品。
bfd40f7e7080.original: We were only six weeks into the launch of GPT 3.5 when we actually had a beta version of Fin.
bfd40f7e7080.originalContext: Fin is Intercom's AI customer service agent that became their fastest-growing product after pivoting from traditional chat-based customer support.

20e942c09cdc.text: 一家像Cursor或Windsurf这样的AI原生公司,他们会如何执行?我们是否像他们一样快速地利用所有新技术呢？
20e942c09cdc.context: Cursor和Windsurf是内置AI集成的AI驱动型代码编辑器,代表了"AI原生"公司。
20e942c09cdc.original: How would an AI native company, like a cursor or windsurf, et cetera, how would they execute? And are we executing as fast as them and taking advantage of all the new stuff as well as them?
20e942c09cdc.originalContext: Cursor and Windsurf are AI-powered code editors built from the ground up with AI integration, representing "AI native" companies.

9f32f36fda1b.text: 最令人震惊的加速案例之一是Sora安卓应用,我们在18天内建造了一个全新的应用,10天后就对外发布了。
9f32f36fda1b.context: Sora是OpenAI在2024年底发布的AI视频生成模型。
9f32f36fda1b.original: One of the most mind-blowing examples of acceleration, the Sora Android app, like a fully new app, we built it in 18 days and then 10 days later, so 28 days total, we went to the public.
9f32f36fda1b.originalContext: Sora is OpenAI's AI video generation model that was released to the public in late 2024.

7f5f4d28be38.text: 大多数开发人员只有不到25%,甚至少于20%的时间用于编码。如果我们能给他们节省半个小时,一方面他们可以写更多代码,另一方面也能休息片刻,不会被 burnout,还能有更多时间进行协作和创造性思考,从而激发创新。
7f5f4d28be38.context: Inbal Shani正在讨论AI编码工具如何通过减少开发人员实际编码所花的时间,为他们释放更多时间。
7f5f4d28be38.original: Most developers span less than 25, some say less than 20% of their time writing in code. So if we're able to give them half an hour back, one, they can write more code. Second, they can have a break and take a breath so we don't burn them out and they're more happy. Third, we give them more time for collaboration and creative thinking, so that sparks innovation.
7f5f4d28be38.originalContext: Inbal Shani is discussing how AI coding tools can free up developers' time by reducing the portion of their workday spent actually writing code.

f65e4d497b07.text: 我看到的是,首次演示所需的时间更短,但完全部署需要更长的时间。所以我认为节奏会不平衡。
f65e4d497b07.original: What I'm seeing is that the time to first demo is much shorter, but the time to a full deployment is going to take longer. So I think that there's going to be an uneven cadence.

3787c80b2073.text: 要取代任何关键工作流程或构建能够带来可观ROI的东西,即使您有最好的数据层和基础设施层,也需要4到6个月的工作。
3787c80b2073.original: To replace any critical workflow or to build something that can give you significant ROI, it easily takes four to six months of work, even if you have the best data layer and infrastructure layer.

e4611eceffbf.text: 你需要表现出脆弱性。我会非常坦诚地告知你现在的状况。'我们是一家初创企业,还有很多需要学习的地方。你能否给予一些见解,告诉我们这个问题在你那边是如何体现的?'
e4611eceffbf.original: You need to be vulnerable. I would be very open and honest with where you are. Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?

964798ccb101.text: 如果你告诉他们你有一个完全成熟、可以立即使用的产品,他们是不会给你真诚的反馈的。当你表现出脆弱性,告诉他们这个产品还没有完全建成时,即使它实际上已经建好了,你也会得到更加真实、坦诚的反馈。
964798ccb101.original: If you tell them you have a fully baked, ready to go product, they're not going to give you honest feedback. When you're vulnerable and when you tell them it's not fully built yet, even if it is, you will get more raw and honest feedback.

432cc0b0347f.text: 如果你站在我的立场上,你会如何处理这件事?我称之为'黄金问题'。这是一个非常有创意的问题,它真的能打开对话。
432cc0b0347f.original: If you were in my shoes, how would you approach this? I call that the golden question. It's such a creative question. It really opens the conversation.

952bb4fdeb8c.text: 以'什么'、'何时'、'哪里'、'如何'开头的问题。远离'为什么'这样的提问。
952bb4fdeb8c.context: 这个建议适用于在不引起他人防备的情况下给予反馈,正如他们在对人际交流的讨论中提到的。
952bb4fdeb8c.original: Questions that start with what, when, where, how. Stay away from why.
952bb4fdeb8c.originalContext: This advice applies to giving feedback without making people defensive, as discussed in their conversation about interpersonal communication.

914dee95e555.text: 如果我们对此非常认真,那就把1百万美元汇给我们吧。我们随时欢迎你随时取回这笔钱,但让我们实际地为这个价值做出承诺。
914dee95e555.original: If we're super serious about this, send us $1 million. Wire us $1 million. We'll happily wire it back anytime you need it, but let's actually put some stake in the ground about the value.
914dee95e555.originalContext: "This" refers to enterprise deals where big companies request extensive custom features and integrations in exchange for promised large contracts.

f725ebcd9781.text: 愿意付款和真的付款是不同的。这种差异非常大。付款意味着一个独立的群体说:'我的问题迫切到我愿意用自己有价值的东西来换取你将要做的承诺。'
f725ebcd9781.original: Ready to pay is different than paying. Significantly different. Paying is an independent group of people saying, 'My problem is burning enough that I'm willing to exchange something I have that has value for the promise of what you're going to do.'

020ef8d44c59.text: 突然之间,通话不再是'哦,这听起来很有趣。'而是'等等,你们是如何定价的?我们什么时候可以开始做一个概念验证?我知道要连系我团队里的哪些人。'
020ef8d44c59.original: Suddenly, the call didn't end with 'Oh, this sounds super interesting.' The call sounded like, 'Wait, how are you pricing this? When can we start doing a POV? I know exactly who I need to connect you to in my team.'

a75a22f32397.text: 有时你只需要根据市场的需求来调整方向,因为如果很难销售,如果很难获得边际客户,你就无法建立一个巨大的企业。
a75a22f32397.context: 「shear」似乎是「steer」的錯誤轉錄 - 指根據市場需求信號來指導業務方向。
a75a22f32397.original: Sometimes you just need to sheer it from the market and know that it's there, the poll, to know the right places to focus. Because if it's difficult to sell, if it's extremely difficult to sell the marginal customer, you're not going to be able to grow a huge business.
a75a22f32397.originalContext: "Sheer" appears to be a transcription error for "steer" - referring to steering/guiding business direction based on market pull/demand signals.

a180d84f65a7.text: 你不希望被客户置于朋友区,也就是说客户喜欢你,但并不热爱你,也不需要你。
a180d84f65a7.original: You don't want to get friend-zoned by your customers, where your customers like you, but they don't love you and they don't need you.

31792eefd19e.text: 这是一个非常注重解决问题的过程,这是一个重要的观点。
31792eefd19e.context: 这里指的是策略冲刺的第一天,团队分享研究发现并确定阻碍产品前进的问题。
31792eefd19e.original: It's a very problems focused process, and that's an important point.
31792eefd19e.originalContext: "It" refers to the strategy sprint's first day, where teams share research findings and identify problems holding the product back.

c669a99e565a.text: 它的优点在于,你实际上知道每个大类下面的子问题是什么,因为你是以一种非常有机的方式产生的。
c669a99e565a.context: "大类"和"子问题"指的是在策略冲刺的问题聚类练习中确定的用户问题的分类。
c669a99e565a.original: The beauty of it is each of those bigger cluster, you actually know what the sub problems are within that cluster because you sort of generated it very organically.
c669a99e565a.originalContext: "Bigger cluster" and "sub problems" refer to grouped categories of user problems identified during a strategy sprint problem-clustering exercise.

5b60df5a27d7.text: 你生产力受到的最大障碍是什么,或者完成工作的最大挑战是什么?让他们选三个。在这三个中,这种情况会影响到你多久?是每小时吗?是每天吗?是每周吗?还是每季度?
5b60df5a27d7.original: What are the biggest barriers to your productivity, or what are the biggest challenges to getting work done? Let them pick three, just three. Of those three, how often does this affect you? Is this hourly? Is this daily? Is this weekly? Is this quarterly?

7dfcb1cdaa6d.text: 你不能仅通过查看截图或录制的视频来了解一个新的产品功能。人工智能是需要亲身操作的,理想情况下,你既要使用你构建好的 AI 应用程序或解决方案,也要直接玩弄底层的原语。
7dfcb1cdaa6d.original: You can't just look at screenshots or a pre-recorded video of a new product feature. AI is something you have to play with, and ideally you're playing with both the packaged up app or solution that you've built with it, but you're also playing around directly with the underlying primitives.

0569c41844bc.text: 那个 v0 版包含了如此丰富的细节,我们都只是说'赶快发布吧,没什么好讨论的了'。它是动画的、交互式的。我们展示了错误状态、成功状态、慢速流状态。这真的让产品建造者不仅拥有技术技能,我认为这是对这个工具的贬低。它让他们可以探索和丰富他们的思维,考虑到一些他们原本可能不会思考的东西。
0569c41844bc.context: "v0"是Vercel的一款基于AI的Web开发工具,它可以从文本提示生成交互式原型和代码。
0569c41844bc.original: The amount of detail that was contained in that v0, I mean, we're all just saying, 'Well, just ship it. There's nothing else to discuss.' It was animated, it was interactive. We were demonstrating the error state, the success state, the slow stream state. So it really empowers product builders not only with technical skills, I think that does a disservice to the tool. It empowers them to explore and augment their thinking with a lot of things that perhaps they wouldn't have considered otherwise.
0569c41844bc.originalContext: v0 is Vercel's AI-powered web development tool that generates interactive prototypes and code from text prompts.

4f31768b851a.text: 提示是一种新的产品开发或原型设计方式,对于设计师和产品经理来说都是如此。
4f31768b851a.context: "提示"指的是编写文本指令来指导AI模型的行为和输出。
4f31768b851a.original: Prompting is a new way of product development or prototyping for designers and for product managers.
4f31768b851a.originalContext: "Prompting" refers to writing text instructions for AI models to guide their behavior and outputs.

5ec5178da5cb.text: 如果你有一个MVP,只是想获得对某个可能使用AI的想法或功能的支持,那就伪造一下,创建一个小的Figma原型并向一些用户展示,假装AI已经在起作用了。
5ec5178da5cb.original: If you have an MVP and you just want to get buy-in for an idea or feature that may use AI in the future, fake it, create a little figma prototype and just show it some users, just fake what the AI is going to be doing.

019b5167cf23.text: 第一条规则是你不在 Stripe 工作,第二条规则是我们并不在这里解决任何问题。这只是为了练习同理心,去了解客户的视角。
019b5167cf23.context: 这里的 "Stripe Study Groups" 是 Stripe 员工扮演其他公司客户的角色,来练习理解用户视角的角色扮演练习。
019b5167cf23.original: Rule one is you do not work at Stripe and rule two is we're not here to solve any problems. This is just about practicing empathy for the customer.
019b5167cf23.originalContext: Stripe Study Groups are role-playing exercises where Stripe employees pretend to be customers of other companies to practice understanding user perspectives.

e914e321e457.text: 仅今年就已经有超过 25 次的 "Study Groups"，超过 250 人参与其中。这对参与的人来说都是深有感触的。
e914e321e457.context: "Study Groups" 指的是 Stripe 内部的角色扮演练习,员工假扮其他公司的员工使用 Stripe 的产品作为客户。
e914e321e457.original: More than 25 of these Study Groups at Stripe thus far in just this year, more than 250 people have participated in the Study Group. And it is deeply eyeopening for those involved.
e914e321e457.originalContext: "Study Groups" refers to Stripe's internal role-playing exercise where employees pretend to work at fake companies while using Stripe's products as customers.

216f00bbd61c.text: 你需要一些反向平衡来达到这一点。而且我认为这种平衡必须是非自然的。
216f00bbd61c.context: "达到这一点" 指的是真正理解客户的视角,"反向平衡" 意味着抵消内部公司偏见,这种偏见自然会渗透到产品中。
216f00bbd61c.original: You need some counterbalance to get there. And I think it has to be an unnatural counterbalance.
216f00bbd61c.originalContext: "Get there" refers to truly understanding the customer perspective, and "counterbalance" means offsetting internal company bias that naturally creeps into products.

ca60e3be063d.text: 为什么我一开始就没有分配给那些最终会使用它的人呢?我现在都觉得很纳闷。我在构建东西这条路上已经走了十几年,我竟然自己干这个,为什么没有直接分配给最终用户呢？
ca60e3be063d.original: Why didn't I just assign it to the people who are going to use it in the first place? I now scratch my head. I'm several years into a decade-plus building things and I was like, 'I doing this by myself. Why didn't I just assign it to the people who are going to use it in the first place?'
